lawyer:
Mr. Sk. Atiar Rahman, Advocate, ------For the Petitioner. 
Mr. Ali Imam Khaled Rahim, Advocate, ------For the opposite parties.
parties:
Kohinoor Begum And Others
Vs.
Most. Rusia Begum And Others.
full_judgment:
A.N.M.Bashir Ullah, J: This Rule on an application under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure (in short, the CPC)at the instance of the defendant- petitioners was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-5 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 27.05.2002 passed by the Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Jhenaidah in Title Appeal. No. 96 of 1997 reversing the judgment and decree dated 21.8.1997 passed by the Assistant Judge, Kotchandpur, Thenaidah in Title Suit No. 2 of 1997 should not be set aside.

2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule, in short, is that the present opposite-party nos. 1-5 as plaintiffs instituted above numbered title. Suit for permanent injunction contending inter-alia that 3.25 acres of land appertains to C. S. plot No. 7674, 7675, 7674/7792, 223, 226, 227 of C.S. Khatian no. 705 originally belonged to Banu Sikder, Matiar Rahman Sikder and Ejer Ali Sikder in 2 annas 13 gondas 1 kara 1 krant share each, Afil Sikder, Keamuddin Sikder, Rasik Sikder, Azibor Sikder in 1 anna share each and Damini Bewa and Beni. Madhab Saha in 2 annas share each. Out of the said 6 plots in plot No. 227 there were 93, acres of land. Before the preparation of C S. record Beni Madhab Saha settled .23 acres of land to Mann Sikder from the land plot no. 227 and accordingly a separate C.S Khatian being No. 706 for the said .23 acres of land being part and parcel of plot no. 227 was prepared in the name of Monts Sikder and the rest .70 acres of land was recorded in C.S Khatian 705.

3. Before the preparation of C.S. record in an amicable arrangement among the co-sharers AIR Sikder and Keamuddin Sikder had been possessing.70 acres of land of plot No.227 jointly Which is the suit land of the present suit. The other co-sharers had been possessing the other lands. As part of an amicable arrangement between the two brothers Keamuddin had gone Baro Simla village under Kaligonj Police Station surrendering his portion infavour or his brother Afil Sikder. Thus Afil Uddin Sikder had been possessing the entire .70 acres of land of plot no. 227. Later on Alit Uddin Sikder also had shined himself at Baro Simla village lie ,(Afil Sikder) settled .70 acres of land of plot No. 227 to Baharam Biswas the predecessor of the plaintiffs on 11.9.1939 by a registered patta. Keamuddin Sikder died leaving minor son Elahi Box Sikder, minor daughter Amena Khatun and wife Natnesa Bibi. Though the heirs of Keamuddin had no interest in to the suit land but to avoid any further complication, the heirs of Keamuddin Sikder was made party in the settlement deed and for the same reason since recorded tenant Azibor was present in the Sub-Registrar office at the relevant lime he was also a party in the settlement deed Afil uddin and Azibor executed the settlement deed dated 11.9.1939 which was registered on the same date but heirs of Keamuddin did not execute the same.

4. Manu Sikder had surrendered .23 acres of land to the land lord Beni Madhab Shaha who ultimately sold the said .23 acres of land of C.S. plot no. 227 to Baharam Biswas by a registered deed dated 8.12.39 and thus Baharam Biswas, the predecessor of the plaintiffs had acquired total .93 acres of land of CS. Plot no. 227.

5. In the SA record of right the said .93 acres of land have been correctly recorded in the name of Baharam Biswas in two separate khatians, .77 acres of land was recorded in plot no. 227 in SA khatian no. 867 along the other co- sharers while remaining .16 acres of land has been recorded in his name in plot no. 227 in SA khatian no. 870 and while Baharam Biswas was in possession of the said land died leaving the plaintiff as Iris successive heirs.

6. The heirs of Afil Uddin and Keamuddin jointly filed title suit no. 67 of 1989 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Kotchandpur for declaration for then title Into the land of plot no. 227 but ultimately the said suit was dismissed on compromise. The plaintiffs and the defendants of that suit filed solenama in the Court admitting the title of the present plaintiff's. Very recently, before tiling of the suit the defendants had erected a tinshed house in the north east corner of plot no. 227 without prior permission from the poura shava and on the prayer of the plaintiffs, the Kotchandpur poura shava had demolished the said house of the defendants. But even then the defendants have threatened the plaintiffs with dispossession on 15th Kartic, 1403 BS corresponding to 29.10.96. Hence, the suit after filing of the suit on 7.1.1997 the, plaintiffs sought amendment of the plaint averring inter-alia that after filing of the suit the defendants have forcibly erected a house in the east corner of the sun land on 17.1.1997 and the defendants have planted some banana plants also.

7. The defendants appearing in the suit filed written statements denying the material allegations of the plaint. The case of the defendants, in short, is that the CS khatian being no 705 was though correct in respect of its quantity and ownership but there appears some wrong comments and entry as to the possession of the tenants. It has been wrongly articulated in the column of the comment that the land of plot no. 227 was exclusively possessed by Afil Uddin and Keamuddin only but this entry was not correct. Azibor, the one of the recorded tenant had also dwelling but on the land of plot no. 227 along with Afil Uddin and Keamuddin. Azibor possessing .09 acres of land from plot no. 227, .07 acres of land from plot no 226 and .24 acres of land from plot no. 7674 who sold the said .40 acres of land to Md. Moksed Ali by a registered kabala on 14.3.1949. Moksed Ali while was in possession of that land died leaving son Altaf Ali, daughter Rezia Khatun and wife Chaina Khatun. The said heirs of Moksed Ali sold .09 acres of land from plot no. 227 and .07 acres of land from plot no. 226 to this defendant Kohinoor Begin, by a registered kabala deed on 10.6.1989. The defendant no. 1 purchasing the said land had erected a dwelling but covering .09 acres of land on the south east corner of plot no 227 and the son of the defendant no. 1 has been living there. The defendants have also erected cow shed and kitchen in their land. The plaintiffs have no possession in the said land and the pourashava had never demolished any hut of the defendants in the stilt land as asserted by the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs have no right, title and exclusive possession over the land of plot no. 227. So the suit is liable to be dismissed with cost,

8. Upon the above pleadings tile trial Court framed as many as five issues to dispose of the suit. In course of trial, the plaintiffs examined four witnesses while the defendants examined three witness and both the parties filed seine documentary evidence in support of their respective claim winch have duly been marked as exhibits in the suit. The trial court on consideration of evidence and other materials on record dismissed the suit by his judgment dated 21.8.1997 against which the plaintiffs preferred title Appeal being no. 96 of 1997 in the Court of District Judge, Jhenaidah which have been ultimately heard by the Additional District Judge, First Court, Jhenaidah who reversing the judgment of the trial Court below decreed the suit infavour of the plaintiffs by his impugned judgment dated 27.5.2002. The defendant petitioners being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said judgment and decree of the Appellate Court below moved this Court and obtained the present Rule.

9. Mr. Sheikh Atiar Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners supports Rule. He submits that the trial Court rightly found that the defendant-petitioners are in possession in some portion of the suit land and since the suit was for permanent injunction their appears no scope to pass a decree for permanent injunction and ultimately the trial Court dismissed the suit but the Appellate Court below reversing the said findings and the judgment of the trial Court decreed the suit holding that the right of the parties should be determined considering the existing facts at the time of filing of the suit. But in fact the defendant-petitioners had entered in to the possession of their purchased land on the date of their purchase on 10.6.1989 from the son of Moksed Ali and the defendant-petitioners had mutated their name and baize been paying rents to the government. The Appellate Court below committed an error of law in decreeing the suit with a further direction to surrender the possession by the defendants in favour of the plaintiffs.

10. The learned Advocate also submits that though in the C.S. record of right Afil Uddin Sikder and Keamuddin Sikder had 1 anna share each and in that view of the matter they had title into .40½ acres of land out of 3.25 acres of land but they settled .70 acres of land to the predecessor of the plaintiff on 11.9.1939. So the predecessor of the plaintiffs did not acquire title into .29½ acres of land in to the land of plot no. 227.The defendants have been claiming .09 acres of land only in the suit plot no. 227 which has no collision with the plaintiffs as they cannot demand more than .40½ acres of land in plot no. 227 of khatian no. 705 and as such the impugned judgment of the Appellate Court below arc liable to be set aside.

11. On the other hand Mr. Ali Imam Khaled Rahim, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party nos. 1-5 opposing the Rule submits that in the column of the possession in plot no. 227 of C.S. khatian no. 705 it has been articulated clearly that Afil Uddin and Keamuddin had been possessing the said land exclusively and C S. record of right has a presumption as to its genuineness which has not been rebutted by the defendants in any way. The defendants in their written statement very strongly asserted that Azibor, Damini and Rasik had been also residing in the land of plot no. 227 along with Afil Uddin and Keamuddin but this assertion of the defendants has not been proved in any way. The trial Court on due consideration of the evidence and other materials on record found the title and, possession of the plaintiffs into the suit land but also opined that since the plaintiffs had been ousted from a certain portion of the suit land during the pendency of the suit, so it will not be proper to pass a decree for permanent injunction in favour of the plaintiffs but the Appellate Court below relying on the decision of 35 DLR (AD) 43, 47 DLR 170 and 39 DLR 23 rightly held that the right of the parties should be determined at the time of filing of the suit and since after filing of the suit on 7.1.1997 the defendants had entered into possession forcibly in a portion of the suit land on 17.1.1997 the Appellate Court below rightly decreed the suit with a direction to surrender the possession by the defendants in favour of the plaintiffs.The learned Advocate also relying on the decisions of the case of Zamini Bala Vs. Abdul Aziz 10 MLR 25, submits that if a party is dispossessed from the suit land during the pendency of a proceeding, the Court must restore his possession. So the Appellate Court did not commit any error of law and fact in decreeing the suit and as such the judgment of the Appellate Court below did not call for any interference from the this court.

12. I have considered above submission of the learned Advocate of both the parties with profound attention and perused the materials on record.

<u>13. On going to the materials on record it appears that Afil Uddin and Keamuddin had 1 anna share each in the land of CS khatian no. 705 comprising 3.25 acres of land and in plot no. 227 there is an area of .70 acres of land. In the column of possession of the land of plot no. 227 the exclusive possession of Afil Uddin. and Keamuddin was articulated and in pursuance of the said CS khatian Afil Uddin settled .70 acres of land of plot no. 227 to Baharam Biswas, the predecessor of the plaintiffs by a register patta on 11.9.1939. It may be noticed here that 23 acres of land of plot no. 227 under CS khatian no. 706 has been sold to Baharam Biswas by Beni Madhab Shaha on 8.12.1939 and the same is not the disputed land in this suit.</u>

<u>14. Since Afil Uddin and Keamuddin had 1 anna share each in 3.25 acres of land of khatian no. 705 and in that in view of the matter each brother had acquired .20¼ acres of land and thus the 2 brothers jointly acquired .40½ acres of land in the land of khatian no. 705, It is not under stood and there appears no explanation as to how they settled .70 acres of land to Bahamm Biswas but in the S.A record the said .70 acres of land has been recorded in the name of Baharam Hossain in khatian no. 867 and it may be mentioned foe noticing all that the rest .16 acres of land of CS. plot no. 227 has also been recorded in the name of Baharam Biswas in S.A khatian no. 870. The S. A record of right manifest that Baharam Biswas had been possessing the entire land of plot no. 227 exclusively.</u>

<u>15. The present contesting defendant-petitioners have been claiming .09 acres of land in the land of plot no. 227 relying on her kabala dated 10.6.1989. It is the clear case of the defendant- petitioners that Azibor being owner of .09 acres of land Irons plot no. 227 sold the said land along with some other lands to one Moksed Ali on 14.3.1949 who died leaving one son, one daughter and one wife and the said land was recorded in the name of the heirs of Moksed Ali in S.A. khatian no. 867 but it is interesting to note here that the said S.A record shows the exclusive possession of Altaf, the son of Moksed Ali in the land of plot no. 7664 which ultimately establishes that the vendor of the defendant had no possession in the suit land of plot no. 227.</u>

16. The trial, Court and the appellate Court below concurrently found the exclusive possession of the plaintiffs in to the land of plot no. 227 and in this revision I find no reason to disturb the said concurrent findings of the. Courts below and in coming to such conclusion by them their appears no misreading, non reading and non consideration of evidence by the Courts below and as such the findings of in respect of possession of the plaintiffs deserve no interference from this Court. The trial Court though found the possession of the plaintiffs into the suit land but for the dispossession of the plaintiffs from a certain portion of the land after filing of the suit did not pass a decree for permanent injunction.

17. However; be that as it may as I have found that the vendor of the plaintiffs had tide in .40½ acres of land in the land of plot no. 227 of khatian no. 705 but the documentary evidence as well as the oral evidence has established the exclusive possession of the plaintiffs in to the entire land of plot no, 227 of C,S khatian no. 705. Thus the Moat question before us whether the plaintiffs can maintain their such possession until or unless disturbed by the order of any competent. Court. In this regard, the answer will be available in the case of Sefatullah Sheikh Vs Mst. Abjannesa Bibi, 5 DLR 39 where in it has been held in the following ways.

"A person is not entitled to oust his co-sharer from a plot of land in exclusive possession of the latter on the plea that he has got title to every inch of the joint property and that if he feels that his co-sharer is in possession of some lands in excess of his share, his remedy lies in a suit for partition."

18. In the case Abdul Gani Talukder VS. Rushan and others 12 DLR 40 Imam Hossain Chowdhury, J, as he was then held in the following ways:

"It is no doubt true that every co-sharer has equal right of enjoyment in every part and parcel of a joint land. If one co-sharer is in possession of a specific part of a joint land, the other co-shares cannot dispossess Min without a suit for partition."

19. In the above referred cases it has been held by our Apex Court that if a co-sharer is found in exclusive possession of a specific part or portion of a joint holding, the other co-sharer cannot dispossess him without a suit for partition.

20. In this particular case, the defendants have been claiming some land into the suit plot through consecutive purchase from the heirs of recorded tenant Azibor, so the they are, also co-sharers in the suit holding with the plaintiffs. In the case of Moharram Ali and another VS Mohammad Miah 41 DLR 92 we find that a suit was filed by one of the co-sharer for permanent injunction claiming possession over some specific portions of land against the admitted co-sharers, the suit was decreed the by the trial Court holding that though the defendants are co-sharer in the suit holding but the plaintiffs are in exclusive possession into the suit land. The said judgment of the trial Court was confirm by the Appellate Court below against which. Civil Revision was preferred in this Court and in the Civil Revision, said judgment of the Courts below were reversed and against the said judgment of this Court Civil Appeal no. 9 of 1987 was preferred. In the said appeal the Appellate Division observed in the following ways:

"The only question of law agitated in the suit all through was whether an injunction could issue at the instance of a co-sharer in exclusive possession of the separate and well defined share, against another co-sharer who threatens the former with dispossession. This question was rightly answered by the trial Court and the appellate Court but the learned Single Judge on an erroneous view of law reversed their decision."

21. From the above observations of the Appellate Division I find that the Appellate Division restored the judgment of the Courts below which granted permanent injunction against the admitted co-sharers.

22. Now, corning to the Tact’s of the present case we find that both the plaintiffs and defendants are co-sharers in the suit holding but the defendants could not establish possession of their predecessor and vendor including themselves before filing of the suit in to the suit land of plot no. 227. Though the plaintiffs appear to have claimed share more than that of they are legally entitled in to the land of suit plot no. 227 but since they have been in possession of the land of plot no. 227 from the time C.S record I find that the plaintiffs are entitled to maintain their such possession until and unless they are directed to surrender their possession of the excess land by a competent Court and in that view of the matter the plaintiffs are entitled to get a decree for permanent injunction against the defendants.

23. The plaintiffs filed the suit on 7.1.1997 while they were dispossessed by the defendants on 17.1.1997 from a certain portion of the suit land. The appellate Court below relying on the decisions of 35 DLR (AD) 43, 47 DLR 170 and 39 DLR 23 Field that since on the date of filing of the suit the plaintiffs were in exclusive possession of the suit land and since the plaintiffs have been dispossessed from a certain portion of the land, their possession should be restored for those portion of the dispossessed land. I find it difficult to show any disagreement with the very rational and logical findings and decision of the appellate Court below which is based on proper assessment of the evidence on record and the law connected there to. In the case of Zamini Bala -VS- Abdul Aziz and others, 10 MLR 25 it was held in the following ways:

"It is now well settled that if a party is dispossessed from the suit land during the course of a proceedings the court is not only entitled but also duty bound to restore such party to possession in order to ensure status quo ante."

<u>24. Having regards to the above decision it can safely be said that when a person is dispossessed by the defendant during the pendency of the suit, it has become the incumbent duty of the Court to restore his possession and the appellate Court below rightly exercising his jurisdiction passed the order for restoration of the possession of the plaintiffs in to the suit land along with the decree for permanent injunction restraining the defendants from entering into the suit land. More so, this type of the defendants who dispossess the plaintiffs after filing of the suit, in fact, shows a big toe to the law, disregards the rule of law and judicial system of the country, so, if such a defendant is not ousted that will be a simple ironical and funny to the rule of law and sheer indulgence to his or her illegal act, but a Court of law, as a matter fact can never do the same.</u>

25. Having regards to the discussion made above I find no illegality in the impugned judgment and decree of the Appellate Court below rather the same was passed on proper assessment and appreciation of fact and law, so, the same does not call for any interference from this Court.

26. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs.

27. The stay order passed in this Rule on 31.7.2002 is hereby vacated.

28. Let a copy of the judgment and order along with lower Court records be sent to the concerned Court for information and necessary action.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 701 of 2005
lawyer:
Abdul Quayum, Senior Advocate instructed by Sayed Mahbubur Rahman, Advocate-on-Record --- For the Petitioners. 
Nurul Islam Chowdhury, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Respondents.
parties:
Billal Hossain and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Mofizur Rahman and others ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 23rd I February, 2005 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3050 of 2001).
full_judgment:
Md. Tafazzul Islam J.: This petition for leave to appeal arises out of the judgment and order dated 23.2.2005 of a Single Bench of the High Court Division passed in Civil Revision No. 3050 of 2001 discharging the Rule obtained against the judgment and decree dated 22.3.2001 of the learned District Judge, Comilla in Title Appeal No. 254 of 2000 reversing those of dated 19.9.2000 of the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Chandina, Comilla in Title Suit No. 28 of 1999 dismissing the suit.

2. The plaintiffs instituted the above suit seeking declaration of their title in the suit land on the averments that the suit land, together with the other lands of C.S. Khatian No. 258, originally belonged to Amjad Ali and Jabbar Ali; by amicable partition Amjad Ali possessed the entire land of suit plot No. 2719 and half portion of suit plot No. 2718 and Jabbar Ali possessed the remaining half portion of the above suit plot No. 2718; Amjad Ali died leaving behind two sons, Wahid Ali and Rawsan Ali; Wahid Ali transferred 34½ decimals of land in favour of Alimuddin from plot No. 2719 by two registered kabalas dated 10.01.1959 and 31.12.56 and made over possession thereof to him; Rawshan Ali sold 12½ decimals of land from plot No. 2719 to Ambar Ali by two registered Kabalas dated 17.01.47 and 18.09.47; Haider Ali sold 15½ decimals of land to Ansar Ali from plot No. 2719 and 15½ decimals of land from Plot No. 2718 to Alimuddin by registered kabala a dated 20.02.48; Alimuddin while owning and possessing in total 67½ decimals of land from Plot No. 2718 and 2719 died leaving behind one son Dud Miah, one wife Joferer Nessa and two daughters. Fulmati and Panmati: Dud Miah, Who on amicable partition with his mother and sisters got the aforesaid 67½ decimals of land, transferred 15 decimals of land from Plot No. 2718 and 52 decimals of land from Plot No. 2819 to the plaintiffs by kabala dated 3.5.1993 and since then the plaintiff had been possessing the same, the defendants have no title and possession in any portion of the suit land but they on 25.4.1999 claimed title over the same and hence the suit.

3. The defendants contested suit by filing joint written statement contending, inter alia, that the suit has not been properly valued, is barred by limitation and is not maintainable without the relief of partition as well as recovery of possession; Alimuddin while owning and possessing the suit land died leaving behind one son Dud Mia, two daughters Fulmati and Panmati and one wife Joferer Nessa; by amicable partition Fulmati and Panmoti got 51 decimals of land from. Plot No. 2719 and subsequently they by kabala dated 27.04.1995 transferred their interest to Ayub Ali, father of the defendant Nos. 1 to 3, and also handed over possession of the above land to him; Ayub Ali died leaving behind three sons, the defendant Nos. 1-3, one wife and four daughters; Dud Miah had no title and possession over the land of Plot No. 2719 and accordingly had no right to transfer any land from the above plot to the plaintiffs; the kabala dated 03.05.93 is fraudulent, inoperative, without consideration and void and the plaintiffs acquired no title and possession by the said kabala.

4. The learned Assistant Judge, after hearing, dismissed the suit. The plaintiffs then preferred Title Appeal No. 254 of 2000 and the learned District Judge, Comilla, after hearing, allowed the appeal. The defendants then moved the High Court Division and obtained Rule in Civil Revision No. 3050 of 2001 and the High Court Division, after hearing, discharged the Rule.

5. The learned counsel appearing for the defendant petitioners submits that the High Court Division failed to consider that Dud Miah, by exhibit-Gha series, transferred his entire property and so the plaintiff respondents, being purchasers from Dud Miah, were not entitled to a decree for declaration of title; the sisters of Dud Miah being co-sharer and also in ejmali possession of the suit land no decree for declaration of title could be passed against their transferees unless a case of ouster was made out; the finding of possession as found by the learned District Judge is based on non-consideration and misreading of material evidence on record and the High Court Division also did not consider that a suit for declaration of title is not maintainable against co-sharers without a prayer for consequential relief and that the provision of section 47 of Registration Act is misconceived because Dud Mia was not entitled to transfer the properties belonging to his sisters.

6. As it appears the trial Court dismissed the suit holding that the plaintiffs purchased 60½ decimals of land from Dud Mia by sale deed dated 03.05.93, Ext-4, from suit plot Nos. 2718 and 2719 only and that Dud Miah, who had no subsisting title in the suit land, could not transfer the suit land to the plaintiffs and accordingly by their alleged purchase from Dud Mia, the plaintiffs did not acquire any title to the suit land and further the defendants were in possession of .51 decimals of land of plot No. 2719 and thus the plaintiffs having no title or possession in the suit land were not entitled to get any decree.

<u>7. However the appellate Court on consideration of the evidence on record found that Dud Miah had subsisting interest in 1.80 acres of land out of 3.60 acres of land left by his father Alimuddin and Dud Miah also purchased 24½ decimals of land with his own money and thus he became owner in respect of 2.04½ acres of land including .15½ decimals of land from suit plot No. 2718 and the remaining portion from suit plot No. 2719 and the plaintiffs) also proved their title and possession in the suit land. The High Court Division found that there is no dispute as to the fact that the suit land belonged to Alimuddin who acquired the same by registered kabalas, Exts. 2 and 3, and he died leaving behind one son Dud Miah, two daughters in Fulmoti and Panmoti and one widow Jofere Nessa and it is on record that the Alimuddin died leaving behind 3.60 acres of land and so Dud Mia inherited 1.80 decimals of land from his father and that records also show that Dud Mia also purchased .24½ decimals and thus he became owner of 2.04½ acres of land and that the kabala dated 3.5.93, Ext. 4, shows that .60½ decimals of land was sold by Dud Mia to the plaintiffs from suit plot Nos. 2718 and 2719. The High Court Division found that the contesting defendant did not claim any land from plot No. 2718 and according to them Dud Mia had no subsisting interest in the suit land to transfer to others because long before his transfer his sisters Fulmoti and Panmoti transferred the suit land to defendant Nos. 1-3 by kabala dated 27.4.95, Ext. Ka, and that the learned District Judge considering the cases of both the parties found that Dud Mia had subsisting interest in the suit land of suit plot Nos. 2718 and 2719 and accordingly the plaintiffs acquired valid title by their purchase of .60½ decimals of land from Suit Plot Nos. 2718 and 2719 the contesting defendant. Nos. 1-3 having claimed 51 decimals of land in Suit Plot No. 2719 by a subsequent sale deed dated 27.4.95, Ext. Ka, from Fulmot and Panmoti High Court Division held that "since the ejmali property left by Alimuddin was never partitioned by metes and bounds and the plaintiffs kabala is earlier then the defendant's kabala so their kabala Ext. 4 will prevail over the kabala of defendants". The High Court Division further found that the learned District Judge, the final court of facts, having come to the conclusion that the plaintiffs have proved their possession in the suit land and that admittedly Fulmoti and Panmoti, after their marriage were living with their husbands at different villages and so they, not being in possession of the suit land physically, were not in a position to deliver possession of the same to Ayub Ali, the predecessor-in-interest of defendant Nos. 1-3 at the time of the alleged sale and so the defendants therefore did not get possession in the suit plots at the time of their purchase which is about 2 years after the purchase made by the plaintiffs from Dud Mia and thus Ayub Ali did not get any possession in the suit plot No. 2719 at the time of the alleged purchase by the kabala Ext. Ka. The High Court Division also found that the learned District Judge considering the provisions of Order I rule 9 CPC and also citing few decision of superior courts held in the facts and circumstances of the present case the suit should not fail for defect of parties and further the grounds taken in the revisional application are of general nature and there is no ground with regard to misreading of evidence, non consideration or misconstruction of evidence.</u>

8. We are of the view that High Court Division after due consideration of the evidence and materials on record and answering the relevant issues as raised arrived at a correct decision and there is no cogent reason to interfere with the side decision.

9. The petition is dismissed.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1301 of 2004
lawyer:
A.K. Mujibar Rahman, Advocate instructed by Md. Nurul Islam Chowdhury, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioners. 
Respondents ------ Not represented.
parties:
Chairman, Raisree (North) Union Parishad and another ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Abdul Khaleque and another ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 24th March, 2004 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3102 of 1994)
full_judgment:
Md. Tafazzul Islam J.: The defendant Nos. 4 and 5 have filed this petition for leave to appeal impugning the judgment; and order dated 24.3.2004 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3102 of 1994 making the Rule absolute. The above Rule arose out the judgment and decree dated 19.7.1994 passed the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Chandpur in Title Appeal No. 16 of 1991 reversing those of dated 20.9.1990 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Shasrasti, Chandpur in Title Suit No. 4 of 1989 decreeing the suit.

2. The respondent Nos. 1 and 2, as plaintiffs, instituted the above Title Suit No. 4 of 1989 praying for permanent injunction contending, inter alia, that they are owners in possession of the suit land by way of inheritance as well as by purchase and the previous and present khatians were correctly prepared and published in their names as well as in the names of their predecessor and they have been paying rents regularly; the defendants have no right, title, interest or possession in the suit land and the suit land was never acquired; the plaintiffs did not authorise anybody to cut earth from the suit land and that if the defendants attempt to construct the road ignoring objection of the plaintiffs there may be serious breach of peace which may even result to murder which may not be compensated by money. The defendant Nos. 1-6 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement contending, inter alia, that the plaintiffs have no locus standi to file the suit; in order to ensure suitable movements in the locality six projects were taken up in the fiscal year 1988-89 under the Food for Works Programme on 28.3.1988 for reconstruction of the disputed road and a Project Implementation Committee was formed on 5.12.1988 with the defendant No. 4 as its Chairman; the defendants never thereat and the plaintiffs on 4.12.1988 or in any other dated and there was also no reason to give such thereat and hence the suit is liable to be dismissed. The learned Assistant Judge, after hearing, decreed the suit. On appeal, the lower appellate court allowed the appeal. The plaintiffs then moved the High Court Division and obtained Rule in Civil Revision No. 3012 of 1994 and upon hearing the High Court Division made the Rule absolute.

3. The learned counsel for the petitioners submits that P.W. 1 stated that after filing the suit the defendants forcibly constructed the road in the last part of Baishak, the plaintiffs in their application dated 26.7.89praying for local inspection admitted that on 12.5.89, which is two and a half months before the institution of the suit, the road was constructed; admittedly the road in question is an old one and it is there construction of the public road to connect villages through the khas land and during the pendency of the suit there was no construction of new road and so the decision as arrived at by the High Court Division cannot be sustained in law.

4. As it appears the trial Court decreed the suit on the findings that- “আবদুল আলী ঠিকাদারের বাড়ী তথা ১২৯ দাগের দক্ষিন পশ্চিম কোন হইতে ১২২ ও ১২১ দাগের পার্শ্ব দিয়া ১১৫ দাগের কোন পর্যন্ত রাস্তা টুকুর জন্য মুলত কোন বিরোধ নাই। কারণ স্বীকৃত মতে ১২২ দাগের জমি বিবাদীদের মালিকানাধীন এবং ১২০ ও ১২১ দাগের মধ্যে কিঞ্চিৎ হালট বিদ্যমান যদিও ১২১ দ���শের জমি বাদী পক্ষের বলিয়া পরিদর্শনকালে স্বীকার করা হইয়াছে ৷ ঠিকাদারের বাড়ীর ৬/৭ ঘরের লোকজন চাইলে ১২২ ও ১২১ দাগের পার্শ্ব দিয়া ৬৮ দাগের হালট দিয়া উত্তরমুখী দিয়া ১১৫ ও ১১৪ দাগের উত্তর কিনারা দিয়া ৭৯ দা'গস্থ মসজিদ ও বক্তব্যে (মন্তবে) সহজে যাতায়াত করিতে পারে এবং উক্ত পক্ষে ৬৮ ও ২৬ দাগের হালট দিয়া ১৬ দাগের রাস্তার সহিত যোগাযোগের সুন্দর সুযোগ রহিয়াছে ৷ অধিকস্ত ঠিকাদার বাড়ীর ৬২ দাগের উত্তর পশ্চিম কোন হইতে বিদ্যমান ৬৭ ও ২৬ দাগের হালট দিয়া অতি সহজে ১৬ দাগের রাস্তা ও বর্ণিত মসজিদ মক্তবে ঠিকাদার বাড়ীর লোকজন যাতায়াত করিতে কোন বাধা দেখা যায় না । শুধু মাত্র হালটের উপর রাস্তা বাধিয়া দিলেই হয় । এত সহজ সব বাদ দিয়া বিবাদীগন কেন যে বাদী পক্ষের ১০৯, ১১০, ১১২, ১১৪ ও ১১৫ দাগের স্বত্ব দখলীয় ভূমির উপর দিয়া রাস্তা করার জন্য ঠেলা ঠেলি করিতে গেলেন তাহা ভাবিতে অবাগ লাগে। নালিশী রাস্তা বরাবর ১টি রাস্তা থাকিলে তাহা ঠিকাদার বাড়ীর লোকজনের জন্য সোজা হইলেও রাস্তা সোজা করার জন্য কাহারা সর্বনাশ করিয়া নিজেদের পোষ মাস নীতি গ্রহনের যুক্তি কোথায়?

5. পরিদর্শন কালে দেখা দিয়াছে যে, নালিশী রাস্তার স্থলেপূর্বে আদৌ কোন রাস্তা ছিল না এবং নালিশী রাস্তার স্থলে বিদ্যমান রাস্তাটি কিছু দিন আগে বাধাই বলিয়া প্রতিয়মান হয় ৷ জবাবে বলা হইয়াছে অনুমোদিত পূনঃনির্মান প্রকল্পের জন্য ৯/১/৮৯ ইং তারিখে বিশ মেট্রিক টন গম অনুমোদন করেন এবং উক্ত কাজের জন্য গত ৯/১/৮৯ ইং তারিখে ২০ মেট্রিক টন গমের ডি/ও ইস্যু করেন ৷ অথচ বিবাদীপক্ষের দাখিলী শাহরাস্তি উপজেলা পরিষদ কার্য্যালয়ের উপজেলা চেয়ারম্যান কর্তৃক ৯/১/৮৯ ইং তারিখে স্বাক্ষরিত স্বারক নং-৮-১২/৮৮-৮৯/ - ত্রান, পত্র দৃষ্টে দেখা যায় যে,তিনি ৯/১/৮৯ ইং ২০ মেট্রিক টন গমের ডি/ও ইস্যু করারজন্য উপজেলা খাদ্য কর্মকর্তা বরাবরে অনুরোধ কারিয়াছেন মাত্র ৷ ঐ ডিম খাদ্য কর্মকর্তা কোন তারিখে ইস্যু করিয়াছেন তাহার কারনেই-প্রমান পত্র বিবাদী পক্ষ দাখিল করে নাই । ইহার দ্বারা প্রথমঃ জবাবে বর্ণিত ৯-১-৮৯ ইং ডি/ও ইস্যু হওয়ার দাবী মিথ্যা প্রমাণিত হয় ৷ দ্বিতীয়ত: উক্ত চিঠি থানা খাদ্য অফিসে পৌছিয়া সংশ্লিষ্ট ফরমালিটিস সম্পন্ন করতঃ ডি/ও ইস্যু হইতে আরো ও যে ৮/৯ দিল গালইি স্বাভাবিক । তৃভীয়তঃ অত্র মামলা দায়েরের হইয়াছে ২১/৯/৮৯ ইং এর পরে ইস্যু হয় বিধায় এবং উক্ত ডি/ম (ও) ইস্যু ওয়ার প্রমান পত্র দাখিল করিলে অত্র মামলা দায়েরের পর নালিশী নতুন রাস্তাটি রাখিয়াছে প্রমান হইবে বিধায় ডি/ম (ও) ইস্যুর কাগজপত্র দাখিল করা হয় নাই ৷ ইহাতে প্রতীয়মান হয় যে, অত্র মামলা দায়েরের পর বাদীগনের বর্ণিত দাগ সমুহের ভূমির উপর দিয়া নালিশী নতুনভাবে রাস্তাটি রাখা হয় ৷ সতর্কতা অবলম্বন আদালত উল্লেখিত স্মারক নং-৮-১২-৮৮-৮৯ ত্রান পত্রটি আদালত স্ব-উদ্যোগে একজিবিট এ চিহ্নিত করিলাম।

6. উল্লেখীত আলোচনা হইতে প্রমানিত হইয়াছে যে, নালিশী রাস্তার স্থলে পূর্বে কোন রাস্তা ছিল না, অত্র মামলা দায়েরের পর বিবাদীগন বাদীগনের ধানি জমির উপর দিয়া নতুন ভাবে নালিশী রাস্তা তৈরী করিয়াছেন ৷ যেহেতু নালিশী নতুন রাস্তার স্থলে পূর্বে কোন রাস্তা ছিল না । সেহেতু দেখা যায় যেন, উক্ত রাস্তা সংস্কারের নাম করিয়া সম্পূর্ণ মিথ্যা বানােয়াট ও কয়েক ব্যক্তির স্বার্থে বিবাদীগন ভুয়া প্রকল্প গ্রহণ করিয়াছেন। পরিদর্শন প্রতিবেদন ও উপরোক্ত আলোচনা হইতে দেখা যায় যে, ঠিকাদারের বাড়ী হইতে মূল রাস্তার সহিত যোগাযোগের জন্য একাধিক সুযোগ সরকারী জমির উপর দিয়া থাকিলেও বিবাদীগন তাহা গ্রহন না করিয়া বে আইনী ও ইচ্ছাকৃতভাবে বাদীগন এর জমির উপর দিয়া নতুন ভাবে রাস্তা করিয়াছেন যাহা সম্পূর্ণ ন্যয় বিচার পরিপন্থী ৷

7. ঠিকাদার বাড়ী হইতে যোগাযোগের বিকল্প কোন পথনা থাকিলেও প্রয়ােজনের খাতিরে নালিশী নতুন রাস্তা নির্মানের একটি যুক্ত করা যাইত ৷ যেহেতু সরকারী তথা সর্বসাধারনের মালিকানাধীন হালটের উপর দিয়া যােগাযোগের অবিরত সুযোগ রহিয়াছে সেহেতু বাদীগনের প্রভূত অপুরনীয় ক্ষতি করিয়া রাস্তা নির্মানের কোনই যুক্তি নাই সংগত কারন নাই । এহেন কর্ম সম্পূর্ণ অবৈধ ও জোরজবরদস্তিমূলক বিধায় উক্ত কর্যকে আদৌ প্ৰশ্রয় দেয়া যায়না ৷ স্মরনযােগ্য যে নতুন রাস্তা নির্মান করা হইয়াছে কেবলমাত্র ঠিকাদার বাড়ীর ৭টি পরিবারের স্বার্থে, এই রাস্তার সহিত কােন প্রকার সর্ব সাধারণের স্বার্থও জড়িত নহে অর্থাৎ এই ক্ষেত্রে জন স্বার্থের দোহাইও সম্পূর্ণ অচল ৷

8. However the lower appellant Court allowed the appeal holding that- “বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন আদালত রায়ে উল্লেখ করিয়াছেন, পূর্বে নালিশী রাস্তার স্থলে কোন রাস্তা ছিল না ৷ বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন আদালত আরো সিদ্ধান্ত উপনীত হইয়াছে যে, মামলা দায়ের এর পরনালিশী রাস্তাটি নির্মিত হইয়াছে এবং সে কারনে তিনি আদেশমূলক নিষেধাজ্ঞার ডিক্রী প্রদান করিয়াছেন ৷

9. বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন আদালত স্থানীয় পরিদর্শন করিয়া এবং পূর্ব হইতে স্থিত অন্য রাস্তার সহিত তুলনা মূলক সুবিধা অসুবিধা নির্ধায়ন করতঃ সিদ্ধান্ত উপনীত হইয়াছেন যে, নালিশী রাস্তাটির অসিত্ব (অস্তিত্ব) পূর্বে করি না । বাদীপক্ষ ২১-১৭৮৯ ইং তারিখে অত্র মামলাটি আনয়ন করিয়াছেন ৷ মামলার কারন হিসাবে উল্লেখ করা হইয়াছে যে, ২8-১২-৮৮ ইং তারিখে রাস্তা নির্মানের হুমকি দিয়াছে । বাদী পক্ষের ১নং সাক্ষী তাহার সাক্ষে উল্লেখ করিয়াছেন যে, বৈশাখের শেষ ভাগে মামলা দায়েরের পর বিবাদীরা জোরে জবাবে রাস্তা রাখে । বাদী পক্ষের ২২-৭-৮৯ ইং তারিখে কমিশনার নিয়ােগের প্রার্থনায় দরখাস্তদায়ের করিয়াছেন যাহাতে উল্লেখ করিয়াছে যে, ১২-৫-৮৯ইং তারিখে নব্য রাস্তা নির্মান করিয়াছে । ১২-৫-৮৯ তারিখে রাস্তা নির্মান করিলে বাদীপক্ষ তৎক্ষনিকভাবে আদালতে দরখাস্ত দাখিল করিত ৷ বাদীপক্ষ প্রায় আড়াই মাস পরে কমিশন নিয়ােগের প্রার্থনা করিয়াছে । যে কারনে ১২-৫-৮৯ ইং তারিখে রাস্তা নির্মান সম্পর্কে সন্দেহের অবকাশ থাকিয়া যায় ৷ মামলা দায়েরের পর হইতে বাদীপক্ষ কমিশন দিয়া রাস্তার অস্তিত্ব নাই মর্মে প্রমাণের উল্লেখ গ্রহন করেন নাই ৷ অপর দিকে বিবাদী পক্ষে বলা হইয়াছে যে, নালিশী রাস্তা পূর্ব হইতে স্থিত ছিল ইহা মেরামত করা হইয়াছে মাত্র। বিষয়টি প্রমানের জন্য বিবাদপক্ষে ২৮-৩-৮৮ ইং তারিখের সভার কার্য্য বিবরনী প্রকল্প কমিটির সদস্যগনের নাম সংক্রান্ত ফিরিস্তি এবং বিশ মেট্রিক টন গম উত্তোলন এর প্রস্তাব অনুমোদন সংক্রান্ত কপি মাস্টার রুল ইত্যাদি দাখিল করিয়াছে ৷

10. উক্ত দলিলাদির মধ্যে ২৮-৩-৮৮ইং তারিখে সভায় রেজুলেশন কপি পর্যালোচনায় দেখা যাইতেছে যে, নালিশী রাস্তাটি একটি পূর্ণনির্মান প্রকল্প এই প্রকল্পের সম্পর্কিত ৯-১-৮৯ তারিখে অনুমোদিত হয় ৷ একই তারিখে বিশ মেট্রিক টন গমের ডিও ইস্যু করার অনুরোধ করা হয় ৷ ১১-১২-৮৮ ইং তারিখের অফিস আদেশ মূলে ইহার কারিগরি কর্মকর্তা নিয়োগ করা হয় । ৪-১-৮৯ইং তারিখে মাষ্টার রুল পরীক্ষা নিরীক্ষার জন্য কর্মকর্তা নিয়োগ করা হয় । বিবাদীগনের দাখিলী ৭-২-৮৯ইং বিবাদীগনের দাখিলী ৭-২-৮৯ইং তারিখের প্রকল্প বাস্তবায়ন কর্মকর্তার মাসিক প্রতিবেদন পর্যালোচনার দেখা যাইতেছে যে, ৭-১-৮৯ ইং তারিখে প্রকল্পের কাজ শুরু হয় ৷ বিবাদী পক্ষে প্রকল্প এর মাটির কাজের ষ্টেটমেন্ট এবং মাষ্টার রুল দাখিল করিয়াছে । এই সকল দলিল পত্র পর্যালোচনায় দেখা যাইতেছে যে, রায়শ্ৰী উত্তর ইউনিয়ন ভুক্ত ৮২০৭৩ প্রকল্পটি রাস্তা পূর্ন নির্মান প্রকল্প এই প্রকল্পের নতুন রাস্তা নির্মান করা হয় নাই ৷

11. বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন আদালত ২১-১-৮৯ ইং তারিখে ডিও সম্পর্কে সন্দেহ পােষন করিয়াছেন ৷ তিনি সিদ্ধান্ত উপনীত হইয়াছে যে, ৯-১-৮৯ ইং তারিখে চিঠি খাদ্য অফিসে পৌছিয়া সংশ্লিষ্ট ফরমালিটি পুরন করতঃ ডিও ইস্যু হইতে আরো ৮-১০ দিন লাগা স্বাভাবিক । বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন আদালতের উক্ত রূপ সিদ্ধান্ত যুক্তিযুক্ত বলিয়া প্রতিয়মান হয় না ৷ এমন কি ৯-১-৮৯ ইং তারিখের অধিচারন মূলে ২১-১-৮৯ ইং তারিখে ডিও ইস্যু করা খুবই স্বাভাবিক ৷ বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন আদালত ডিও ইস্যুর কাগজপত্র দাখিল না করার সিন্ধান্ত উপনীত হইয়াছেন যে, মামলা দায়ের পর নালিশী রাস্তা তৈরী করা হইয়াছে । বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন আদালতের উক্ত রূপ সিদ্ধান্ত সাক্ষ্য নির্ভুল নহে ।

12. বিবাদী পক্ষের ১নং সাক্ষী বিবাদী পক্ষের জবাবের সমর্থনে বক্তব্য দিয়াছেন ৷ বিবাদী পক্ষের ২নং সাক্ষী ১নং বাদী জালাল উদ্দিন পুরানো রাস্তা মেরামত এর কথা বলিয়াছেন ৷ বিবাদী পক্ষের অপরাপর সাক্ষীগন একই ভাবে পুরানো রাস্তার বিষয়টি উল্লেখ করিয়াছেন ৷ বাদী পক্ষের ১ নং সাক্ষী রাস্তা তৈরি নির্মান করিতে দেখে নাই। তাহার কথিত মতে বাদী ওমর হোসেন রাস্তা নির্মান করিতে দেখিয়াছে। কিন্তু ওমর হোসেন আদালতে উপস্থিত হয় নাই। উপরোক্ত সাক্ষ্যদি নিরূপণ করিয়া সিদ্ধান্তে উপনীত হওয়া যায় যে, মামলা দায়ের পূর্বেই নালিশী রাস্তার অসিত্ব (অস্তিত্ব) ছিল। সে কারনে বাদীর নিষেধাজ্ঞার প্রার্থনা অচল।

<u>13. As it appears the High Court Division made the Rule absolute holding that the plaintiffs filed an application for local inspection on 26.7.1989 and the learned Assistant Judge himself went to the suit land along with the learned Advocate of both the sides on 12.9.1990 and then inspection was held in presence of the elites of the locality and thereafter on 13.9.1990 the learned Assistant Judge himself along with learned Advocates of both the sides prepared a joint Inspection Report which was made part of the trial court judgment wherein it was found that there was no old road. The High Court Division also found that both the courts I below concurrently held that the Plaintiffs could establish their right, title and interest in the property and further the report of the Advocate Commissioner, Ext.3, which formed part of the judgment, also shows that the disputed road going to be constructed on new land and further the trial court found that the C.S. and S.A. record there was no mention of any road and this fording was not controverter by the court of appeal below. The High Court Division further found that in the documents submitted, there was no road on the disputed land and the suit land is covered by paddy.</u>

<u>14. Accordingly we are of the view that the High Court Division on proper consideration of the materials on record arrived at a correct decision and as such there is no cogent reason to interfere with the judgment sought be appealed.</u>

15. The petition is dismissed.

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 11.05.2003 passed by the high Court Division in Civil Rule No. 93 (R) of 2002)
full_judgment:
Nazmun Ara Sultana, J. This appeal, by leave, is against the judgment and order dated 11.05.2003 passed by Division Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Rule No. 93(R) of 2002 making the Rule absolute.

2. Sabitri Sundari Mali predecessor of the appellants filed Preemption Case No. 18 of 1994 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Munshiganj, under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act for pre-emption of the land transferred by the respondent Nos. 3-7 by kabala dated 18.11.1993 to the respondent Nos. 1 and 2. The case of the pre-emptor originally was that she was the co-sharer in jote and that the purchaser-respondent Nos. 1 and 2 were stranger to that.

3. The respondent No. 1 contested that preemption case by filing written objection contending, inter alia, that the pre-emptor was not a co-sharer and the pre-empted kabala also was not out and out sale deed.

4. The trial Court dismissed that miscellaneous case by the judgment and order dated 27.05.1995. Against that judgment and order the pre-emptor Sabitri Sundari Mali filed, Miscellaneous Appeal No. 35 of 1995 in the Court of District Judge, Munshiganj. In that appeal the pre-emptor-appellant filed an application under Order 6 Rule 17 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for amendment of the pre-emption petition including the fact that the pre-emptor was the owner of plot No. 334 which was contiguous to the land under pre-emption and therefore the pre-emptor was entitled to get pre-emption as a contiguous land holder also. The appellate Court allowed that appeal and sent the case hack on remand for fresh trial. The trial Court, on retrial, again dismissed that pre-emption case by the judgment and order dated 21.04.1998 against which the pre-emptor preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 15 of 1998 in the Court of learned District Judge, Munshiganj. The appellate Court allowed that appeal and thereby allowed the pre-emption case by the judgment and order dated 30.05.1999. Being aggrieved by that judgment and order of the appellate Court below the respondent No. 1 filed Civil Revision No. 3535 of 1999 in the High Court Division and obtained Rule. Ultimately, on hearing both the parties, the said rule was discharged by a Division Bench by the judgment and order dated. 23.01.2002. The respondent No. 1 then filed an application for reviewing the said judgment passed in Civil Revision No. 3535 of 1999 on the ground that the preemptor Sabitri Sundari Mali transferred her entire interest in the contiguous plot No. 334 during pendency of the revisional application and therefore she lost her right of pre-emption before final decision as to her pre-emption case. Rule was issued in that review petition which was registered as Civil Rule No. 93(R) of 2007. The High Court Division, after hearing, allowed that review petition and made the rule issued in Civil Revision No. 3535 of 1999 absolute and dismissed the pre-emption case No. 18 of 1994 on the Findings and decisions that the pre-emptor Sabitri lost her entire interest in the contiguous plot No. 334 during continuation of the civil revision and thus lost her right of preemption and that this fact of transfer by the preemptor Sabitri Sundari Mali alter entire interest in the contiguous plot No. 334 to her son Sunil Chandra Biswas was discovered after the disposal of the said civil revision and also on the ground that the pre-emption case was bad for non-impleading the other contiguous land holders. Being aggrieved by that judgment and order of the High Court Division the heirs of pre-emptor Sabitri Sundari Mali filed civil petition for leave to Appeal No. 950 of 2003 and leave was granted on 02.03.2005 to examine only whether the pre-emptor, after transfer of land from the contiguous plot Nos.  334 and 333 had any subsisting interest in those plots.

5. We have heard the learned Advocates for both the parties in details. Mr. Bivash Chandra Biswas, the learned Advocate appeared for the appellants has mainly argued that the High Court Divisions findings that the original pre-emptor Sabitri Sundari. Mali transferred more than her share in the contiguous plot No. 334 and thus lost her entire interest in that plot is wrong; that this plot No. 334 contains 74 acre of land and by the deed of gift the pre-emptor-Sabitri Sundari Mali transferred 72 acre of land to her son and as such she had still .02 acre of land in this plot No. 334 and as such was very much entitled to pre-empt the land in question as contiguous land holder. The learned Advocate has contended that the High Court Division's decision being based on this wrong finding that the pre-emptor Sabitri Sundari Mali had no subsisting interest in this contiguous plot No. 334 is wrong and not sustainable.

6. Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate for the contesting respondent No. 1 has made submissions controverting the above arguments of the learned Counsel for the appellant. Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan has made submission to the effect that the preemptor Sabitri Sundari Mali had only .42 acre of land in plot No. 334 but by the registered deed of gift she transferred .72 acre of land in favour of her son the present appellant Sunil Chandra Biswas and thus she lost her entire interest in this plot No. 334 and consequently she lost her right of pre-emption also as a contiguous land holder.

<u>7. We have considered the submissions of learned Advocates of both the sides and gone through the judgments of the courts below and other relevant papers on record. It appears that the High Court Division, in the impugned judgment, has elaborately discussed to the effect that the contiguous plot No. 334 measured a total area of 74 acre of land and that Nitai Mali-the predecessor of preemptor Sabitri Sundari Mali got less than 42 acre of land in this plot in his 8. annas 13 gondas 1 kora and 1 kranti share and that the pre-emptor Sabitri Sundari Mali acquired this 42 acre of land of plot No. 334 by virtue of inheritance from Nitai Mali and also by virtue of purchase from her other three sisters and subsequently by a registered deed of gift dated 27.10.1999 pre-emptor Sabitri-Sundari Mali transferred 72 acre of land of this plot No. 334 to her son Sunil Chandra Biswas, that is, she transferred 30 acre land more than her actual share in that plot No. 334 and  thus she lost her  entire interest  in this contiguous plot No. 334. Mr. Bivash Chandra Biswas, the learned Counsel for the appellant though has assailed the finding of the High Court Division that Sabitri Sundari Mali lost her entire interest in this contiguous plot No.  334 but could not controvert the finding of the High Court Division that Sabitri Sundari Mali acquired only 42 acre of land in this plot No.  334 by virtue of inheritance and by purchase. The learned Counsel though claimed that the preemptor Subitri Sundari Mali still had 02 acre land in this contiguous plot No. 334, but could not establish that this 02 acre land out of vast 72 acre land of this plot No. 334 was contiguous to the case plot No. 335. The learned Counsel for the appellants however has made argument to the effect also that in another plot No. 333 the pre-emptor Sabitri Sundari Mali had subsisting interest and thus she was entitled to get the pre-emption of the land in question. But to substantiate this argument the learned Counsel could not produce necessary materials before us, rather it appears that in the amendment petition filed by the pre-emptor Sabitri Sundari Mali before the appellate Court below praying for amendment of the pre-emption petition including the alleged fact that she was a contiguous land holder also the plot No. 334 though has been mentioned as contiguous plot but plot No. 333 was not mentioned as contiguous plot. Before this Court or before any other courts below the appellants could not prove that the plot No. 333 also is adjacent to case plot No. 335. Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, on the other hand, has submitted to the effect that this plot No. 333 is not contiguous to plot No. 335 and that the preemptor Sabitri Sundari Mali lost her entire interest in this plot No. 333 also.</u>

<u>8. However, we do not find any reason to interfere with the impugned judgment of the High Court Division. The High Court Division has written a very elaborate and exhaustive judgment which suffers from no legal infirmity. It should be mentioned here that the High Court Division in the impugned judgment has held also that the preemption case was bad for non-impleading the contiguous land holders. This finding and decision of the High Court Division has not been assailed in this appeal. In the circumstances, it appears that this pre-emption case is bad for defect of party also.</u>

<u>9. From the above discussions, it is evident that this appeal must fail.</u>

10. Hence, the appeal is dismissed on contest without any order as to costs.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1281 of 2010
lawyer:
Mahbubey Alam, Attorney General instructed by B. Hossain, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioners

parties:
Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh represented by the Deputy, Commissioner Dhaka and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Md. Bazlul Karim and others ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment dated 12.04.2010 passed by the high Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2558 of 2007)
full_judgment:
Nazmun Ara Sultana J.: This appeal, interest in more than .0090 acres of land of C.S. Plot No. 371 and also for directing the defendant No. 1 to hand Over possession of the 'Ga' schedule land to the plaintiffs within 30 days, in default to pass a decree entitling the plaintiffs to take possession of the same land through Court.

2. The defendant.Nos. 1-7 appeared in that suit and filed an application under Order 7 Rule 11 read with Order 14 Rule 20 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for rejection of the plaint or in the alternative for hearing of the law points first. The learned Subordinate Judge, by the order dated 27.07.1999, rejected the said application of the defendants. Being aggrieved by that order dated 27.07.1999 the defendants preferred Civil Revision No. 2757 of 1999 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule. A Division Bench of the High Court Division, after hearing both the parties, and considering the facts and circumstance, made that Rule absolute setting aside the impugned order and allowing the defendants application under Order 7 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of plaint by the impugned judgment and order dated 18.11.1999 holding thus: "this is a fit case where the provisions of Order 7 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure are applicable and as such the plaint is liable to be rejected". Being aggrieved by this judgment and order dated 18.11.1999 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2757 of 1999 the plaintiffs preferred Civil Petition No. 125 of 2000 which though was once dismissed summarily, but subsequently, on review, the said civil petition was allowed and leave was granted to examine whether the contesting defendants practiced fraud upon Court in obtaining the judgment in their favour in the earlier Title Suit No. 177 of 1994 and whether the High Court Division considered this allegation of fraud raised by the plaintiffs in passing the impugned judgment.

3. Mr. Mahmudul Islam, the learned Senior Advocate has appeared for the appellants, Mr. T.H. Khan and Mr. Mainul Hossain, the learned Senior Advocates have appeared for the respondent No. 1, Mr. Mohammad Nazim Islam, the learned Senior Advocate has appeared for respondent No. 4 and Dr. M. Zahir; the learned Senior Advocate has appeared for the respondent No. 7. We have heard all the learned advocates in details.

4. Mr. Mahmudul Islam, the learned Counsel for the Appellants has mainly argued to the effect that in the earlier suit the contesting defendants very cleverly practiced fraud upon the. Court in obtaining the judgments in their favour and that  in the subsequent suit this allegation of fraud though was specifically agitated for declaring the decree of the earlier suit illegal and ineffective, but the High Court Division in rejecting the plaint of the subsequent suit did not at all take into consideration this allegation of fraud. To elaborate this argument Mr. Mahmudul Islam has stated that in the earlier suit the contesting defendants although claimed that the C.S. Plot No. 371 measured only .0090 acres that is 90 Ajutangsha land only and in support of this claim the defendants produced also a printed copy of C.S. Khatian No. 4300 'Ja' which showed that the C.S. Plot No. 371 measured .0090 acres of land only. The learned Counsel has contended that by making such false statement and producing false and forged copy of C.S. Khatian No. 4300 'Ja' the defendants made the court believe that this C.S. Plot No. 371 actually measured .0090 acres (90 Ajutangsha) land only and there by very cleverly made the court find that the defendants purchased the entire land of C.S. Plot No. 371 by 5 registered kabalas the exhibit-Ka to Ka-4. To support this argument the learned Advocate has drawn our attention to the judgment of the Appellate Division passed in Civil Petition for leave to appeal No. 412 of 1998 and Civil Review Petition No. 45 of 1998 and submitted that in both these judgments the Appellate Division clearly stated that the defendants claimed and also proved that the Plot No. 371 measured 0090 acres of land. The learned Advocate has contended that this finding of the Appellate Division proves sufficiently that the defendant by practicing fraud upon the Court made the Court believe that the C.S. Plot No. 371 measured only .0090 acres of land and thus managed the judgment in their favour with the finding that they purchased the entire land of the C.S. Plot No. 371 and therefore the plaintiffs had no subsisting interest in this plot. Mr. Mahmudul Islam has argued that in the impugned judgment the High Court Division did not at all consider this allegation of fraud and as such arrived at wrong findings and decision. Mr. Mahmudul Islam has argued also that the High Court Division committed wrong also in holding that since the judgment of the trial Court in earlier. Title Suit No. 177 of 1994 was upheld by the Appellate Division this judgment cannot be now declared illegal and ineffective by the Subordinate Court without taking into consideration the allegation of fraud in obtaining this judgment. The learned Counsel has contended that if it is now proved and accepted that the said judgment of the earlier suit was obtained by practicing fraud upon Court there will be no legal bar far the Subordinate Court to declare this judgment illegal and ineffective even if it was affirmed by the Appellate Division. The learned Advocate has argued further that had the High Court Division taken into consideration the allegation of fraud it would have found clear fraud  practiced by the defendants in obtaining the judgment in the earlier suit and then it would not have found any legal bar in entertaining and maintaining the subsequent suit.

5. Mr. T.R. Khan and other learned Advocates for the respondents have made submissions to the effect that no fraud was at all committed by the defendants in the earlier suit, that in the earlier suit one of the main questions raised was what quantum of land the C.S. Plot No. 371. contained and that both the trial Court and the appellate Court in the earlier suit made proper investigation including measurement of C.S. Plot No. 371 by a Survey knowing Advocate Commissioner and found that the C.S. Plot No. 371 contained .9007 acres of land and that the defendants purchased the entire land of this plot that from the reading of judgments of both the trial Court and the appellate Court in earlier Title Suit No. 177 of 1994 it is also very much clear that in the earlier suit the defendants rather claimed that though in their purchase deeds the quantum of land of C.S. Plot No. 371 was written as .0090 acres in view of wrong recording. In C.S. Khatian but in fact this plot contains .90 acres of land and they purchased the entire land of this plot by 5 registered kabalas the exhibits-Ka-Ka (4) The learned Advocates for the defendant respondents have argued also that in Civil Revision No. 2757 of 1999 the High Court Division considered all these facts, and also the judgments of the trial Court and appellate Court in earlier Title Suit No. 177 of 1994 and clearly found that in the earlier suit it was found out by the court through proper investigation that C.S. Plot No. 371 measured .9007 acres of land and that the defendant purchased this entire land of the C.S. Plot No. 371 and in the circumstance the allegation that in the earlier suit the defendants practiced fraud by making the courts believe that this plot No. 371 contains .0090 acres (90 Ajutangsha) land only does not stand at all. The learned Advocates for the defendants has contended that in the facts and Circumstances the High Court Division rightly allowed the defendants application for rejection of plaint.

6. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates of all the contesting parties and the facts and circumstance narrated above. We have also examined the judgment of the trial Court and the appellate Court in earlier Title Suit No. 177 of 1994. It appears in the earlier suit one of the important questions raised for determination was what quantum of land the C.S. Plot No. 371 actually contained. It appears that to resolve this question the trial Court appointed a survey knowing Advocate Commissioner to find out the actual quantum of land of C.S. Plot No. 371 and this appointed Advocate Commissioner, on measurement, found that this C.S. Plot No. 371 contained .9007 acres of land. The trial Court and also the appellate Court took into consideration this Advocate Commissioner's report 4nd also discussed about it in their respective judgments and clearly recorded their finding also that this C.S. Plot No. 371 contained .9007 acres of land. So in these facts and circumstances the argument of the learned Counsel for the appellants that in the earlier suit the defendants, by practicing fraud, made the Courts believe that this C.S. Plot No.  3716 contains .0090 acres (90 Ajutangsha) land only and thus managed the court's finding that they purchased the entire land of the C.S. Plot No. 371does not stand at all. In the stated facts and circumstance where in the earlier suit both the trial Court and appellate Court by making elaborate discussion clearly found that the C.S. Plot No. 371 measured 9007 acres of land it is not acceptable at all that the defendants in the earlier suit made the Court hold that the defendants purchased the entire land of C.S. Plot No. 371 on the basis of their wrong belief that the C.S. Plot No. 371 measured .0090, acres (90 Ajutangsha) land only. It appears from the judgments of the trial Court and the appellate Court in the earlier suit that both the Courts, on consideration of all the facts and circumstance and evidence on record, clearly found out that the C.S. Plot No. 371 actually contained 9007 acres of land and by the 5 registered kabalas of the year. 1954-55 the exhibit-Ka-Ka (4) the defendants purchased the entire land of this C.S. Plot No.  371. This concurrent finding and decision of the trial Court and the appellate Court were affirmed by the Appellate Division in Civil 'Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 412 of 1998. In the judgment of the Civil Petition for leaves to Appeal No. 412 of 1998 the full Court of the Appellate Division clearly observed "We have ourselves gone through the evidence produced by the parties and are satisfied that the Courts below have rightly decided the matter. In the face of concurrent finding of facts on the question of the area of C.S. Plot No.  371 in question we see no reason to interfere in this matter." Mr. Mahmudul Islam, the learned Counsel for the appellant has drawn our attention to 2 sentences of the judgment of this Appellate Division which arc thus "the defendants contended that the plot actually measured 0090 acres.." and "all these documents consistently prove that the total area of the plot was .0090 acres " Mr. Islam has contended that these very two sentences of the judgment of the Appellate Division prove that the defendants in the earlier suit' by their fraudulent act made the Court believe that the C.S. Plot No. 371 actually contained .0090 acres of land. But in view of above discussion it is evident that this contention of the learned Counsel is not correct and not acceptable at all. It has already been discussed above that in the earlier suit the defendants rather pleaded and claimed that the C.S. Plot No.  371. though actually measured 90 acres of land but in the C.S. Khatian, through mistake it has been wrongly recorded as .0090 acres (90 Ajutangsha) and both the trial Court and appellate Court after proper investigation accepted this case of the contesting defendants and found that the C.S. Plot No.  371 actually measured 9007 acres of land and the Appellate Division also found, as has been quoted above, that the courts below rightly decided the matter and there was no reason to interfere with the concurrent finding of the trial Court and the appellate Court on the question of the area of C.S. Plot No. 371. Obviously the figure ".0090 acre" in the above quoted two sentences of the judgment of the Appellate Division in 'Civil Petition for leave to Appeal No. 412 of 1998 is a typing mistake and this mistake has been allowed to remain in this judgment inadvertently. This figure "0090 acres" obviously, has been typed wrongly in place of ".90 acres".

<u>7. Mr. Mahmudul Islam has argued also that the High Court Division's observation to the effect that since the judgment of the trial Court in earlier Title Suit No. 177 of 1994 was affirmed by the Appellate Division it cannot be now declared illegal by the trial Court-is erroneous. The learned advocate has argued that any judgment and decree obtained by practicing fraud can he declared illegal and void by the trial Court even after its affordance by the Appellate Division upon proof of fraud. This argument of the learned Counsel does not require much discussion in view of the facts and circumstances discussed above. It is true that. fraud vitiates everything; even a judgment the decree affirmed by the apex Court of the Country can be declared illegal and void by the trial Court if it is proved that the judgment and decree was obtained by practicing fraud upon Court. But mere allegation of fraud is not enough to entertain a suit for declaring a judgment and decree affirmed by the apex court of country illegal. Unless strong prima facie case of fraud is made out and sufficient acceptable evidence and materials are produced before court to substantiate the allegation of fraud a suit for declaring a judgment and decree affirmed by the apex court of the Country should not be entertained. In the present case, from the very record, the allegation of fraud has been proved baseless and not acceptable at all.</u>

<u>8. However, from the above discussion it is evident that the High Court Division committed no wrong in allowing the defendants application under Order 7 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint of Title Suit No. 42 of 1999 of the 5th Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka. The parties of this subsequent Title Suit No. 42 of 1999 and the parties of earlier Title Suit No. 177 of 1994, are same, the subject mailer of both these suits being the entire land of C.S. Plot No. 371 of C.S. Khatian 4300 'Ja' of Mouza Shahar Dhaka, are same and also the issue raised and settled in the earlier suit and the issue for determination in the subsequent suit are same. In the circumstances the subsequent suit is barred  by the principle resjudicata as enunciated in section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure and as such the High Court Division rightly allowed the application under order 7 Rule 11 of the Code o4t Civil Procedure and rightly rejected the plaint of subsequent suit. We find nothing to interfere with the impugned judgment of the High Court Division.</u>

9. Leave is granted (on the additional ground).

10. Petitioner is permitted paper book out of Court with Rules to prepare the in accordance

11. The order of stay granted earlier he extended till disposal of the appeal.

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 10 March 1999 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3538 of 1993)
full_judgment:
Md. Tafazzul Islam J: This appeal, by way of leave, arises out of judgment and decree dated 10.3.1999 passed in Civil Revision No. 3538 of 1993 discharging the Rule affirming the judgment and decree dated 21.11.1993 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Cox's Bazar in Other Class Appeal No.59 of 1987 affirming those dated 3.8.1987 passed in Other Suit No. 175 of 1978 by the learned Assistant Judge, Sadar, Cox's Bazar decreeing the suit.

2. The respondents, as plaintiffs, instituted the above suit praying for declaration of title and also recovery of possession of .07 acres of land, being part of land of R.S. Plot No. 2543 appertaining to R.S. Khatian No.1109 at Mouza Cox's Bazar as described in the schedule of the plaint, stating inter alia that .14 acres of land of the above R.S. Plot No.2543 along with other land, belonged to Nilamber Chowdhury and he by patta dated 30.3.1936, settled .07 acres of land i.e. the suit land, from the above R. S. Piot No. 2543 along with other land of R. S. Plot Nos. 2537, 2538 and 2541 of the said khatian to Nalini Ranjan Dutta and that aforesaid R. S. plot No. 2543 was wrongly   printed twice in the R. S. Map and further   R.S. plot No. 2540 was also printed as R. S. plot No. 2543 and that the description as to boundary of the land attached to the schedule of the patta dated 30.4.36 was wrong and that since Nalini Ranjan Dutta was in possession of the suit land the same was recorded in M.R.R. Khatian No. 568 as plot No. 869 and the remaining .07 acres of the said R.S. Plot No. 2543 was recorded in the name of Nur Ali Chowdhury arid others; Nalini Ranjan sold out the land of R. S. Plot Nos. 2538, 2541 and the suit land to the plaintiff and Nur Ahmed in his turn sold his interest to Saleha Begum, wife of the plaintiff, and that the plaintiff mutated his name and the B. S. Khatian was prepared in his name in spite of the objection of the defendant who has no right, title or possession, in the suit land, in the month of April 1978 the plaintiff was in Dhaka and taking advantage of his absence the defendant forcibly erected structure on the suit land and thereby dispossessed the plaintiff from the suit land. The defendant appellant contested the suit and filed written statements denying the material allegations and contending, inter alia, that the above R. S. Plot No.2543 comprising an area of .14 acres belonged to Nilambar Mahajan who settled .36 acre of land including .14 acres of land of plot No.2543 to one Mosan Ali by registered patta dated 12.5.1936 and after death of Mosen Ali his heirs sold out their interest in favour of Hossain Ali Medbar, Hakim Ali Chowdhury, Yakub Ali Chowdhury, Noor Ali Chowdhury and Shahar Ali Chowdhury by registered kabala dated 08.10.1937, while the aforesaid Hossain Ali Medbar and others were in possession of the suit land, Hakim Ali Chowdhury and the heirs of Hossain Ali Matbar and Yakub Ali Chowdhury sold out their right, title and interest to the defendant No.1 by kabala dated 19.6.1961 and since then the defendant No.1 have been in peaceful possession of the same and got a plan approved by Cox's Bazar Pourashava for construction, Nalini Ranjan Dana, was granted settlement of all the lands of the R. S. Plot Nos. 2437/ 2538/ 2541 measuring 0.26 acre of land and 314 gondas, i.e. .07 acres of land, from the R. S. Plot No. 2540 and from the boundary of the above .07 acre of R. S. plot No. 2543 as given in the said patta it is clear that Nalini Ranjan Dutta took settlement from plot No. 2540 and not from plot No.2543; Nalini Ranjan Dutta possessed the lands settled by said patta including .07 acre of R. S. plot No. 2540 situated within the boundary given in the patta more than thirty years and he never took settlement of the suit land and never possessed the same and Nilambar Mohajan never granted settlement of the suit land to Nalini Ranjan Dutta and the plaintiff to grab the suit land, has given a totally different boundary in the schedule of the plaint only to show that the suit land relates to the R. S. plot No.2543 and not to the Khas Plot No.2540 wrongly printed as plot No.2543 measuring 0.25 acre only. The learned Assistant Judge, Sadar, Cox's Bazar decreed the suit. On appeal the learned Additional District Judge, Cox's Bazar, after hearing, dismissed the appeal. The defendant then filed Civil Revision No. 3538 of 1993 and after hearing   High Court Division discharged the 7 Rule.

3. Leave was granted to consider as to whether in view of the evidence of the plaintiff, P.W.2, that he has got a hotel named "Niribili" and since the hotel compound, hotel courtyard and the bridge connecting the road as well as the hotel stands on the lands of Plot Nos.2537, 2538, 2540 and 2541 it is clear that the plaintiff is in possession of the land leased out by Patta dated 30 April 1936 and not on the suit land which is Plot No.2543 and the High Court Division has failed to consider the same.

4. The learned counsel appearing for the defendant appellant submits that the defendant appellants having made out a clear case in their written statement that they got lease of land of Plot No.2540 as indicated by the boundary given in the patta dated 30.4.36, there should have been an issue as to identity of the land settled by the Patta dated 30.4.1936 but neither such issue as to identity of the land attracted by the patta dated 30.4.36 was framed nor the plaintiff respondents took any step for local investigation to ascertain the identity of suit land and thereby the courts below and the High Court Division erred in law in deciding the title of the plaintiff in Plot No.2543 without at all ascertaining the identity of the land leased out to him by patta dated 30.4.1936 and further the courts below did not consider the map, Ext.4, which proves that the lease by patta dated 30.4.1936 was in respect of the land of Plot No.2540 and not 2543 and that P.W.2 in his deposition stated that he has a hotel named "Niribili" and the hotel compound, hotel courtyard, the bridge connecting the road and the hotel stands on the lands of Plot Nos.2537, 2538, 2540 and 2541 which shows that the plaintiff respondent is in possession of the land leased out by patta dated 30.4.1936 i.e. .07 acres of plot No. 2540 and not the suit land which is Plot No. 2543.

5. The learned counsel appearing for the plaintiff respondent No.1 on the other hand submits that R.S. Plot No. 2543 appertains to P.S. Khatian No.1109 belonged to Nilambor Mohajan who granted Dar Rayoti settlement of .36 acres land of plot No. 2543 to one Mohasen Ali by a registered patta dated 12.5.1936 and on the death of Mohasen Ali his heirs sold their interested to Hossan Ali Madbar and his brothers by registered deed of sale dated 08.10.1937 and from them the defendant No.1 purchased the land on 19.9.1961 by registered deed of sale and has been in possession since then and that the learned Assistant Judge decreed the suit on the finding that by the pasta dated 30.4.1936 executed by Nilambor Mahajan only .07 acres of land in R. S. Plot No. 2543 was settled with Nolini Ranjan Dana on Dar Rayoti and thereafter the Nolini Ranjan Dutta by a registered kabala dated 2.5.1969 sold the above property to the plaintiff and the said Nilambor Chowdhury sold .07 acres of land to one Kali Komer Paul on 3.3.1937 by registered deed as such the total 14 acres of land appertaining to R.S. Plot No.2543 was sold out and Ext.5 would show that by Mutation Case No. 1044/69-70 the name of the plaintiff was recorded in the record of right and the plaintiff paid rent and had remained in possession of the land and Ext. 6 series show that the name of the plaintiff has been recorded in the R. S. khatian and it also appears that R. S. Plot No.2540 is the khas land of the Government and the High Court Division in consideration of the materials on records rightly did not interfere with the concurrent findings of the courts below which are also based on the evidence and materials on record.

<u>6. As it appears the learned Assistant Judge found that by patta of Nilambar Mahason dated 30.4.1936 i.e. Ext.2, only .07 acres of land in R.S. Plot No. 2543 was settled with Nalini Ranjan Dutta on Dar Raioti and thereafter the vendee Nolini Ranjan Dutta by a registered kabala dated 2.5.1969 sold the property in favour of the plaintiff and the said Nilambor Chowdhury sold the remaining .07 acres of land in favour and Kalikomar Paul on 3.3.1937 by registered deed as such the entire .14 acres of land appertaining to R.S. Plot No. 2543 was sold out and from the materials on record it is also evident that Mutation Case No. 1044/69-70, the suit land was mutated in the name of the plaintiff after disallowing the objection raised by the defendant appellant and thereafter the plaintiff paid rent against the suit land and remained in possession of the suit land and from Ext. 6 series it also transpired that the name of the plaintiff has been recorded in the 13.S. khatian and that R.S. Plot No. 2540 is the khas land of the Government and further even the defendant No.2, who deposed as D.W.2, in his cross-examination admitted that the patta granted by Nilambar Mohasan in favour of Nolini Ranjan Dutta is a genuine one and in that patta the R.S. Plot No. 2543 has been mentioned and further D.W.2 in his cross-examination also admitted that the suit land has been recorded in the M.R.R. khatian No.586 in the name of the plaintiff and the defendant No.1 has no claim in the said suit land appertaining to M.R.R. khatian No. 586.</u>

<u>7. It also appears that the learned Additional District Judge, who heard the appeal, considering the documentary evidence similarly found that Nilambar Mahajan, the original owner of the suit property settled the same in favour of Nolini Ranjan Dutta by registered patta, Ext.2, and the adjacent R.S. Plot No.2540 the nature of which is a nal land is a khas land of the Government and the suit land was recorded in the name Nolini Ranjan Duna and the plaintiff purchased the suit land by kabala dated 1.5.1969, Exbt.3, and his name was duly recorded in the records of right and though an objection was raised by the defendant against the mutation of the name of the plaintiff but the same was disallowed and D.W. 1, the scribe of the above sale deed, stated that the dag number was inserted in the kabala wrongly and he wrote it on the advice of the defendant and that D.W.2 has admitted that he has no right, title and interest in the suit land and the R.S. Plot No. 2543 has been wrongly crept in his sale deed and the land in M.R.R. Khatian No.586 belonged to the plaintiff and he has no claim therein and considering that the defendant have disclaimed their title in the suit land and that the defendant trespassed into the land of the plaintiff as has been established by report of the pleader commissioner, affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the trial court. The High Court Division considering that the impugned judgment and decree dated 21.11.1993 are judgment and decree of affirmance and are based on materials on record, declined to interfere with the same.</u>

8. We are of the view that the High Court Division on correct appreciation of the materials on record discharged the Rule and accordingly no interference is called for.

9. The appeal is dismissed with costs.

End.
