case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 03.10.2010 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.6864 of 2004)
full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hossain J: This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 03.10.2010 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 6864 of 2004 making the Rule absolute.

2. The facts, leading to the filing of this petition for leave to appeal, in short, are as follows:

3. On 16.09.2000, writ-petitioner filed an application to writ-respondent No. 1 for allotment of about 3 kathas of land appertaining to R.S. Plot Nos. 1101 (part) and 1435 (part) of Chittagong Agrabad Commercial Area for running his business. On 19.09.2000, office of writ-respondent No. 1 received the application with a remark to take necessary steps. In view of the aforesaid application of the writ-petitioner, writ-respondent No. 4 issued allotment letter on 15.7:2001, vide Memo No.  শাখা-৯/১এল-২২/২০০০/১৭৪ on the terms and conditions mentioned therein. Thereafter, writ-respondent No.  6 issued a letter on 1.8.2001 asking the writ Petitioner to deposit 25% of the value of the allotted land. A.s per direction of writ-respondent No. 6, the writ-petitioner deposited taka 3,50,307.00 i.e. 25% of the value of the allotted land, vide Chalan No.  Ta-2 dated 5.8.2001 with Chittagong Branch of Bangladesh Bank. In respect of the allotted land Other Class Appeal No.  311 of 1991 was filed by Amelia Khatun and others and the said appeal was dismissed for default. Against the said order of dismissal the appellant has not taken any Step On 19.08.2004 writ respondent No. 6 wrote a letter to writ-respondent No. 5 seeking direction in respect of execution of lease deed and handing over possession of the allotted land to the writ petitioner. Since handing over of possession of the allotted land to the writ-petitioner Was being, delayed he filed an application to writ respondent No. 1 On 2.10.200 informing him about a decision of cancellation of the said allotment and re allotment of the same in favour of one Engineer Abu Siddique. In the application the writ-petitioner also made request to hand possession of the said allotted land to him. After that on 6.10.2004 writ respondent No. 6 wrote a letter to writ respondent No. 5 making proposal for some correction in the letter dated 19.8.2004. By his order under Memo No. শাখা-৯/১এল-২২/২০০০/৬৯২ dated 4.1 2004 respondent No. 4 cancelled the allotment of the writ-petitioner without issuing any notice for showing cause. Pursuant to the allotment letter the writ-petitioner deposited 25% of the value of the allotted land and thereafter applied to the concerned authority to hand over possession of the land to him. But because of pendency of a suit in respect of the land, handing over of possession was sespended for the time being and subsequently the suit was dismissed. Thereafter the writ-petitioner applied to writ-respondent No. 6 to execute and register the lease deed on acceptance of the remaining amount of the salami. Writ-respondent No. 6 recommended registering the lease deed in favour of the writ-petitioner to his higher authority. Writ-respondent Nos. 3 and 5 recommended handing over possession of the allotted land in favour of the writ-petitioner to writ respondent No. 1 but because or some reason not known to him the handing over of possession was delayed. It has been stated hi the application that the writ-petitioner did not violate any of the terms and conditions of the letter of allotment and no notice for showing cause Was served upon him regarding, cancellation of his allotment. In the circumstances, the writ-petitioner through his learned Advocate sent a telegraphic notice to writ-respondent No. 4 demanding justice but to no avail. Alter that the writ-petitioner filed the writ-petition.

4. After issuance of the Rule, the writ-petitioner filed an application for addition of party as well as for issuing further Rule reiterating the facts stated in the writ petition and stating further that since civil litigation as pending regarding the ownership of the allotted land no deed of lease was executed and possession of the allotted land has handed over to him. While waiting for the next step to be taken by the writ respondents suddenly, the writ-petitioner came to know that one Abu Bakkar Sidddique prayed for allotment of the said allotted land by cancelling the allotment of the writ-petitioner and respondent No.  4 by his order under Memo No.  শাখা-৯/১এল-২২/২০০০/৬৯২ a dated 4.12.2004 cancelled the allotment of the writ-petitioner. Challenging the said order of cancellation, the writ-petitioner filed the writ petition in which he obtained Rule and an interim order staying operation of the above mentioned letter. The allotment of the writ-petitioner was cancelled on 4.12.2004 and on the same date (4.12.2000) the land in question was allotted to one Abu Bakar Siddique. The Judge Court Division was in seisin of the matter and knowing fully well about the issuance of Rule respondent No. 4 by his letter under Memo No. শাখা-৯/১-২২/২০০০/৭৪৩/১(৫) dated 23.12. 2004 permitted said Abu Bakkar Siddique to deposit money in respect of the land in question and on 28.12.2004, possession of the said land was handed over to him. The allottee Abu Bakar Siddique tried to raise boundary wall of undertake construction work on the land in question. After making inquiry in the office, the writ-petitioner came to know that the land in question was allotted to Abu Bakar Siddique but as the writ-petitioner had no knowledge of the disputed allotment of Abu Bakar Siddique, he had no scope for challenging the allotment letter dated 4.12.2004 in the writ petition. In the aforesaid circumstances, allottee Abu Bakar Siddique was required to be added as respondent to the writ petition as respondent No. 7. After hearing the application for addition of party on 17.8.2006, Abu Bakar Siddique of 9/11, Panna Para, Agrabad, Police Station Double Mooring, District Chittagong, was added as respondent No.  7 and further Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the writ-respondents to show cause as to why Memo No.  শাখা-৯/১-২২/২০০০/৬৯৩/১(৭) dated 4.12.2004 and the letter under Memo No.  শাখা-৯/১এল-২২/২০০০/৭৪৩/১৭(৫) dated 23.12. 2004 (annexure K and L) issued by writ-respondent No.  4 in favour of writ-respondent No.  7 should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and to be of no legal effect. At the time of issuance of the second Rule, writ-respondent No.  7 was restrained from Making any construction on the land in question or changing the nature and character thereof for a period of 3(three) months from date. Subsequently, the said order of restraint was extended from time to time and the same remained in force till hearing of the Rule.

5. The Rules were contested by writ-respondent Nos.  6 the Executive Engineer, Public works Circle-1, Chittagong, and added writ-respondent No.  7 by filing separate sets of affidavits-n-opposition.

6. In his affidavit-in-opposition writ-respondent No. 7. Controverted the material allegations made in the writ-petition. His case, in short, is that the writ-petition involves questions of facts. After filing the same, the writ-petitioner has filed Other Suit No. 32 of 2005 in the Court of Joint District Judge, Second Court, Chittagong, which is pending and, as such, the instant writ petition is not maintainable. Office of writ-respondent No. 4 by letter dated 18.4.2000 instructed writ-respondent No. 7 to file the order of dismissal for default/withdrawal of Other Appeal No. 31 of 1991 filed by the original land owner Amena Khatun and others to facilitate allotment of the land in question to him. Writ-respondent No. 7 obtained certified copy of the order of dismissal on 27.7.2004 and submitted the same to the Ministry of Housing and Public Works on 31.7.2004 for taking necessary action. After submitting the certified copy of the order of dismissal for default of the said appeal by writ-respondent No. 7 the writ-petitioner submitted the self-same certified copy on 4.10.2004. On 1.5.07.2001, the writ-petitioner illegally obtained allotment of the strip of land of R.S plot No. 1101 (part) with R.S plot. No.  1435 (part) owned by writ-respondent No. 7 from the Ministry of Public works by suppressing the fact that R.S. Plot No.  1435 is not an acquired land but is a private land exclusively owned by writ-respondent No. 7 by way of purchase from its original owner Amena Khatun and others. The writ-petitioner also suppressed the fact that R.S. Plot No.  1101 is adjacent to R.S. Plot No. 1435 and is the only passage of the writ-respondent No. 7 for his ingress and egress from the other adjacent private land owned by him. In obtaining the allotment, the earlier applications dated 17.7.1999 and 13.07.2001 filed by the writ-respondent No. 7 to respondent No.  For granting him lease of R.S. Plot No. 1101 (part) were by-passed. On 27.05.2003, writ-respondent No. 7 filed an application to writ-respondent No. 1 for cancelling the illegal allotment given to the writ-petitioner and then to give allotment to him the land of plot No. 1101(part). In the application writ-respondent No. 7 stated in detail about the fraudulent activities of the writ-petitioner and suppression of actual facts by him in obtaining the allotment of the land in question. On the basis of the application of writ-respondent No. 7 dated 27.5.2003 two physical inquiries were held, one by respondent No. 4 on 15.8.2002 and the other by the concerned Ministry itself on 20.11.2003 within the knowledge of the writ-petitioner and they submitted their reports in the matter. Both the inquiry reports revealed that R.S. plot No. 1435 is not an acquired land of the Government and that it is owned by writ-respondent No. 7. The inquiry reports also disclosed that the land of R.S. Plot No. 1101 acquired by the government is adjacent to R.S. Plot No. 1435 and as such, the claim of the writ-petitioner in the application filed by him on 2.10.2004 that writ-respondent No. 7 has no land adjacent to R.S. Plot No.  1101 was not proved. The entire matter has been reflected in the opinion of the legal Adviser of the Ministry of Housing and Public Works dated 5.8.2003.

7. Respondent No.  4 also in his inquiry report dated 15.8.2002 passed similar opinion. Moreover, it is evident from note No.  37 of the note sheets of the Ministry dated 24.8.2002 that writ-respondent No.  4 in his inquiry report gave indication for resolving the dispute with the writ-petitioner, the previous allottee by allotting him another plot instead of the land in question.

8. The writ-petitioner was quite aware of, and participated in, the above mentioned inquiry process which is evident from his own statements made in paragraph No.  8 of the writ petition wherein the writ-petitioner categorically stated that he came to know about the cause of action on 2.10.2004, that is, two months before the cancellation of his allotment on 4.12.2004 and further allotment in the name of writ-respondent No. 7 on the same date (4.12.2004) and as such, in law there was no necessity for issuing any notice to the writ-petitioner For showing cause. Private properties of writ-respondent No. 7 i.e. H.S. plot No. 1435 (part) has been allotted in favour of the writ-petitioner and on coming to know about the said Fact he made an objection in writing to the concerned authority for cancelling the allotment of the writ-petitioner. Consequently, the writ-petitioner did not pay the remaining amount of the salami and no lease deed was executed in his favour. On 02.10.2004, the writ-petitioner submitted objection to respondent No. 1 informing him about the decision of cancellation of said allotment and re-allotment of the land in question in the name of writ-respondent No. 7. The writ-respondents considered the objection of the writ-petitioner by way of several physical investigations and as such, the writ-petition is not maintainable in the eye of law. Writ-respondent No. 7 Purchased 0.825 acre of land from R.S. plot Nos. 1435, 1436, 1437 of R.S. Khatian No. 496 corresponding to R.S. plots No. 3256 arid 3257 of R.S. Khatian No. 687 under mouza Gosaidanga Police Station Double mooring. District Chittagong vide registered deed No. 1849 dated 11.3.1999 and deed No. 2946 dated 6.5.1999. After purchase writ-respondent No. 7 mutated his time vide Mutation Case No.  6953 of 1998-99 dated 23.11.1999 and has been possessing the land. Here is a strip land of R.S. Plot No. 1101 adjacent to the land of R.S. plot No.  1.435. Writ-respondent No. 7 is the owner of R.S plot No.  1435; R.S. plot No. 1101 was acquired by the government and the writ-respondent No. 7 has been using the said land as his only passage so he filed an application on 17.7.1999 to writ-respondent No. 1 leasing out the said land to him. But by keeping the application of writ respondent No. 7 pending, the land of R.S. plot 1101 (part) including R.S. plot No.  1435 (part) was leased out to the writ-petitioner. On coming to know about the said lease writ-respondent No. 7 filed several applications to writ-respondent No.  1 for leasing out the said land of R.S. plot 1101 to him by cancelling the earlier allotment of the writ-petitioner. Considering the above facts, writ-respondent No. 1 informed the writ petitioner about the above mentioned irregularity of lease and after discussion with the writ petitioner cancelled his allotment and allotted 2.98 kathas of land of R.S. plot No. 1101 to writ-respondent No. 7 on 4.12.2004 (Annexure-K to the writ petition). On receipt of entire lease money writ-respondent No. 1 registered the lease deed, and handed over possession of the lease hold property to writ-respondent No. 7. Writ-respondent No. 7 has since been possessing the lease hold property as his passage from his other properties.

9. In the affidavit-in-opposition filed by writ-respondent No. 6 it has been contended. Inter-alia that the Public Works Department/Circle -1 Chittagong, owned a strip of land in R.S. Plot No.  1101 (part) adjacent to R.S. Plot No.  1435 owned by Engr. A. B. Siddique the present lessee of the strip of land. The writ-petitioner prayed for giving him lease of 3(three) kathas of land of R.S. plot No-1101(part) and R.S. Plot No.  1435 (part) vide his application dated 16.9.2000 and writ-respondent No. 7 filed application For allotment on 17.7.1999. The present lessee was instructed by the office of writ-respondent No. 4 by letter dated 18.4.2004 to file the order of dismissal of Other Appeal No 331 of 1991 to facilitate allotment of the land in question. Accordingly he filed the order of dismissal dated 24.7.2004 which was sent to the ministry on 31.07.2004 for necessary action. The Government had adopted policy from time to time for allotment of plots and strips of land and according to that policy writ-respondent No.  4 issued Memo No.  shakha-911.1-22/2000/692 dated 4.12.2001 cancelling the allotment of the writ-petitioner. Only 25% of the value was deposited by the writ-petitioner out of total amount of value of the land. But because of the pendency of Other Appeal No. 311 of 1991 before the Sixth Additional District Judge, Chittagong and objection of adjacent plot owner, writ-respondent No. 7. The possession of the land could not be delivered to the writ-petitioner. The whole process of cancellation of allotment was done within the knowledge of the writ-petitioner. Actually, writ-respondent No.  7 is the owner of R.S. Plot No.  1435 which is adjacent to the disputed land owned by the government and his application was earlier than that of the writ-petitioner and as such, cancellation of allotment of the writ-petitioner and allotment of the land ill question in favour of writ-respondent No.  7 Were done owing to legal obligation. As the writ-petitioner filed Other Class Suit No.  32 of 2005 in the Court of Joint District Judge. Second Court, Chittagong seeking self-same relief for the same subject matter, the Rule is liable to be discharged.

10. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the order under Memo No. " শাখা-৯/১-এল-২২/২০০০/৬৯২ dated 4.12.2004 issued by respondent No. 4, the petitioner filed Writ Petition No. 6864 of 2004 before the High Court Division. The learned Judges of the High Court Division, upon hearing the parties, by the judgment and order dated 03.10,2010 made the Rules absolute and declared Annexure 'K' and 'L' to the writ-petition to have been issued without lawful authority.

11. Feeling aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division, writ-respondent No. 7 filed the instant Civil Petition for leave to Appeal.

12. Mr. T. H. Khan, learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the writ-respondent No. 7, submits that the learned Judges of the High Court Division erred in law in having failed to take notice of the fact that the writ-petitioner had no locus standi to file the present writ petition for enforcement or an incomplete and inconclusive contract of lease and that consequently, he could not complain of any grievance and as such the writ petition was not maintainable; moreover, the case bristles with disputed and complicated questions of fact, which cannot be decided in writ jurisdiction. In further submits that the High Court Division erred in law in not holding that the writ petitioner Kazi Akram Uddin, having filed the application for addition of party. on 15.08.2006, i.e. to add Engineer A. B. Siddique as respondent No. 7, the writ-petitioner himself filed Other Suit. No. 32 of 2005 on 28.02.2005 in the Second Court of Joint District Judge, Chittagong, making selfsame averments and seeking self-same relief, as is evident from the plaint of the suit, Annexure- VI and the learned Judges erred in law in not holding that on this ground alone the writ-petition is not maintainable, as the writ-petitioner had already sought appropriate and efficacious relief before a competent Civil Court. In support of his contention, the learned Advocate relies upon the cases of Shahjadi Begum and others vs. Mirza Gias Uddin, 21 BLD (AD) 59 and Chairman of Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh vs. Kazi Abdur Rouf and others, 46 DLR (AD)145. He then submits that the High Court Division erred in law in having failed to take notice of the fact that the right to property, as guaranteed under Article 42 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, is subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by law and that the Government has no right to transfer any private land without acquisition. Admittedly, the writ-petitioner's allotment letter contains some private land, more specifically, part of R.S. Plot No. 1435 not owned and possessed by the Government, rather by the present petitioner, therefore, the aforesaid allotment is void ab initio. He also submits that the curt cannot pass any order which is not executable, bill in the present ease, the High Court Division passed an order which is not executable for the inherent illegalities in the allotment letter itself, affecting the right to property of another and his legal right as well. His last sub-mission is that the writ-petitioner Kazi Akram Uddin had lull knowledge about the cancellation process and that he even raised objection vide Annexure-G to the writ-petition and that the authorities have already decided to allot him an alternative plot; hence, there was no malafide on the part of the Lessor and that it is also evident from Annexure-G that the writ-petitioner deliberately refrained from paying balance consideration; hence he cannot seek equity before any Court of law.

13. Mr. Mahmudul Islam learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of respondent No. 1, supports the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division.

<u>14. The above submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner merit consideration and as such, leave is granted to consider the following grounds:</u>

<u>1. Whether the learned Judges of the High Court Division erred in law in having failed to take notice of the fact that the writ-petitioner had no locus standi to file the present writ petition for enforcement of an incomplete and inconclusive contract of lease and the writ petition was not maintainable, and whether the case bristles with disputed and complicated question of fact., which cannot be decided in writ jurisdiction.</u>

<u>2. Whether the High Court Division erred in law in not holding that the writ-petitioner Kazi Akram Uddin, having filed the application for addition of party on 15.08.20061, i.e. to add Engineer A. B. Siddique as respondent No. 7, and he having filed Other Suit No. 32 of 2005 on 28.02.2005 in the Second Court of Joint District Judge, Chittagong, making self-same averments and seeking selfsame relief, as is evident from the plaint of the suit, the learned Judges erred in law in not holding that on this ground alone the writ-petition is not maintainable, as the writ-petitioner had already sought appropriate and efficacious relief before a competent Civil Court.</u>

<u>3.Whether the High Court Division erred in law in having failed to take notice of the fact that the right to property, as guaranteed under Article 42 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, is subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by law and the Government has no right to transfer any private land without acquisition as per provisions of law and whether the writ-petitioner's allotment letter contains some private land, more specifically, part of R.S. Plot No. 1435, not owned and possessed by the Government; rather by the present petitioner and the aforesaid allotment is void abinitio.</u>

<u>4. Whether the Court cannot pass any order which is not executable, and in the present case, the High Court Division passed an order which is not executable for the illegalities in the allotment letter itself, affecting the right to property of another and his legal right as well.</u>

<u>5. Whether the writ-petitioner Kazi Akram Uddin had full knowledge about the cancellation-process and he even raised objection vide Annexure-G to the writ-petition and the authorities have already decided to allot hint an alternative plot; and whether there was no malafide on the part of the lessor and it is also evident from Annexure-G that the writ-petitioner deliberately refrained from paying balance consideration and he cannot seek equity before any Court of law.</u>

15. Security of Tk. 1000/- is to be deposited within one month.

16. Preparation of paper book is dispensed with as prayed for.

17. The order of status quo granted earlier be extended till disposal of the appeal.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 164 of 2006
lawyer:
Mohammad Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioners 
Bivash Chandra Biswas, Advocate-on-Record ------ For Respondent Nos.1-2 
For the Respondent Nos.3-82 ------ None represented.
parties:
Most. Rabeya Khatun ------ Petitioner.
Vs.
Md. Afzal Hossain Prang and others ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 6th day of December, 2005 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.2638 of 2004).
full_judgment:
Mohammad Fazlul Karim J.: At the instance of the petitioner this petition for Leave to Appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 06.12.2005 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.2638 of 2004 discharging the Rule affirming the judgment and order dated 28.06.2004 passed by the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Bogra in Miscellaneous Appeal No.129 of 2002 allowing those dated 08.09.2002 passed in Miscellaneous Case No.31 of 1998 by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Bogra dismissing the same.

2. The respondent No.1 as pre-emptor filed a Miscellaneous Case No.34 of 1998 under Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act in the Court of the learned Assistant Judge, Bogra forgetting preempted the land transferred by the pre-emptee Nos. 2-4 in favour of pre-emptee by a kabala deed dated 22.05.1997 as contiguous land holder. The preemption case was filed stating, inter alia, that the preemptors were owner of Plot No. 981 and 962 and those two plots were contiguous to the Plot Nos. 967, 966, 965 and 964; that the land of those four plots belonged the pre-emptee Nos. 2-4 who sold 0.57 decimals of land from those four plots by kabala deed No.8257 dated 22.05.1997 in favour of the pre-emptee No.1; that the pre-emptee No.1 is a stranger purchaser to the said land; that the pre-emptors being contiguous land holder came to know about the said transfer on 01.04.1998, got the certified copy of the kabala deed on 05.04.1998 and filed the preemption case on 14.08.1998.

3. The pre-emptee No.1 contested the case by filing written objection denying the contiguity of the preemptors with the case land; that the pre-emptee is the owner of a portion of land of Plot Nos. 981 and 962; that the Plot Nos.981 and 962 are in spite of contiguous to Plot No.967 but the portion of land possessed by the preemption are not contiguous in the portion of land transferred by the deed under preemption from Plot No.962; that the portion of land Plot No.967 which is contiguous to the land of Plot No.981 is in possession of the pre-emptee Nos. 17 and 18; that thereafter, the contiguous portion of land of Plot No.967 measuring an area of 0.9 decimals of land is in possession of Moslem and Younus who have not been made parties; that thereafter, 0.18 decimals of land which is just contiguous to the Plot No.967 belongs to the pre-emptee-petitioner; that the land of Plot No.962 of the petitioner is contiguous to the Plot No.967; that there is no contiguity of the preemptors land with the land of Plot Nos. 964, 965, 966 and 967; that the pre-emptors were given offer to purchase the land under pre-emption but they denied to purchase the same expressing their inability; that thereafter, the pre-emptee Nos.2-4 sold the case land by the kabala under pre-emption in favour of the pre-emptee No.1(petitioner) within the knowledge of everybody; that the pre-emptors being not contiguous land holders the pre-emption case is liable to be dismissed.

4. Mr Mohammad Nawab Ali, learned Advocate-on-Record, appearing for the petitioner submitted that the High Court Division erred in law in failing to discuss and consider the evidence of P.W. 1 who himself admitted the fact that out of four plots of the land under pre-emption he is not a contiguous land holder in respect of plot Nos.964, 965 and 966 and in view of that admission the judgment and order is liable to be set aside; that it erred in law in failing to consider the admitted testimony of the P.W.1 that the pre-emptee is a contiguous land holder to plot No.962 only and in view of the said evidence the pre-emption at the instance of the pre-emptor was barred by law; that pre-emption case was not all maintainable in view of the fact that deposit of money as against the kabala deed under pre-emption was not made to the credit of the pre-emptee as per mandatory provisions of Section 96(3)(a) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act.

<u>5. It appears from the record that the pm-emptor filed a pre-emption case under Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the trial Court dismissed the pre-emption case holding that the pre-emptors were not the contiguous land holders of the land under pre-emption. On appeal; the Court of appeal below found that the disputed property is a compact block of land and the plots are contiguous to each other and also contiguous to pre-emptors land. The Court of appeal below specifically found that the pre emptor is a contiguous land holder of the disputed jote. The Court of appeal below relied upon a decision in the case of Haji Tajamal Ali vs. Abdus Sattar and another reported in 2BCR (AD) 317 wherein it is held that the preemptor being the contiguous land holder is entitled to pre-emption of the whole land transferred consisting of several plots out of which his land is contiguous to any of such plots and several plots forming a compact block of land, all the plots being contiguous to each other and contiguous to pre-emptor's land, the pre-emptor petitioner is entitled to pre-empt the entire block. The Court of appeal below relying upon decisions as reported in 2BCR (AD) 317 ibid which has also been published in 34 DLR (AD) 217 considering the materials on record allowed the pre-emption setting aside the judgment and order of the trial Court holding, inter alia, that "... we find the land transferred, though it consists of several plots, is a compact block of land, all the plots being themselves contiguous to each other. This compact block of land being contiguous to the pre-emptor's land he is entitled to pre-empt the entire block. One of the purposes for allowing preemption to a contiguous land holder appears to help enlarge small uneconomic agricultural holdings in the country by consolidation and amalgamation. In a case like the instant one, the different plots constituting the land transferred but forming a compact area, the pre-emptor, if successful in his pre-emption, will be in a position to enlarge his existing holding. Be that as it may, he is entitled to pre-empt the whole of the land transferred on the basis of 'contiguity' within the meaning of Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act."</u>

6. The High Court Division observing the facts and circumstances of the case and materials on record viewed that "the Court of appeal below on proper consideration of the decision of the superior Court and after adverting to the masons assigned by the trial Court, has reversed the judgment passed by the trial Court. The findings recorded by the Court of appeal below are supported by evidence on record and are based on correct principle of the appreciation of evidence. It found no illegality in the impugned judgment that calls for an interference."

7. In view of the above, the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner deserve no consideration.

8. The petition is accordingly dismissed without any order as to costs.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos. 1077 & 1206 of 2006
lawyer:
Dr. M. Zahir and Ozair Farooq, Senior Advocate, (Abdus Samad, Senior Advocate with him) instructed by Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record. ------ For the Petitioners (in C.P. No. 1077 of 2006) 
Mahbubey Alam, Senior Advocate, instructed by Chowdhury Md. Zahangir, Advocate-on-Record. ------ For the Petitioner (in C.P. No. 1206 of 2006) 
Ajmalul Hossain, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mvi. Md. Wahidullah, Advocate-on-Record ------ For Respondent No.2 (in both the cases) 
Respondent No.1 (in both the cases) ------ Not represented.
parties:
S.M. Shakil Akhtar ------ Petitioner. (in C.P. No. 1077 of 2006)
Shamsun Nahar Khan ------ Petitioner. (in C.P. No. 1206 of 2006)
VS
Rajdhani Unnayan Katripakha & another ------ Respondents. (in both the cases.)
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 11.07.2006 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition Nos. 5972 of 2003 & 575 of 2004.)
full_judgment:
M.M. Ruhul Amin J: These two petitions for leave to appeal are directed against the common judgment and order dated 11.07.2006 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Writ Petition Nos. 5972 of 2003 and 575 of 2004 discharging both the Rules with some directions and observations.

2. The case of the writ petitioner in Writ Petition No. 2301 of 1992, in short, is that the High Court Division passed an order of injunction on 28.06.1992 and the order was extended from time to time and was ultimately extended till disposal of the Rule restraining the writ respondents from leasing out the writ petitioner's plot of land to anybody. After hearing of the Writ Petition the Rule issued was made absolute and direction was given to the writ respondents to hand over possession of Plot No.9, Block No. CEN(A), Gulshan Model Town, Dhaka, (measuring 16 kathas and 7 chattaks) to the writ petitioner within two months from the date of receipt of the order of the Court but despite receipt of the certified copy of the judgment on 04.04.1999, the writ respondent contemner has in disobedience of the Court's judgment and order failed to hand over the said plot to the writ petitioner.

3. The further case of the writ petitioner is that she was allotted a plot as mentioned above by DIT now Rajuk on 06.04.1962. The DIT granted 99 years lease in favour of the writ petitioner, which was executed and registered in 1967.

4. The writ petitioner received a Memo from Rajuk on 11.12.1991 asking her to show cause as to why the said lease of the demised land should not be determined on the ground that she did not make any construction according to the approved plan within the time stipulated in the lease deed.

5. The writ petitioner's contention is that she constructed one storied building within the date as approved by Rajuk and started residing therein. Thereafter, she received another letter on 18.03.1992 informing that the lease had been determined and the Rajuk also illegally demolished the boundary walls and building in the petitioner's plot. Rajuk made advertisement for applications for lease of the writ petitioner's plot on 17.04.1992 and she filed Writ Petition No. 2301 of 1992 in June, 1992 impugning the actions of Rajuk and the Rule was issued on 28.06.1992 and interim order was passed restraining the Rajuk from leasing out the plot in question to anybody for a period of 4(four) months and subsequently the same was extended till disposal of the Rule and ultimately the Rule was made absolute by judgment and order dated 22.11.1998 directing the Rajuk to hand over the possession of the demised premises to the writ petitioner within two months from the date of receipt of the order. But inspite of communication of the order of injunction to the Rajuk, they illegally leased out the plot in question in favour of 3(three) different persons and renumbered the petitioner's demised plot from plot No. 9 to Plot No. 5 and sub-division in Plot Nos.5, 5A and 5B respectively and Plot No.5 was allotted to Mrs. Shamsur Nahar Khan by Rajuk, Plot No. 5A was allotted to Mr. S.M. Shakil Akhter by Rajuk and Plot No. 5B was allotted to Mr. Shawkat Shamim by Rajuk and granted them 99 years lease and lease deeds were executed on different dates. Therefore, the Rajuk and others committed gross contempt of the Court for violation of the judgment and order of the Court and in not implementing the judgment of the Supreme Court. The contemner respondents have tendered apology. The judgment of the High Court Division was challenged in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 384 of 2000. Thereafter another Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 154 of 2000 was filed by subsequent lessees and a review petition was also filed for reviewing the judgment dated 6th July 2000 by the Appellate Division. The review petition was also dismissed. When the respondents decided to cancel the lease in favour of subsequent lessees for implementing the judgment and order of the High Court Division, 3(three) writ petitions by subsequent lessees were filed, namely, Writ Petition Nos. 4311 of 2004, 575 of 2004 and 5972 of 2003. In all the writ petitions the writ petitioners obtained interim order. In Writ Petition No. 5972 of 2003 the writ petitioner obtained injunction order restraining the respondent No.1 from cancelling the lease of the Writ Petitioner in Plot No. 5A, Road No. 96 of Gulshan Model Town and dispossessing him from the said plot or to make any hindrance to the enjoyment by the writ-petitioner of the property.

6. In three writ petitions the case of the writ petitioners is that they are bonafide lessees under Rajuk by registered lease deed and they were inducted into possession and made construction spending huge amount of money and, therefore, cancellation of the lease is without any lawful authority. Their further case is that they were not made parties in the Writ Petition No. 2301 of 1992 and the contempt petition and they had no knowledge of the pendency of the writ petition and the judgment passed in the writ petition.

<u>7. The High Court Division after hearing held that none of the subsequent allottees have acquired any legal title in the plot which was earlier allotted in favour of the writ petitioner of Writ Petition No. 2301 of 1992. The judgment of the High Court Division as well as the Appellate Division must be implemented and any impediment created in implementing the judgment or obstruction thereto or disobedience of the judgment is a clear contempt. The High Court Division also held that the respondents in the contempt petition are already in contempt and accordingly the Rule issued in the writ petitions filed by the subsequent allottees, namely, Writ Petition Nos. 4311 of 2004, 575 of 2004 and 5972 of 2003 were discharged and the Rajuk was directed to hand over vacant possession of the Plot No.9, Block No. CEN(A) Gulshan Model Town, Dhaka in favour of the writ petitioner of Writ Petition No. 2301 of 1992 without any further excuse and to make arrangement for allotment of alternative plots in favour of the writ petitioners of Writ Petition Nos. 4311 of 2004, 575 of 2004 and 5972 of 2003.</u>

8. We have heard Dr. M. Zahir and Mr. Ozair Farooq, the learned Counsel for the petitioner in C.P. No. 1070 of 2006 and Mr. Mahbubey Alam, the learned Counsel for the petitioner in C.P. No. 1206 of 2006 and Mr. Ajmalul Hossain, the learned Counsel for respondent No.2 in both the cases and perused the judgment of the High Court Division and other connected papers.

9. It is not disputed that, Plot No.9, Block No. CEN(A), Gulshan Model Town, Dhaka was allotted to the writ petitioner of Writ Petition No. 2301 of 1992 and leased out for 99 years by a registered lease deed by Rajuk and she constructed one storied building and was residing therein. Rajuk subsequently cancelled the allotment and demolished the building and the plot was renumbered as Plot No.5 and sub-divided into Plot Nos.5, 5A and 5B and allotted to the writ petitioners of Writ Petition Nos. 4311 of 2004, 575 of 2004 and 5972 of 2003.

10. In the background of the above facts, Writ Petition No. 2301 of 1992 was filed and Rule was made absolute as noticed earlier with some directions to the Rajuk. The Rajuk did not take any positive step for restoration of the lease granted earlier in favour of the writ petitioner of Writ Petition No. 2301 of 1992.

11. The subsequent allottees filed three Writ Petition Nos. 4311 of 2004, 575 of 2004 and 5972 of 2003 on the grounds stated in the writ petition as discussed above. The High Court Division on consideration of the materials on record held that inspite of the fact that the sub-sequent allottees lost both in the High Court Division and in the Appellate Division, the Rajuk did not take any step for restoration of the lease granted earlier in favour of writ petitioner of W.P. No. 2301 of 1992. So, she filed a contempt petition against Rajuk and others. In respect the writ petitioners of Writ Petition Nos. 4311 of 2004, 575 of 2004 and 5972 of 2003 filed by the subsequent allottees, the finding of the High Court Division is that they did not acquire any valid title by taking lease of Plot No.9 subsequently renumbered as Plot Nos.5, 5A and 5B of Block No. CEN(A), Gulshan Model Town, Dhaka.

12. In our view since plot No.9, Block No. CEN(A), Gulshan Model Town, Dhaka was earlier allotted in favour of writ petitioner of writ petition No. 2301 of 1992 and the lease deed for 99 years was executed and registered on 15.11.1967 and possession was delivered to her and she constructed pucca building and was residing therein. Subsequent cancellation of the same and demolition of her building and granting of lease of the same plot by sub-dividing into Plot Nos.5, 5A and 5B are patently illegal and an act of high handedness on the part of Rajuk.

13. Therefore, in our view, the High Court Division took into consideration all aspects of the matter and came to a correct decision. There is no cogent reason to interfere with the same. The direction to the Rajuk given by the High Court Division as regard the writ petitioners in Writ Petition Nos. 5972 of 2003, 575 and 4311 of 2004 in our view is quite sufficient in respect of the grievance of the said writ petitioners.

14. Both the leave petitions are dismissed.

End.

case_source: (From the Judgment and Order dated March 14, 2004 passed by the High Court Division in Second Appeal Nos. 463 of 1973 and 109 of 1974)
full_judgment:
Md. Ruhul Amin J: These two petitions for leave to appeal have been filed against the common judgment dated March 14, 2004 of a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Second Appeal Nos. 463 of 1973 and 109 of 1974 dismissing the same. The aforesaid Second Appeals were filed against the judgment and decree dated August 3, 1972 of the Court of Additional District Judge, Sylhet in Title Appeal Nos. 159 and 160 of 1969 allowing the same upon reversing the judgment and decree dated January 31, 1969 of the 1st Court of Additional Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) Sylhet in Title Suit Nos. 5 and 6 of 1968 so far the same relates to the plot Nos.9, 10 and 4.

2. The trial Court by the aforesaid judgment and decree decreed the Title Suit Nos. 4, 5 and another Title Suit being No. 6 of 1968. The trial Court declared the title of the plaintiffs of the aforementioned suits and also passed a decree for recovery of khas possession of the land of the plot numbers as regard which the suits were filed upon evicting the contesting defendants.

<u>3. It appears before the trial Court a solehnama was filed by some defendants. The Court while decreeing the suits made the said compromise petition part of the decree.</u>

4. As against the judgment and decree of the trial Court in Suit Nos.5 and 6 of 1968 so far the decrees therein related to plot Nos. 9, 10 and 4 two appeals i.e. Title Appeal Nos. 159 and 160 of 1969 were filed.

<u>5. The suit was filed seeking declaration of title and for recovery of khas possession as well as mesne profit and also for rectification of Khatian Nos. 331, 330, 120, 314, 329, 313/12, 325 and 332.</u>

6. The suit was filed stating, inter alia, that the land in suit originally appertained to Elam Patta No.12 and now is of patta No.1, that the land at the time of settlement in 1923-24 was Patit land, that proforma defendant Nos. 14 and 15 acquired 4 annas interest by inheritance and by purchase, that predecessor of defendant Nos. 7-11 owned 10 gondas land of the aforementioned patta, that the land of the patta was put to auction and was purchased by Nim Chand Kartik (Kakuria) in the Execution Case No. 237 of 1943 (money execution case), that defendant No. 14 purchased the land sold in the aforementioned Execution case in the benami of Nim Chand Kakuria and that in fact defendant No.14 acquired title to the land and remained in possession, that neither Nim Chand Kakuria nor his heirs claimed the land, that because of the auction sale defendant Nos. 4-11 have no title in the said land, that the land of previous plots at the time of subsequent survey was listed in Plot No. 313 and later on in plot No. 720, that the land of these plots were owned by the villagers of village Amua, Palpur and Mirpur, that there was an amicable partition in 1315 B.S. and thereby land of plot No. 313 fell in the share of villagers of village Amua and Palpur, that in 1359 B.S. there was another partition and Chitta saham was prepared and thereupon land of plot No. 313 fell in the share of proforma-defendant Nos. 14 and 15 and the said defendants wanted to cultivate the land of the said plots in 1362 B.S. but the other defendants forcibly entered upon the land of plot Nos.9 and 10 and kept the land of the said plots illegally in their possession and growing paddy, that plaintiffs purchased the land of the said plots along with other land by the kabala dated 21st Bhadra, 1370 B.S. and they are being prevented by the defendants from entering into the land.

<u>7. The defendant Nos. 7-11 contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material averments made in the plaint and stating, inter alia, that the suits are barred by limitation, that the description of the land is vague, that 10 gondas of the land of patta in question belonged to their predecessor Mujaffar and he also purchased 10 gondas land of the, said patta from Hemlata Dam, wife of Bipin Behari Dam who was brother of Kunja Behari Dam, that defendants' predecessor Mujaffar acquired 1 anna share in the land of the patta and that their predecessor's interest was never sold in auction and that if any papers relating to auction are produced the same are not genuine and that Benode Behari never purchased the land of their predecessor nor possessed the same, that the defendants are in possession of the land which their predecessor acquired, that plaintiffs or their predecessor at no point of time possessed the land in suit and as such the suit is liable to be dismissed. It may be mentioned other defendants compromise the suit with the plaintiffs.</u>

8. The trial Court decreed the suit on the finding that the plaintiffs have acquired right, title and interest in the land of the respective suits by purchase by Ext. 1, that the Title Suit Nos. 5 and 6 of 1968 are not barred by limitation and as such the same are maintainable, that the relief sought in Title Suit No. 6 of 1968 by the plaintiffs is also available to them. The trial Court while decreeing the suits did not allow the plaintiffs' prayer for rectification of the record of right.

<u>9. The contesting defendants went on appeal. The appellate Court upon due discussion of the materials on record reversed the judgment and decree of the trial Court passed in Title Suit Nos. 5 and 6 of 1968 so far the same relates to plot Nos. 9, 10 and 4 and thereupon dismissed the said suits on the finding that the plaintiffs could not prove claim of possession of his predecessor in plot Nos. 9, 10 and 4 within 12 years from the date of filing of the suit and that the defendants have been able to prove that they are in possession of the said 3 plots since the time of their predecessor that the Title Suit Nos. 5 and 6 of 1968 are barred by limitation so far the same relates to plot Nos. 9, 10 and 4.</u>

10. The plaintiff Abdus Sattar Khan's heirs filed appeals before the High Court Division. The High Court Division dismissed the appeals on the finding that plaintiff did not produce sufficient evidence to prove his case i.e. plaintiff's predecessor-in-interest Benode Behari purchased the land in auction in the Benami of Nim Chand Kakuria, that Ext.8 clearly shows that the land was purchased in auction by Nim Chand Kakuria and EXt.1 shows that Nim Chand Kakuria was a decree holder. The plaintiff failed to establish that Benode Behari purchased the share of Mujaffar, predecessor of the defendant Nos. 7-11, that Ext. C series (rent receipts) show that Mujaffar paid rent in respect of his share up to 1358 B.S. and the said fact totally disproved the case of the plaintiff that Benode Behari purchased the share of Mujaffar in the Benami of Nim Chand Kakuria, that by the materials on record particularly Ext.9 and Ext. C series, the claim of the defendant as to possession of the land in suit has been established, that the defendants, both by oral and documentary evidence, have proved their possession of the land which their predecessor Mujaffar owned and possessed and that the defendants are possessing the land for more than 12 years. The defendants have proved that they are possessing the interest of Hemlota for more than 12 years, that defendants by their possession of the, interest of Hemlota for more than 12 years perfected their title as regard the land owned by Hemlota, that signatures of Kunja and Bipin appearing in Exts. 6 and 6(a) are different from the signature appearing in Ext. A of Title Suit No. 5 of 1968 and in the state of the matter plaintiff has not taken any step to ascertain the genuineness of the signature appearing in the said exhibits, that plaintiffs' witnesses have not proved the possession of the plaintiff in the land of plot Nos. 9, 10 and 4.

<u>11. We have heard the learned Advocate and perused the materials on record. It is seen from the judgment of the lower appellate Court that the said Court on due consideration of the evidence arrived at the finding that the plaintiffs suit Nos. 5 and 6 of 1968 was barred by limitation, since they failed to prove their possession in respect of the land of plot Nos. 9, 10 and 4. The High Court Division also in the background of the materials on record arrived at the finding that plaintiff failed to prove that Benode Behari purchased the interest of defendant Nos. 7-11's predecessor Mujaffar in auction sale in the benami of Nim Chand Kakuria. The plaintiff having had failed to establish the said case we are of the view that the plaintiffs claim so far the land owned by Mujaffar i.e. predecessor of the defendant Nos. 7-11 was not established. The plaintiff could also not proved his possession in the land of plot Nos. 9, 10 and 4 and also could not prove his claim so far the same relates to the land owned by Hemlota.</u>

12. In that state of the matter we are of the view that the High Court Division committed no error of law or procedure in dismissing the appeals.

13. Accordingly the petitions are dismissed.

End.

lawyer:
MA Wadud Bhuiyan with Syed Golam Mustafa, Advocates—For the Petitioners.

parties:
M Sayeedur Rahman Al-Mahbubi and another ------ Petitioners
vs
Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakkha & anr ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Emdadul Huq J: In the application under Article 102 of the Constitution the petitioners have challenged a notice dated 22-8-94 (Annexure-A) issued under the signature of respondent No. 2, Magistrate 1st Class, RAJUK directing petitioner No. 1 to vacate 27 decimals of land (approximately) and to remove the structures thereon. In that notice the said 27 decimals of land has been identified as CS plot Nos. 795 (part) and 777 (part) of Mouja Brahmanchiron under PS Motijheel District Dhaka and the description of the adjacent boundaries on the four sides have been also stated.

2. In the writ petition and a supplementary affidavit, the petitioners claim that petitioner No.2 is the owner of the disputed land and the structures thereon which are being used as a religious institution called Dewan Bag Sharif and petitioner No. 1 is the Secretary General of the institution. Petitioner No. 2 acquired 28 khatas or 40 decimals of land in SA plot No. 622 of the aforesaid mouja by virtue of seven registered transfer deeds (Annexure-D to D-6) executed by the respective owners including one Md Jalaluddin at different dates within the period from 27-1-1987 to 12-4-1999. After acquisition of the land petitioner No. 2 developed it by earth filling, constructed mosque and other structures thereon and have been in possession of the property and using it for religious purposes. In respect of the land transferred by the six out of the said seven deeds, petitioner No.2 got his name recorded in the mutation khatian and paid rent (Annexure D-7). The mutation in respect o the land purchased by the other deed is under process. Previously the land of SA plot No. 622 was part of the CS plot No. 777/795 measuring 2.30 acres out of which 75.50 decimals was acquired by the Government and the un-acquired part was duly recorded in different holdings of SA khatian No. 345/2 and the land of plot No.622 remained non-acquired. In 1993, the said Md Jalaluddin, one of the transferors of petitioner No. 2, applied to the ADC (Rev) Dhaka for demarcation of his portion of land in plot No. 622. So Demarcation Case No. 9 of 1993 was initiated, survey was conducted and the revenue authority found Jalaluddin in possession of plot No. 622 (Annexure -11). But at the instance of some vested interest group RAJUK issued a notice dated 11-12-2003 directing the petitioners to vacate the land and the structures of the Darbar Sharif. So, the petitioner filed Writ Petition No. 7453 of 2003 and obtained a Rule and a stay order. After contested hearing the Rule was made absolute by a Division Bench of this Court in terms of the judgment dated 22-8-2004 (Annexure-C). But sensing their defeat in the said writ petition the respondents signed the impugned notice on 21-8-2004, kept it ready and on 22-8-04 issued the same just after the delivery of the said judgment only to fruatrate the decision of this Court. The petitioners claim that before issuance of the impugned notice, no show cause notice was served upon them and that such notice is a malice in law and infringes their fundamental right guaranteed under Article 42 of the Constitution to enjoy their property.

3. Respondent No. 1 the Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakkha represented by its Chairman, has filed an affidavit-in-opposition denying the material allegations of the petitioners with regard to the acquisition of this plot and possession over the disputed land. The respondent claims that the land of SA plot No.622 corresponds to CS plot No.795 and 777 and out of these two plots 1.295 acres was acquired in LA Case No.1/85-86 and possession thereof was transferred by the Government to RAJUK on 7-7-96 (Annexure-111). Petitioner No.1 submitted an application (Armexure-11) seeking RAJUK permission to construct temporary tin shed on the disputed land for the devotees. But RAJUK refused the permission and wrote a letter to Motijheel Police Station to record this information as a general diary (Annexure-1) stating therein that the illegal structures raised by the petitioner on that land were liable to be evicted. The fact of unlawful possession of the petitioners has been admitted in their aforesaid application (Annexure-11). So, previously they were issued with a notice to vacate that land, but without proper specification of the land. The petitioners challenged this notice in Writ Petition No.7453 of 2003 and this Court decided the case against RAJUK on the ground of improper description of the land. In view of such decision, the land has been properly described in the impugned notice (Annexure-A) with a direction to the petitioners to vacate the land unlawfully possessed and evict the structures erected therein by them.

4. In a reply to the affidavit-in-opposition the petitioners have stated that the RAJUK land on which petitioners earlier created temporary structures is not relatable to SA plot No. 622, that they have already removed the tin shed from the said land which is different from the 27 decimals of land of the said SA plot No. 622 claimed by the petitioners. They further claim that in the judgment dated 22-8-04 delivered in Writ Petition No.7453 of 2003, this Court has apart from the issue of improper description of the land also decided all other relevant issues.

5. Mr Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan with Mr Syeed Golam Mustafa appearing for the petitioners advanced law of two-fold arguments as follows:

6. Firstly, the land described in the impugned notice (Annexure-A) is not identifiable as it contains reference only to CS plot No.795(Part) and 777(Part) but not to any corresponding to SA plot No. or to any RS plot No and that till now no inquiry has been made in order to determine whether the petitioners are unauthorised occupants of the land in question.

7. Secondly, the memo of the impugned notice is dated 22-8-2004 but the signature of respondent No.2 at the bottom of the notice is dated 21-8-2004. This manner of signing the notice and issuance thereof clearly indicates the purpose of circumventing the decision of this Court delivered in Writ Petition No.7453 of 2003 on 22-8-2004 in which a similar notice was challenged and the same issues were decided. Therefore, the subsequent notice which is similar in nature and has been impugned in this writ petition is malafide and the action of the respondents purporting to evict the petitioners from their lawful possession is malice in law in view of the principle laid down in the case of Dr Nurul Islam vs Bangladesh reported in 33 DLR (AD) 201.

8. On the other hand, Mr AMM Mazed Chowdhury the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No. 1, draws our attention to Annexure-111 by which the possession of the disputed land was handed over by the Government functionaries to RAJUK in consequence of acquisition of the land along with other land in LA Case No.1/85-86. Mr M Chowdhury submits that in the impugned notice (Annexure-A) the disputed land measuring 27 decimals has been sufficiently described with reference to the adjacent boundaries and also to the CS plot nos. as mentioned in the document of delivery of possession. He continues that the said land has further been identified in the acquisition map. Annexure-IV and that all these actions were taken to comply with the decision of this Court delivered on 22-8-2004 in Writ Petition No. 7453 of 2003 and therefore no question of malics in law arises.

9. We have gone through all the annexures to the writ petition, affidavit-in-opposition and reply to the affidavit-in-opposition. It appears that Writ Petition No. 7453 of 2003 was between the same parties and the issue was fundamentally the same, namely, the eviction of the petitioners from the same land, though the notices impugned in that case and in the present case are admittedly different. From Annexure-11, a letter dated 30-4-2003 sent by petitioner No.2 addressed to RAJUK, it appears that, in anticipation of RAJUK's permission sought by the petitioners by an earlier application dated 25-1-03 they admittedly constructed some tin shed structures for a religious conference on the RAJUK land adjacent to the land stated by them as Bab-e-Madina at Kamalapur. They continued to keep those structures on the RAJUK land and then again sent to RAJUK by the said letter dated 30-4-2003 (Annexure-11) seeking permission for some more time with an undertaking to remove the structures after the Eid-e-Miladunnabi Conference was over. But RAJUK did not accord permission (Annexure-1). Petitioners claim that, they have already removed the said structures and that the impugned notice for eviction of the petitioners from the land in question is unwarranted, as they have acquired it by registered instruments.

10. The difference between the parties with regard to description of the disputed land is noticeable. According to the petitioners, SA plot No. 622 was previously part of a single CS plot being No.777/795. But respondents claim that the said SA plot originated from two CS plots namely 777 and 795, parts of which have been acquired in an LA Case. But the respondents have not ascertained which portion of the said CS plot was acquired and whether possession thereof was taken in due process of law.

<u>11. The question as to whether SA plot No.622 was part of CS plot No. 777/795, as claimed by petitioners or the said SA plot originated from two CS plots, as claimed by the respondent, that cannot be decided in writ jurisdiction. Similarly, petitioners' claim of title to the said SA plot No. 622, on the basis of annexure-D series also cannot be decided in writ Jurisdiction.</u>

<u>12. Keeping aside the aforementioned disputed question of fact with regard to identity of land the petitioners claim of title to the disputed land, the issue before us in the present case, as was in the writ petition No.7453 of 2004. is, whether the petitioners are unauthorised occupants of the disputed land for the purpose of eviction of the petitioners in terms of the impugned notice. In order to decide this issue, the respondents have to ascertain that the portion of the land allegedly occupied by petitioners in SA plot No.622 was requisitioned and acquisitioned in the said LA case and that possession was taken over in due course.</u>

13. The certified copy of the judgment (Annexure-C) of that case, in which one of us was a signatory, the following findings and observations were made:

"It appears that the impugned notice Annexure-A issued by the respondent No.2 contained no memo number, no date and to schedule of land without having adequate description and identity of the land in question and that it was addressed to the petitioner No.1 of 147, Arambag Dhaka who is not the owner of property and that there is no essential particulars of the acquired properties. No papers showing requisition and acquisition of the land SA plot No.622 have been annexed to the affidavit-in-opposition and, as such, it has been issued without any application of mind and it is vague, indefinite without specifying the essential particulars of the subject matter of the notice which is in violation of fundamental right of the petitioner under Article 42 of the Constitution and that prior to the impugned notice (Annexure-A to the writ petition) no show cause notice was issued to the petitioner."

<u>14. The parties to, and the subject matter of the Writ Petition No.7453 of 2003 and the present case being the same we stick to the same principles as quoted above. For eviction of an allegedly unauthorised occupant claiming title to the land, RAJUK must satisfy the court firstly, that the land of the petitioners was acquired and possession thereof was transferred to RAJUK in the said LA Case and secondly, the land in question is perfectly within the acquired land for which compensation has been paid or offered to the owners.</u>

<u>15. Judging by the aforesaid criteria and the previous decision, it appears that, the boundaries given in the notice impugned in the present case do not signify that the land in question is requisitioned and acquisitioned land, and that in view of the previous judgment the impugned notice is malafide, and therefore, it cannot be sustained.</u>

<u>16. Annexure-III shows that the Dhaka District Revenue Authorities made over possession of 5 decimals of plot No.777 of 75.50 decimals of plot No.795 along with other lands to RAJUK. But this document does not contain any information to show that the petitioners' purchased land-comprising SA plot No.622 was taken over. Moreover, in the impugned notice the land under eviction has been described as CS plot No. 795 (Part) and 777(Part) and the quantum of land for the purpose of eviction is shown as more or less 27 decimals, without reference to quantum in full of the said two CS plots.</u>

<u>17. The notice does not contain any reference to any SA plot. The notice of course gives a description of the contiguous boundary location/structures, and, in this regard, the learned Advocate for the respondent No.1, with reference to Annexure-IV, submits that this boundary description is based on the said map prepared by RAJUK.</u>

<u>18. Clearly the land described in the notice is not identifiable. because firstly, it does not state which part of the CS plot or the corresponding SA and RS plot is the subject matter of eviction and secondly, the acquisition authority namely, District Land Revenue Office Dhaka did not specify such part in their document of delivery of possession (Annexure-111) Again, it is not clear whether the map (Annexure-IV) was prepared by RAJUK on the basis of any map prepared by the concerned land acquiring authority, and apparently, they have not even endorsed it.</u>

19. In the facts and circumstance stated above, we are of the view that reference to the CS plot Nos. and the simple description of boundary are not enough for the purpose of eviction of the petitioners, who claim to have acquired titles in SA plot No.622 by virtue of several deeds and who are admittedly, in possession of the disputed land. Accordingly, we hold that the impugned notice was issued without lawful authority.

20. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The impugned notice under memo No. নিঃপ্রঃ/দঃঢাঃ/রাজউক/৪৪৫(৩)খ, dated 22-8-2004 issued under the signature of respondent No.2 is declared to be without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

No order as to cost.

End.

lawyer:
Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, Senior Advocate instructed by Mrs. Sufia Khatun, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioners

case_source: (From the Judgment and order dated the 2nd day of August, 2009 passed by the high Court Division in Writ Petition No. 3418 of 2008)
full_judgment:
Mohammad Fazlul Karim J.:- This Petition for Leave to Appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated the 2nd day of August, 2009 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 3418 of 2008 discharging the Rule. 

2. The facts involved in the case, in short, arc that the property in C.S. Plot No. 65 is a Debuted property created by Roy Bahadur Karuna Das Bose by a registered deed of Arapaima dated 01.05.1914 wherein the ancestors of the petitioner have given details regarding the management of the property in deity by Managing Shebayet. After transfer of C. S. Plot No. 65 to the deity Sree Sree Laxmi Narayan, the heirs of Roy Bahadur Karuna Das Bose have been managing the property of the deity as Shebayets and scheme for the proper management of the property was declared by decree passed by Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 56 of 1944 and since then the said property is being run by the Shcbayets. The C. S. record was rightly prepared and published in the name of Roy Bahadur Karuna Das Bose on behalf of the deity Sree Sree Laxmi Narayan Jew. The Managing Shebayet started possessing the land of C. S. Plot Nos. 94 and 95 by erecting some sheds and kuccha rooms upon case plot No. 65 and letting out the same. Thereafter, the Managing Shebayet 1anendra Nath Bose went to India permanently and according to the terms of Arapaima the father of the petitioner suit Kumar Bose was appointed Managing Shebayet on behalf of Bigraha and he was looking after the said Debutter property properly while the said Mamnoor Rashid was monthly tenant under the said Debutter properly he transferred his land in C.S. plot Nos. 94 and 95 in 1963 to one Faikuzzaman and handed over the possession. Thereafter the said Mamnoot. Rashid handed over the possession of case land i.e. C. S. plot No. 65 to the Managing Shebayet. Thereafter in 1964 the said Faikuzzaman intended to take on rent the same as monthly tenant and the Managing 'Shebayet let out said Debutter property to him as monthly tenant and he has been paying rent to the Managing Shebayet of the said Debutter property. The tenant Faikuzzaman died in 1978 and the respondent No. 7 Teazle Blahi Sharfuzzaman started possessing the case land as monthly tenant under the petitioner and started paying rent at the rate of TK. 2000.00 per month to the petitioner as accepting him as Managing Shebayet of the said Debutter property and in 1985 the monthly rent was increased from TK. 2000.00 to 5000.00 for the cause of increasing the cost of maintenance, of the Bigraha but on request the petitioner's rent was being realizing at the rate of TK. 2000.00 per month till 2005 and from 2005 respondent No. 7 did not pay any rent. The respondent No. 7 assured to pay the unpaid rent but did not pay and trying to grab the property of the petitioner. The respondent No. 7 has no right and title in the case land i.e. in C. S. Plot No. 65 but in 2007 he started construction in C. S. Plot No. 65 and on 08.08.2007 the petitioner requested the respondent No. 7 to stop the illegal construction in the case plot No. 65 and to vacate the case land; The respondent No. 7 denied the title of the petitioner and disclosed that RAJUK approved the plan for construction of multistoried commercial cum-residential building came to know from RAJUK that the respondent No. 7 along with other 8 persons obtained approval of plan and clearance from RAJUK for construction of high rise building by submitting deed of other plots and then the petitioner as Managing Shebayet of the said Debutter property requested the local respectable persons to stop the illegal construction of the respondent No. 7 in the land of the said Rebutter property and the local people requested to stop the construction in the case land but the respondent No.7 did not stop the construction in the case land as yet. The respondent No. 7 and his brothers have no right, title and possession in C. S. Plot Nos. 94 and 95. The superior predecessor of Bhuban Mohan Ghose purchased the land measuring 1.05 acres of land by a sale deed being No. 22615 dated 04.07.1928 from one Elahi Box Driver and the said vendor Bhuban Mohan (Those as plaintiff filed a suit being Title Suit No. 1537 of 1929 against the vendor Elahi Box Driver and 3 others in the 3rd Court of Munsif, Dhaka praying for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession of the suit land the plaintiffs case was that the defendants sold to him on 19th Ashar, 1335 13.S. C. S. Plot No. 94 and part of plot No. 95 and showed him the land in the locality plaintiff got the western portion of the C. S. Plot No. 94 in his possession but the defendants did not deliver possession in the western portion of the said plot and dispossessed the plaintiff' from the plot No. 94. 

3. The respondent No. 7 contested the Rule submitted affidavit-in-opposition denying the material statement contending, inter-alia, that the land measuring 1.11 acres in plot No. 65 appertaining to C. S. Khatian No. 6947 of mouza Shahar Dhaka under Police Station Kotwali belonged to Karuna Das Bahadur transferred 8 bighas of land including C. S. Plot No. 65 to one Sheikh Shefatullah. Sheikh Shefatullah transferred the same in Elahi Box Driver by dint of registered sale deed on 3rd Magh, 1326 13. S. Elahi Box Driver owned and possessed that land and subsequently on 04.07.1928 transferred 3(three) pakhis of land with specific boundary of Bhuban Mohan Ghose vide registered deed No. 2615. Bhuban Mohan Ghose as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 1537 of 1929 against Elahi Box and others in the 3rd Court of Munsif, Dhaka 'for declaration of title and recovery of 'Kha' possession far it relates to C. S. Plot No. 94. In that suit Elahi Box filed written statement contesting the suit land eventually the suit was dismissed by the trial Court on 23.03.1931 but the findings of possession was in favour of the plaintiff as regards to C. S. Plot No. 65. 

4. Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, learned Counsel, appearing for the petitioners submitted that the C.S. Plot No. 65 is the debuttor property and the said property by Karuna Das Bose by a registered arpannama dated 01.05.1914 in favour of Sree Sree Laxmi Narayan Jew Tagore and the C.S. Khatian No. 6947 was rightly prepared in the name of the said Sree Sree Laxmi Narayan Jew Tagore being represented by Shebayet Karuna Das Bose Bahadur and the writ-respondent No.7's predecessors are the monthly tenants under Shebayet of the said debtor property and the scheme of the proper management of the debuttor property was declared by judgment and decree passed by Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 56 of 1944 and since then the said debuttor property is being run by the Shebayets and the said debuttor property has never by transferred; that the C. S. Plot No. 65 is the debuttor property and the respondent Rajuk has illegally approved the plan in favour of the writ-respondent No. 7 for construction of 20 storied building in C. S.. Plot No. 65 which is debuttor property and writ-respondent No. 7 obtained some certificates from various departments only mentioning 37/2 Purana Paum and with respect to C.S. Plot No. 65 but writ-respondent: No. 7 obtained plan from RAJUK to construct 16 storied building in C.S. Plot No. 94 and 95(part) and 65 by suppression of facts and when he started construction in C. S. Plot No. 65 then it was brought to the knowledge of RAJUK and RAJUK issued a notice upon the writ-respondent No. 7 to show cause as to whey the approved plan should not be cancelled and stopped the construction work and the writ-respondent No. 7 challenging the said notice filed writ petition No. 6875 of 20078 and in the said writ petition the High Court Division found that the C. S. Plot No. 65 is the debuttor property and finally discharged the Rule but thereafter, RAJUK illegally allowed writ-respondent No. 7 to make construction on C. S. Plot No. 65 which is a debuttor property. The learned Counsel further submitted that the predecessors of writ-respondent - No. 7 and also respondent No. 7 were the monthly ten-ants under Shebayet of the said debtor property and respondent No.7 and his brothers in collusion with the dishonest employees of settlement department got S.A. record in their name but in respect of C.S. Plot No. 65 they have no deed by which they ban claim the title of the said plot and in the absence of deed in respect of C. S. Plot No. 65 RA.JUK can not allow respondent No. 7 to make construction on the said plot; that the subject matter of the writ petition and Title Suit No. 1633 of 2008 are not the same or similar as because Title Suit No. 1633 of 2008 filed by the petitioner as plaintiff for of title and recovery of khas possession and the writ petition was filed challenging the action of RAJUK whereby RAJUK approved the plan in favour of respondent No. 7 and his 'brother to construct 16 storied corn-metrical-cum-residential building in C. S. Plot No. 65 which is debuttor property. The learned Counsel also submitted that there is not on record to show that the beet land is the land of. Annexure- A or Anncxure-K unless a relayment is made and report is obtained showing the land of C. S. Plot No.65 is identical with land of schedule 3 of the Annexure-A and Annexure-K it is difficult on the part of the Court sitting in writ jurisdiction to hold that the land of Plot No. 65 of mouza Shahar .Dhaka attracts the lands of schedule 'C' of Annexure-A. It appears that according to C. S. Plot No. 65 is a debuttor property to which writ-respondent No. 7 did not claim as title by any title deed and hence further enquiry as opined by the High Court Division is unnecessary for the purpose of considering the legality of the actions of RAJUK and therefore, the judgment of the High Court Division is not sustainable in law. 

5. It appears that there is no mention of plot number either in Annxure-A or in Annexurc-K. There is no other document available on record to show that the property as described in schedule of the Annexure-A and Annexure-K to the writ petition and supplementary affidavit filed by the petitioner are identical with the land of C.S. Plot No. 65 mouza Shahar Dhaka. It further appears that the plot No. 65 has been recorded as 'beel'. There is nothing on record to show that the said been land is the land of Annexurc-A or Annexurc-K. Unless a relayment is made and a report is obtained showing the land of C.S. Plot No. 65 is identical with the land of schedule-3 of the Annexure-A and schedule-5 of the Annexure-K it is difficult on the part of this Court, sitting in writ jurisdiction to hold that the land of plot No. 65 of inouza Shahar Dhaka attracts the lands of schedule-C of Annexure-A and Annexure-K. Whether or not the said plot No. 65 is identical with Annexure-K and Annexure-A is a question of fact and it could be resolved in a regular title suit by making repayment by an Advocate Commissioner and other support evidence on record and the same could not be the subject matter of writ petition. Admittedly the petitioners being out of possession has instituted the suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession. It appears that S.A. record, R.S. record and mutated Khatian stood prepared in the name of the represented No. 7 and others and their predecessors. Admittedly the respondents are in possession by paying rent and taxes since 1965, it is difficult to hold that the approval made by the respondent Nos. 3 and 5 were without having any law authority. 

6. In view of the above, we find no substance in the submissions of the learned Counsel for the petitioner. 

7. Accordingly, the petition is dismissed. 

End.
