Mr. Sharif Uddin Chaklader, :  - This rule by the defendants, directed against judgment and decree dated 26.2.2007 passed by the learned District Judge, Jhenaidah in Title Appeal No.41 of 2004 decreeing Title Suit No.107 of 2002 for easement right of pathway on setting aside the judgment and decree dated 24.4.2004 passed by the learned' Senior Assistant Judge Shailakupa, Jhinaidaha. 

2. At the out set it is mentioned that it is now become fashion for some lawyers not to attend the Court after obtaining rule and order of stay. Although this matter appeared regularly for hearing in: the cause list with the names of the learned Advocate but I find learned Advocate for the petitioners always absent Which is a misconduct as when an advocate received and filed vokalatnama he is duty bound to appear and defend the case of his litigant client.

 3. It is the case of the plaintiff that .011/4 acres of land of plot No.1409 appertaining to C.S. khatian No.742 corresponding to S.A. khatian No.1203 of Mouza No.137, Bhagaban Nagar within Police Station Sailakupa Jhenaidah was recorded in the name of Rehan Uddin Mandal in Khatian No.1203 Rehan Uddin Mandal died leaving sons and wife, defendant Nos.1-5. There is a path way on the land of plot No.1406 which the plaintiffs using for coming and going; there is another path way in plot No.2915 but plot No.1407 and 1410 are contiguous to Suit Plot No.1409 and road of plot No.1410 and 1407 is linked by the road of plot No.2915. Plaintiffs have used the said road for 33 years. Plaintiff No.1 along with the members of her family resides in some portion of land south to plot No.1410 and in whole part of plot No.1407 for 33 years by erecting homestead therein. 

4. Plaintiff Nos.2-16 have been using the alleged path for long 33 years and they have no, way to go to the southern side other than the path of suit plot No.1409 and also they have no way to go to the land of plot No.1411, 1416 and 1417 excepting this way for the residence and passersby of the locality and this road is only way for coming from plot No.1406 to the road of plot No.1915. Plaintiffs have acquired easement right as they have used the road for 33 years and as such they are entitled to use the suit portion of the road which has fallen to the land of suit plot No.1409. Defendants committed illegality in interfering with their easement right by digging earth and planted banana trees. Defendants threatened the plaintiffs for blocking the road on 19.7.2002, hence the suit. 

5. Defendant's cases are that Al acres of land of suit plot No.1409 appertaining to S.A khatian No.959 of Mouza No.137, Bhagaban Nagar belonged to Rehannuddin Mondal. Rehannuddin Mondal alienated .41 acres of land of plot No.1409 to defendant Nos.3 and 4 by registered kobla dated 17.9.1987, 2.2.1987 and to defendant No.5 by registered kobla dated 29.7.1987. R.S. record has been prepared in their names correctly. Defendants have homestead and different kinds of fruit bearing trees. There is a road in a portion of the suit plot, the non -suited plot Nos.1407-1408 is contiguous west to the suit plot No.1409. The land of plot No.I407 is contiguous north to non -suited plot No.1408 and the land of plot No.1410 is contiguous north to plot No.1407. The land of plot No.141 i is contiguous east to plot No 1410 and the land of plot No.1416 and 1417 is contiguous north to plot No.1411. There was no house of plaintiff No.1 in the land of plot Nos.1407 and 1410. Plaintiff No.1 acquired a bit title in the land of plot No.1410 and 1407 but with a view to grab some portion of the land of the road of plot No.1406 she commenced erecting house on the month of Falgun, 1408 B.S to the eastern side of plot No.1410 and 1407 and erected one kitchen, one tin shed house having two rooms, one latrine and one tube well in the land of road of plot No.1406. There was no road in the land of plot No.1409 and at present no road has gone through the suit plot.

6. Learned Judge although found by depositions of P.W.s 1 to 4 they have clearly stated that there was a road on the suit land which have 'been used by the plaintiffs for 33 years to which every witness corroborated the same but defendants did not give any suggestion to these witnesses to the effect there was no road on the suit but dismissed the suit as on some portion of the road homestead standing on the road and no prayer in the suit having been made for removing the constructing on the road the suit is barred under the provisions of Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act.

 7. Appellate Court reversed the findings on consideration of exhibits 1 series, 2, by and Kha, all these documents filed 133 the plaintiffs and defendants and in' C.S. and S.A. Khatian, there is mentioned of a road and defendant No.4 also admitted there is a road and plaintiffs has no other road. On consideration of this fact, learned District Judge, Jhinaidaha reversed the findings of the trial Court. 

8. I have already mentioned that learned Advocate for the petitioners did not appear in Court at any time. Mr. S. N. Goswami learned Advocate appearing for the opposite parties submits that trial Court without discussing the exhibits on record held that there is homestead on the road and in getting a decree for easement right plaintiffs ought to pray for removing of those construction, which is wrong finding. Learned Advocate further submits on reference to the judgment that plaintiffs in their dispositions stated that they have used the road for the last 33 years which the defendants did not denied. Learned Advocate further submits that learned Judge on reference to the khatian and exhibits filed by both the parties found that there is a road mentioned in the khatian and these finding with . reference to the exhibits on record is binding upon this Court in its revisional jurisdiction. 
9. I have considered the submissions of the learned Advocate for the opposite parties and judgments of the Courts below and exhibits. It appears that trial Court without discussing any exhibits filed by the parties, only on oral evidence of PW2 held that there are construction on the pathway. Learned Judge of the Appellate Court found that P.W.1 to PW.4 have clearly stated in their evidences that there was a road on the land of the suit plot which have been used by the plaintiffs for 33 years. P.W.1 to P.W.4 have given their corroborative testimonies in respect of the path way on the suit plot but no suggestion was suggested to these witnesses to the effect that there was no road on the suit plot. I also find from the exhibits filed by the parties i.e. khatians that there is a road on the suit plot as such I hold learned Judge of Appellate Court committed no illegality in allowing the appeal and decreeing the suit. 

10.1 find no substance in the rule. 

11. In the result this rule is discharge. No costs. 

12. Send down the lower Court records at once. 

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. Faruque Ahmed, J: This rule at the instance of the plaintiff petitioners was issued calling upon the -opposite parties No.1-3 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 25.05.2006 passed by the learned Divisional Special Judge and District Judge, Barisal, .in Title Appeal No.04 of 2005 remanding back the suit reversing the judgment and decree dated 10.04.2004 passed in Title Suit No:37 of 1997 should not be set aside and  or' pass such other or 'further order' or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Short facts of the case are as follows:- 

(a)The Petitioners as plaintiffs on 18.05.1992 instituted suit for Partition and declaration of title being Title Suit No. 37 of 1997 in the court of Assistant Judge, Mehendigonj, Barisal with respect to the land described in scheduled to the plaint. 
(b) The case of the plaintiffs, in short is that Land measuring 1.00 acre appearing to hal Plot Nos. 296, 297, 298, 299 and 300 of S.A. khatian No. 2942 under mouza Bogura Alekanda, P.S. Barisal Sadar belonged to Rahimzan Bibi who died leaving behind only son Rossul alt khallfa and that Rossul Ali Khalifa while enjoying the suit jama died leaving. behind 4 sons being defendant No. 4-7 and 3 daughter being defendant Nos. 2 and 3 and Zarina Begum. That Zarina Begum died behind leaving behind defendant Nos. 8-11. That Rossul Ali Khalifa also left behind his wife Moyful Bibi. That defendant No. 6 Alauddin Khalifa and defendant No. 7 Zalaluddin Khalifa by Registered Kabala dated 28.04.1969 transferred 0.16 acre of land from Plot No. 298 and 299 to the Plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2. That they were minors at the time of execution of the kabala and their mother obtained permission from the court and executed registered kabala on behalf of the Minors. That the plaintiffs in pursuance of the kabala got 0.045 acre from suit Plot No. 299 and 0.1150 acre from suit Plot No. 298. That defendant No.3 Anwara and Zarina Begum transferred 0.1450 acre of land from Plot No. 298 and 299 to Plaintiffs Nos. I and 2 by way of Registered kabala dated 06.10.1965. That plaintiff No. 2 by deed gift dated 18.10.1988 transferred 0.08 acre from plot No. 298 and 0.02 acre from plot No. 299 to Plaintiff No. 1. But deed writer erroneously failed to insert plot No. 299 in the deed. That the Plaintiffs in pursuance of kabala dated 16.10.1965 and kabala dated 28.04.1969 obtained (0.04+0.0450) of 0.0850 acre in plot No.299 and (0.1050+ 0.1150) of 0.22 acre in plot No. 298. That the plaintiffs transferred 0.06 acre of land from suit plot No. 298 to the defendant No.6 and has been possessing rest .02450 acre of land. That the plaintiffs mutated their names in the khatian. That defendants Nos. 4-5 and Moyful Bibi Transferred 0.15 acre from plot No. 298 and 0.07 acre from plot No. 299 total measuring 0.22 acre to the defendant No.1 Rehana Begum but she fraudulently managed to open a new khatian being No.2941/1 showing 0.16 acre from plot No. 2999 and .0666 acre from plot No. 298 in her name and that the collusive record and had no value. That the plaintiff No. I gifted 0.16 acre from plot No. 298 and 0.065 acre from plot No. 299 totaling 0.225 acre to his wife Saleha Khatun being plaintiff No. 3 and that plaintiff No. 3 succeeded to get a decree of declaration of title to her share in T.S. No. 261/98. That the defendant Nos. 13-15 being informed of the suit forcibly tried to make but to the south part of plot No. 299 and plaintiffs filed an application for temporary injunction. That, during pendency of the petition for temporary injunction defendant Nos. 13-15 forcibly constructed a two-storied tinted, which was found by learned Advocate commissioner by way of local inspection. That the Tinshed is situated on 0.0075 acre of land described in schedule Kha to the plaint. Plaintiffs pray for recovery of khass possession in respect of "Kha" scheduled land by demolishing huts constructed thereon during pendency of the suit. Defendants No.2 on 2 Baishakh 1399 B.S. refused to partition plaintiffs share for which cause of action for this suit arose.-Plaintiffs pray for partition to the extent on 0.2450 acre of land from plot No. 298 and 299 out of 0.57 acres as detailed in the schedule to the plaint. 

3. The defendant No. 6 and 13-15 filed separate written statements but at the time of hearing the defendant No. 6 did not turn up and the suit was contested by defendant Nos. 13-15. They denied the material allegations of the plaint and contended that inter alia that the suit was not maintainable in its present forms; that it was bad for defect of parties and Hotchpotch. That the material case of the defendant No. 13-15 were that co-sharer defendant No. 5-6 and Moyful Bibi vide Kabala dated 07.05.1965 transferred 0.16 acre from suit plot No. 299 and 0.06 acre from suit plot No. 298 totaling  0.22 acre to Rehana Begum who succeeded to open a separate khatian bearing No. 2942/1 in her name. That Rehana Begum by way of different kabala transferred (0.03+0.0275+0.0275+0.0075) or 0.0925 acre of land from plot No. 299 to defendant Nos. 13-15 and that they by metes and bounds with other Co-shares have been possessing 0.0925 acre of land in plot No. 299 by making dwelling house, growing fruit bearing trees and paying rents to the government. That the plaintiffs have no right, title and interest in the land. 

4. The plaintiffs examined 4 witnesses and the defendant Nos. 13-15 examined 3 witnesses and they also filed documents in support of their respective cases. 

5. The Learned Assistant Judge on consideration of evidences and materials on record decreed the suit by the judgment and decree dated 10.04.2000. 

6. The defendants No. 143-15 being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree, preferred Title Appeal No. 4 of 2005 before the District Judge, Barisal which on transfer was heard by the Divisional Special Judge and District Judge, Barisal who by his judgment and Order dated 25.05.2006 allowed the appeal and sent back the suit to the trial court for hearing afresh. 
7. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid appellate judgment and decree the plaintiff as petitioners obtained the present rule. 

8. Mr. Abdul Quayum, the learned Advocate along with Mr. Taposh Biswas, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners placed the revisional application, the impugned judgments and decrees and submitted that in the facts and circumstances of the case for non inclusion of plot no. 296,297 and 300 of S.A khatian No. 2954 in the schedule of the suit for partition, the suit will not be hit by the principle of hotch potch and the learned appellate Court committed error in holding that the suit is barred by the principle of hotch potch and remanding the case with direction for amendment of the plaint. The learned Advocate for the petitioners further submitted that the learned trial Court having considered the facts and circumstances of the case found that the plaintiff and defendants are purchasers of land from suit plot no. 298 and 299 only and they having no common interest in other plots of the said khatian for non inclusion of 3 others plots in the schedule, the suit will not be bad for defect of hotch potch and accordingly having decreed the suit in preliminary form, the learned appellate Court without considering this aspect of the case committed error in allowing the appeal and remanding the suit to the learned trial Court with direction for amendment of the plaint. The learned Advocate for the petitioner further submitted that the learned appellate Court without disposing of the appeal on merit committed error in allowing the appeal holding that the suit is bad for defect of hotch potch. 

9. Mr. Md. Nazrul Islam, the learned Advocate along with Mr. Syed Al Asafur Ali, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties No. 1-3, on the other hand, submitted that the established principle of law is that in a partition suit all the plots of a particular khatian should be brought into hotch potch, otherwise, there will be scope for further litigation entailing the parties to further expenses and inconveniences, so the learned appellate Court was justified in allowing the appeal sending the case on remand with direction to make necessary
amendment. The learned Advocate further submitted that the plaintiff petitioners in their pleadings or evidence could not make out any such case of exceptional circumstances in the present suit, as pointed out by the learned appellate Court and that those conditions having not been fulfilled, the learned appellate Court was perfectly justified in allowing the appeal. 
10. On perusal of the judgment passed by the Courts 'below, it appears, the learned appellate Court having found that as all the plots of the khatian have not been brought in hotch potch, the partition suit is bad for defett of hotch potch and as such allowed the appeal remanding the case, and as such the learned appellate Court did not enter into the merit of the suit and did not give any finding as to the share of the parties in the suit. The provision of law is that the learned appellate Court must consider each of the findings of the trial Court then to give his own independent finding on the basis of the material on record, but in the present case, it appears, the learned appellate Court only considered the question of hotch potch and came to the finding that the plaintiff should be given a chance to amend the plaint by inclusion of the rest 3 plots namely plot No.296, 297 and 300 in hotch potch and as such, in my opinion, the impugned judgment and decrees passed by the learned appellate Court are not sustainable in law. 

11. Regarding the question of hotch potch the learned Advocate for the petitioner submitted that since both the Courts specifically found that the plaintiffs' and the contesting defendants' claim are confined to plot No. 298 and 299 and that they have no interest in the plot No. 296,297 and 300 of the suit Khatian, the suit is maintainable without bringing the other 3 plots in hotch potch and the learned Advocate for the petitioners has referred to the, decision of Abdul Gafur and others Vs- Abdul Khaleque and others reported in 1986 BLD(AD)86 wherein their lordships held that partial partition is maintainable when the plaintiffs and the defendants claim their share in some specific plots and not in all the plots of the khatian. 

12. The learned Advocate for the petitioners next submitted that the partial partition is also maintainable when the defendants fails to show that for non inclusion of some plots in the hotch potch none has been affected or any of the parties have been prejudiced, but in the present case, no such case has been made out by the contesting defendants or by any other defendants. The learned Advocate for the petitioners in support of his submission referred to the decision of Safaruddin and others-Vs-Fazlul Huq and others reported in 49 DI,R (AD)151 wherein it has been held that the rule that all the joint property should be included in a suit for partition is not an inflexible one and that a partial partition can be allowed where it is found that none of the parties will be prejudiced by such partition. 
13. In view of the aforesaid 2 decisions, I am of the opinion, that the suit as framed is maintainable and it will not fail for non conclusion of plot No.296,297 and 300 since the plaintiffs' and the defendants' claims are confined only to plot No.298 and 299 and that they have no interest in plot No.296, 297 and 300. It may be noted that the defendants could not also show that for non inclusion of said 3 plots the defendants or any of the parties in the suit will be prejudiced. Thus I am of the opinion that the suit as framed is also maintainable. 

14. Since I have found above that the learned appellate Court without considering 
and without giving any independent finding on other points as arrived at by the learned trial Court, has allowed the appeal, so I think it would be proper if the case is sent back on remand to the learned appellate Court for disposal of the appeal afresh after setting aside the impugned judgment and decree passed by the learned appellate Court. 

15. In the result, the rule is made absolute without any order as to costs and the 
judgment and decree passed by the learned appellate Court are set aside and the case is sent on remand to the learned appellate Court for fresh disposal in the light of the observations as made above and in accordance with law. The learned appellate Court is directed to dispose of the appeal within 4 months from the date of the receipt of the L.R. Records. 

16. The learned Advocate of the petitioners prays that the parties be directed to maintain 
status-quo with regard to possession in the suit land till disposal of the appeal. 

1.7. In view of such prayer of the learned advocate for the petitioners and in view of 
the facts and circumstances of the case the parties arc directed to maintain status-quo till disposal of the appeal by the learned appellate Court. 

18. Send down the L.C. Records immediately.

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Abdul Aziz, .J: This Rule has been issued calling upon the opposite parties No. .1 and 2 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 25.4.95 passed by the learned subordinate Judge. First Court. Munshigonj in Title Appeal No. 21 of 1992 should not be set aside. 

2. Opposite party Nos. I and 2 as plaintiff instituted Title suit No. 16 of 1990 against the petitioners and others for declaration of the impugned Kabalas as collusive, illegal and ineffective etc. and for cancellation of the same. The facts of the case of the plaintiff's-opposite party Nos. I and 2 in short inter-alia is that Abdul Ghani father of plaintiff No. 1 and husband of plaintiff No. 2 acquired title and possession in respect of suit land described in the schedule of the plaint measuring .25 decimals by purchase along with Ali Hossain father of defendant-petitioners who also acquired title and possession of the land measuring .81/2 decimals in the same plot by purchase that lather of plaintiff died leaving four suns including plaintiff No. 1 and 5 daughter and plaintiff No. 2 as wife who made amicable partition of the lands that the plaintiff' Nos. 2 got suit land measuring .25 decimals in plot No. 288 while defendants Nos. 5 to 7 who are also sons and daughter of Abdul Ghani and brothers and sisters of plaintiff' No. 1 got 15 decimals of land in plot No. 270 and 162 which they sold to Ali Hossain father of defendant-petitioners No. 1-4 about 37/38 years ago. The further case of the plaintiffs is that they purchased .7 decimals of land from the heirs of Jalal Box by kabala dated 8.6.88 and 24.7.77 and in this way the plaintiff's area in possession of the suit land as described in schedule 'Ka of the plaint acquiring title and possession by inheritance and by purchase and defendant No. 5 to 7 had no title and possession in the same but they sold the same secretly to defendant-petitioners No. 1-4 by registered kaalas dated 8.11.80 and 5.11.88 which the plaintiff' came to know from the reply of the petitioners tiled in a Criminal Case tiled against them by the plaintiffs on their throat to take possession of the suit land by force. The plaintiffs thereafter instituted the suit after taking certified copies of the said kabalas for declaration that the kabalas collusive and not binding upon the plaintiff's. The petitioners as defendant Nos. 1 to 4 contested the suit by filing written statement denying the averments of the plaintiffs made in the plaint contending that the plaintiff's have no cause of action to tile the suit that the suit is barred by the principle of waiver estoppels an acquiesce etc. The further case of the contesting defendant-petitioners is that defendant No. 5 to 7 namely-Nur Box Dewan. Md. Habibur Rahman Dewan and Sakina Khatun sons and daughter of Abdul Bhani brothers and sisters of plaintiffs No. 1 acquired right title and possession of the suit land along with other proportions and Nur Box Dwean sold .31/10 decimals and Habibur Rahman and Sakina sold 31/2 decimals of suit land to the petitioners by registered and since then they are possessing the suit land in their own right title and interest hence the suit is liable to he dismissed with coat. 

3. Learned Assistant Judge dismissed the suit on the finding that the plaintiff's could not prove as to how much land each heirs of Abdul Ghani-including the plaintiffs and defendant No. 5 to 7 got and from which plot. that through that plaintiff alleged amicable partition that but they could not prove that defendant Nos. 5 to 7 had no right, title and possession in the suit land and their right and title was extinguished, and they failed to prove that the impugned Kabalas dated 8.11.80.and 3.11.88 are collusive, fabricated and illegal. Trial court also found possession of the suit land in favour of the defendant petitioners. The plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 and 2 being aggrieved preferred Title Appeal No. 21 of 1992 before the learned District Judge, Munshiganj. learned Subordinate Judge. First Court who allowed the appeal and decreed the suit reversing the judgment and decree of the Trial Court directing the plaintiffs-appellants to pay advalorem court tee for the decreed prayed for by them. The appellate Court below allowed the appeal finding possession in favour of the plaintiffs and against defendant petitioners and finding the impugned kabalas ineffective illegal and not binding upon the plaintiff: Being aggrieved by the aforesaid impugned judgment and decree of the Appellate Court below the defendant No. 194 as petitioners obtained this Rule on an application under section 115(1) of the code of Civil procedure. 

4. Mr. Sheikh Abdul Awal the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners took me through judgment and decrees of the Courts below and the evidence an materials on record of the case and submits that the learned subordinate Judge erred in law in finding that the impugned kabalas are illegal and not binding upon the p plaintiffs is based on no evidence and as such the judgment and decree of the appellate court is liable to be not aside. He submits that the appellate Court below erred in law in finding possession of the suit land in favour of the plaintiffs and against the petitioner on misreading of evidence and also ignoring the facts that the plaintiff's could not prove that they acquired 25 decimals of land in the suit plot by amicable partition among the co-sharers after the death of their predecessor. He further submits that the appellate Court below having affirmed the finding of the trial court that the appellate court below having affirmed the finding of the trial court that plaintiffs could not prove amicable partition of the proportion left by their predecessor Abdul Gani and the saham acquired by and possessed each of his heirs in his proportion including the suit land, the appellate court judgment is liable to be set aside. He also strongly contended that there is no concurrent finding by the appellate court below from the evidence and materials on record that defendant No. 5 to 7 did not inherit and receive any 'sahan' in plot No. 288 which they sold to the petitioners by registered kabala on due consideration making over possession to them. Mr. Sheikh Abdul Awal, the learned Advocate also contended that there is nothing in the record to show that the impugned kabalas were collusive and fraudulent. He asserts that the title and interest of the vendors of the impugned kabalas having been legally and rightly transferred by them to the petitioners by registered kabalas followed by possession due consideration, the appellate court below has erred in law in decreeing to suit. Mr. Awal has referred a decision in the case of Abul Hossain Mollah & another-Vs-Khoteza Nessa Bibi & others reported in 46 D.L.R. page 310. 

5. No one appeared for the opposite parties. 

6. Perused the judgment of the courts below evidence and materials on record of the case and heard the learned Advocate for the petitioners. plaintiffs examined three witnesses including plaintiff No. 3 while contesting defendants have also examined 3 D. Ws. including defendant No. 1. 
7. Plaintiffs case in short is that they got 23 decimals of land in plot No. 288 by amicable settlement among the hears left by their predecessor Abdul Gani. On the other hand the case of the contesting defendants petitioners is that their vender defendant NO. 3 to 7 also got saham in the suit plot and while in possession they sold the same to them. Admittedly both Abdul Gani the predecessor of the plaintiffs and defendant No. 5-7 and All Hossain father of the petitioners (defendant No. 1-4) were the owners in possession along with others of the lands of the suit plot No. 288 by purchase. This is also admitted that the alleged amicable partition between the heirs of Abdul Gani predessor of the plaintiffs and defendant No. 5-7 allegedly took place 37/38 years ago. The impugned kabalas have not been marked as exhibit in the suit. The trial court found that the p.W.1 being the plaintiff No. 1 has admitted in his cross court in categorically that the land left by their predecessor was amicably partitioned 35 years ago but he could not say the amount/quantity of land got by each heirs nor mentioned in his plaint that the defendant No. 5-7 got their 'Sahan' in plot No. 150. The trial court also found that there is no mention in the plaint or in the evidence that how much land and in which plots heirs of the father of the plaintiff No. 1 got or that the defendant No. 5 to 7 did not get any property from any other plots except plot No. 238 or 270/262. Trial court also found that plaintiff No. 1 could not say as to how muchxiland his father left. On elaborate discussion and consideration of evidence of the P. Ws. the trial court specifically found that the plaintiffs could not prove no in the facts of the suit it could be believed that only plaintiffs got 18 decimals of land in suit plot No. 288 by amicable partition and defendant No. 5-7 got land in 238 and 270/262 only. These findings of the trial court have virtually been affirmed by the Appellate court below by its finding quoted below : 
“পি, ডারিঃ ১ এর জেরায় যদিও কিছুটা ত্রুটি পরিলক্ষিত হয় যেমন বন্টনের সময় বাদী পিতার অন্যান্য ওয়ারিশগণ কোন দাগে কতটুকু পাইয়াছিল তাহা স্পষ্ট ভাবে উল্লেখ করেন নাই ৷ ১নং ৰাদীর পিতার মৃত্যুর সময় কি পরিমাণ জমি রাখিয়া গিয়াছিল তাহাও উল্লেখ করেন নাই।"
Both the courts below having thus concurrently found as above, the learned subordinate Judge has erred in law in decreeing the suit.

 8. As regards possession of the suit land P.W.1 has stated that the amicable partition 35 years ago 15 years after the death of his father who left four sons, one daughter and a wife P.W.2 Sultan admitted that he has no land contiguous to the suit land in cross he stated that amicable settlement took place 40/45 years ago in his presence but he could not say how much of land received by each heir P. W. 3 had also no land to the surrounding of the suit land. He also could not say as how much of land the plaintiff No. 1 purchased. It may be mentioned that P.W.3 is the vagina (nephew) and P.W.3 is uncle-in-law of the plaintiff No. 1. The trial court on due consideration of evidence of the P. Ws. found specifically that it could not be believed that the plaintiffs alone possessed entire .25 decimals of land in suit plot. But the appellate court found possession of the plaintiff against the defendant without reversing the finding of the trial Court and seems to be on misreading without reversing the finding of the trial court and seems to be on misreading of the evidence of the P.Ws. It may be mentioned that no independent witness has been examined by the plaintiffs to prove his possession of the suit land. Trial Court also specifically found that the plaintiff could not prove that defendant Nos. 5-7 fraudulently executed and registered the deeds in favour of the petitioners nor the plaintiff's could prove that the kabalas were collusive. It is also found by the trial Court that all the D.Ws. have categorically deposed about the possession in favour of the defendant-petitioners. The appellate Court below decreed the suit finding that the impugned kabalas are illegal and not effective is not based on evidence nor the appellate Court below reversed the above finding of the trial court in arriving at his said finding. The finding of the trial court that the plaintiff failed to prove that the right, title, interest and possession of the defendants No. 5-7 had extinguished from the suit plot and failed to prove that the kabalas are collusive and without consideration, illegal and not binding on the plaintiff is based on due consideration of the evidence on record of the case which has not been reversed by the appellate court below. In that view of the matter the impugned judgment and decree passed by the appellate court below is not sustainable in law. 
9. This admitted that defendant Nos. 5 to 7 transferred their title by registered kabalas such kabalas cannot be declared illegal and collusive in absence of any evidence to that effect and that the same was done fraudulently. Plaintiffs also could not prove by evidence to show kabalas were fabricated without consideration and collusive and no title passed through those kabals. A valid title transferred by registered kabalas cannot be cancelled in absence of any evidence that that the same is fraudulent fabricated without consideration and obtained by practicing fraud. 

10. 1 find substance in the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioners and find the decision referred by him as quoted above, applicable in this case. The impugned judgment and evidence of the appellate Court below is thus liable to be set aside. 

11. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 25.4.95 and 28.4.95 respectively passed by the learned subordinate Judge, First Court, Munshiganj in Title Appeal No. 21 of 1992 is hereby set aside these dated 27.2.92 and 3.3.92 passed by the learned Assistant Judge. Tungibari Upazila in Title Suit No. 16 of 1990 is hereby affirmed. 

12. Send down the L. C. records at once. 

End.

full_judgment:
At the instance of the plaintiffs this Rule arises out of the judgment and decree dated 04.01.2007, passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Fourth Court, Khulna, in Title Appeal No.203 of 2003, reversing those dated 31.05.2003, passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Domoria, Khulna, in Title Suit No.105 of 2001.

That Sudebi Bairagee, wife of late Kesto Das Bairage @ Krisna Das Bairage and Keturam Kirtania, son of late Ratikanta Bairage as plaintiff Nos.1 and 2 respectively instituted Title Suit No.498 of 1977 in the First Court of Munsif, Khulna for declaration of their title in respect of 2.18 acres of land out of the suit land as well as for partition of the suit land by making proper demarcation of their 2.18 acres of land. Subsequently the names of the said two plaintiffs were struck off since they transferred their share to the plaintiff Nos.3-18 subsequently added as party. Ultimately the suit was transferred to the Court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Domoria, Khulna and renumbered as Title Suit No.105 of 2001.

The plaint of the plaintiffs in brief that the suit land alongwith other lands belonged to Babu Kali Prosonna Chattopadday and others in their mourasi maliki right. They had been enjoying and possessing the same by granting settlement to tenants as well as by keeping it under their khas possession. Adjacent to their land in C.S. Plot Nos.1201 and 1121 situated in the bank of Athar Baki river some land was created by gradual silting forming some char land. The said Char land was contiguous to the land of C.S. Plot No.394, 395, 397 is eastern side. Out of that land Krishna Das Adhikari took settlement of 0.42 acres of land of plot No.1201 by furnishing a kabuliyat dated 17.12.1935, Full Mohon Barai took settlement of further 0.42 acres from the said plot No.1201 by furnishing kabuliyat dated 19.09.1936. Subsequently the defendant No.1 Mofazzal Hossain became owner of 0.42 acres of land of Krishna Das by way of transfer. Kesto Das Bairagee by furnishing a registered kabuliyat dated 08.12.1936 took settlement of 0.84 acres of land out of the land of another Plot No.1121 and 0.15 acres of land from the land of Plot No.396, in total he took settlement of 0.99 acres of land by the said kabuliyat. Kesto Das Bairagee on 03.09.1938 took settlement of further 0.42 acres of land from the land of both plot Nos.1201 and 1121. Kesto Das died leaving behind his wife Sudebi Bairagee as his heir and successor. The plaintiffs by way of transfer became owners of entire property of Kesto Das. At the time of death of Kesto Das he had no wife named as Anarothi and had no son named Dhakur Das Bairagee. By the deed allegedly executed by Dhakur Das Bairagee the defendant No.17 Full Mia and defendant No.18 Md. Ali Sheikh did not accrue any right, title and possession over the suit land. The said char land settled by the aforesaid kabuliyat measuring 2.10 acres was increased up to an area of 3.63 acres due to gradual silting up. The said 3.63 acres of land was recorded in S.A. Plot Nos.1135, 1136 and 1137 under S.A. Khatian Nos.411, 412 and 413. Kesto Das Bairagee had been enjoying and possessing 2.18 acres of land but that was not recorded in his name. That 0.15 acres of land settled by the kabuliyat dated 18.12.1936 was recorded in his name. The kabala No.763 dated 16.06.1978 allegedly executed by Dhakur Das Bairagee in favour of the defendant Nos.17 and 18 is false and forged. Kesto Das had two wives named Basonta and Sudebi and he has no wife named Anarothi or no son by Anarothi named Dhakur Das Bairagee. Against the said deed a criminal case was instituted in which the defendant Nos.17 and 18 were convicted with sentence to suffer imprisonment for two years and to pay fine. Against such sentence an appeal is pending before the learned Additional Sessions Judge. Kesto Das @ Krishna Das Bairagee on 10.04.1974 transferred 0.99 acre of land to Sudebi Bairagee and Kitoram Kirtania. Subsequently Keturam

Kirtania on	12.07.1979 transferred 0.42 acre of land

On behalf of her two minor sons Horidas Bairagee and Keshob Bairagee, Sudebi Bairagee, wife of Kesto Das alongwith Kesto Das’s daughter Sabitree Bairagee on 04.12.1990 transferred 1.46 acres of land to the

of land. In the suit land the plaintiffs have got their residence in a part. They claimed demarcation of the same with the defendants but being denied they compelled to institute the suit.
 
The defendant No.1 Mofazzal Hossain and the defendant Nos.17 Full Miah and 18 Sheikh Md. Ali by filing two separate written statements contested the suit. The defendant No.1 stated in brief, that 1.06 acres of land of C.S. Plot No.131, under C.S. Khatian No.394 admittedly belonged to Kali Prosonna and others and out of that land by kabuliyat No.5948 dated 17.12.1935 Krisno Das Adhikari took settlement of 0.42 acre of land. The said landlord on receipt of kabuliyat dated 19.09.1936 granted settlement of 0.42 acre of land from the land of C.S. Plot No.1201 with Ful Mohon @ Full Mon Barai @ Full Mohon Biswas. Krisno Das and Balaram were two full brothers and by earning of their joint family Krishno Das took settlement in his name. Krisno Das died leaving behind two sons Jadob and Sattendra Adhikari. Jadob died leaving behind two sons Pobitra and Sadai and widow Suvodra. Balaram died leaving behind three sons named Kalipada, Druba and Niren. That 0.42 acre of land of Plot No.1201 settled by kabuliyat No.5948/35 was increased up to an area of 1.9 acres by gradual siltation in its eastern side and that was recorded in S.A. Khatian No.411 in the names of Jadob and Sattendra. Full Mohon and Bizabor were full brothers and by the earning of their joint family they took settlement of the land by kabuliyat No.4901/36 dated 19.09.1936 in the name of Full Mohon alone, but both the brothers had right and title in the said land. Full Mohon died leaving behind two sons named Chitta Ranjan and Mokunda Biswas. That 0.42 acre of land of Plot No.1201 settled by the kabuliyat No.4909/36 was increased up to an area of 1.10 acres by gradual siltation in its eastern side and the same was properly recorded in the names of Bizabor Mohon, Chitta Ranjan and Mukunda in S.A. record. The said land was listed as vested property and Darbesh Sheikh and Shahjahan Sheikh took lease of the same. After death of Jadob Adhikari, owner of 4 anas share of the land of S.A. Khatian No.411, his wife Suvodra Adhikari on behalf of her minor two sons Pabitra and Sadai Adhikari on 29.04.1970 sold 0.492 acre of land to Sattendra Nath Adhikari by way of sale and Sattendra Nath subsequently sold the same to the defendant No.1 on 15.07.1973. Kalipad on 13.01.1970 sold 0.33 acre of land alongwith 0.3 acres of land of another holding to Druba and Niren. The said Druba and Niren sold 0.99 acre of land to defendant No.1. By Mutation Case No.40 of 1975-76 the defendant No.1 mutated the same in his name. Mukunda Barai @ Mukunda Biswas on 05.03.1977 transferred 0.272 acre of land to defendant No.1 Muhitunnessa. Kesto Das died leaving behind two wives the plaintiff No.1 Sudebi Bairagee and another Anarathi alongwith his son Dhakur Das by Anarathi and two daughters Sabitri and Ahalla by Sudebi. Dhakur Das on 16.03.1978 sold 0.55 acre of land to defendant No.17 Full Miah and defendant No.18 Md. Ali Sheikh. Regarding that land they instituted Title Suit No.136 of 1984 in the Second Court of Sub-ordinate Judge, Khulna which was subsequently transferred to the Third Court of Sub-ordinate Judge, Khulna and renumbered as Title Suit No.14 of 1994. The said suit was decreed. Kesto Das on 20.04.1974 transferred 0.99 acre of land to the plaintiffs. The plaintiff No.2 Keturam Kirtania on 12.07.1979 sold his land to added plaintiff No.3 Habibur Rahman. Against which the plaintiff No.1 instituted the pre-emption suit and obtained an order of pre-emption. Kesto Das Bairagee did not get any practical possession rather his land was under water. WAPDA acquired some land and the defendant No.1 got compensation for such acquisition. The plaintiffs have got no right, title and possession over the suit land, hence the suit is liable to be dismissed.

In their joint written statements the defendant No.17 Full Miah and defendant No.18 Sheikh Md. Ali stated that Kesto Das @ Krishno Bairagee was owner and possessor of entire 0.55 acre of land appertains to C.S. Plot No.1137 under C.S. Khatian No.264. The said land was recorded in the name of Kesto Das in S.A. Khatian No.413. Kesto Das had two wives named Anarathi and Sudebi, one son Dhakur Das, two daughters Sabitri and Ahalla. He died leaving behind one wife Sudebi and one son Dhakur Das as his heirs and successors. Out of the suit land Dhakur Das on 16.06.1978 transferred 0.55 acre of land alongwith other lands, in total 1.09 acres, to them. Regarding the said land they instituted Title Suit No.136 of 1984 which was subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No.14 of 1994 on its transfer to other Court and the same was decreed on 15.11.1994. By the Kabuliyat dated 08.12.1936 Kesto Das took settlement of 0.15 acre of land of Plot No.396 under C.S. Khatian No.131 and 0.84 acre of land of C.S. Plot No.1121 under C.S. Khatian No.2/3/7, in total 0.99 acre of land and on 20.04.1974 transferred the same to Sudebi Bairagee and Keturam Kirtania. During Settlement Survey Operation the C.S. Plot numbers have not been changed. The land of C.S. Plot No.1121 and S.A. Plot No.1137 are not same. On 28.07.1979

Sudebi Bairagee transferred 0.252 acre from the land of plot No.1137 to them and they executed a deed of reconveyance in favour of Sudebi, and as such by Preemption Miscellaneous Case No.146 of 1979 the plaintiff Habibur Rahman did not accrue any right, title and possession. For WAPDA 0.43 acre of land was acquired and they (defendant Nos.17 and 18) got compensation for such acquisition and they have been possessing remaining 0.12 acre of land. They were convicted on the allegation that the Deed No.763 dated 16.03.1978 executed by Dhakur Das Bairagee is forged and against that conviction Criminal Appeal No.17 of 1988 had been preferred which was allowed. Moreover, in the said case it was decided that by the Kabala dated 20.04.1974 Keturam and Sudebi did not accrue any right or title and from them the plaintiffs also did not accrue any right or title. The plaintiffs have no right, title and possession over the suit land, and hence the suit is liable to be dismissed.

After hearing the parties, the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Khulna by judgment and decree dated 29.10.1998 dismissed the suit finding that the plaintiffs failed to prove their case beyond reasonable doubt, on the other side the claim of the defendants is also apparently weak, the plaintiffs are not entitled to get any benefit for such weakness of the defendants. Against the said judgment and decree the plaintiffs preferred Title Appeal No.341 of 1998 before the learned District Judge, Khulna. On transfer the said appeal was heard by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, First Court, Khulna who by judgment and decree dated 11.06.2001 allowed the appeal and on setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the learned Assistant Judge sent back the suit on remand for hearing afresh and to decide the suit as per the observation made by him. The said Appellate Court observed that the suit is not barred by limitation and the Trial court did not discuss the evidences on record properly.

After sending back the suit on remand on transfer to the Court of Assistant Judge, Domoria, Khulna the suit was renumbered as Title Suit No.105 of 2001 and some amendment was made in the pleadings of the parties.

The learned Assistant Judge, Domoria, Khulna after hearing the parties and on discussion of the evidences on record by judgment and decree dated 31.05.2003 decreed the suit in preliminary form only in respect of 1.85 acres of land in favour of the plaintiffs finding their right, title and possession over the same. Against the said preliminary decree the plaintiffs and the contesting defendant Nos.17 and 18 did not prefer any appeal, but only the defendant No.1 Mofazzal preferred Title Appeal No.203 of 2003, in the Court of District Judge, Khulna. On transfer the said appeal was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, Fourth Court, Khulna who by the impugned judgment and decree dated 04.01.2007 allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment and preliminary decree passed by the Assistant Judge.

Hence, the plaintiffs as petitioners preferred this revision and obtained the Rule. Mr. Ahmed Nowshed Jamil, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioners submits that the Appellate Court committed illegality in finding that the plaintiffs failed to prove that Kesto Das Bairagee took settlement of 1.26 acre of land by furnishing kabuliyat. The WAPDA for which some of the land was acquired was added as party but did not come forward to contest the suit but without considering that aspect the impugned judgment was illegally passed on misinterpretation or non consideration of the evidences on record. In arriving into its decision the Appellate Court did not discuss the evidences on record and without discussion of the evidences on record on surmise and conjectures allowed the appeal and dismissed the suit. He further submits that such judgment can not be treated as a judgment of reversal as per the provision of law provides in Order 41 Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure which occasioned failure of justice, and hence impugned judgment is liable to be set aside.

In reply of his such argument Mr. Abul Kalam Mainuddin, learned Advocate, appearing for the opposite party Nos.1-3 submits, that the Trial Court in decreeing the suit in favour of the plaintiffs in respect of 0.84 acres of land committed illegality and that decree was passed without any basis and without mentioning any number of any plot in which the decreetal land is situated, but the Appellate Court on proper discussion of the materials on record rightly allowed the appeal and dismissed the suit.

After hearing the learned Advocates I have gone through the above mentioned four judgments, two by the Trial Court and two by the Appellate Court. On perusal of the said judgments it appears that the Trial Court in its first judgment passed in 1998 did not properly discuss the evidences on record rather passed its judgment on surmises and conjectures like a hypothesis. In that judgment the Trial Court did not at all consider the claims of the parties though some of the claims of the plaintiffs were admitted by the contesting defendants. However, on appeal the said judgment was set aside by the Appellate Court and the suit was sent back on remand to the Trial Court to hearing afresh after amendment of the pleadings. The Trial Court on consideration of the materials on record decreed the suit in preliminary form only in respect of 0.84 acre of land. Against that judgment and decree the contesting defendant Nos.17 and 18 and the plaintiffs did not prefer any appeal or cross objection. Only the defendant No.1 Mofazzal Hossain who allegedly succeeded the land settled by the admitted landlords in favour of Kesto Das Bairagee as per claim of the plaintiffs or Krishno Das Adhikari as per claim of the defendants in a different plot being C.S. Plot No.1201 and as per the said claim Krishno Das only took settlement 0.42 acre of the same plot. Accept that 0.42 acre the defendant No.1 did not claim any title in any way in any other part of the suit land. On consideration of the materials on record, particularly the kabuliat and the kabala, as well as the order of the pre-emption case and the aforementioned Criminal Case the learned Assistant Judge, Domoria, Khulna found plaintiff’s right, title and possession only in respect of 0.84 acre of land and as it claimed by the plaintiffs. In the plaint, the plaintiffs clearly claimed about settlement of specific area of land from respective specific plots. But on perusal of the judgment of the Appellate Court passed for the second time it appears that the learned Additional District Judge, third Court, Khulna disposed up the appeal like a criminal case. The learned Additional District Judge also found that the plaintiffs failed to prove their case beyond reasonable doubt. Such finding to decide a Civil Appeal or suit is apparently unnatural. His judgment appears to me as nothing but reproduction of the judgment passed by the Assistant Judge, Khulna in 1998 in the instant suit. On reading the said judgment I find that the same can not be treated as a judgment of reversal as per the provision of law provided in the Code of Civil Procedure. The defendants did not deny the entire claim of the plaintiffs as they claimed by way of settlement and successive transfer, but the Appellate Court without considering the documents of title of the plaintiffs dismissed the suit as a whole, meaning that the plaintiffs have no right, title ad possession in any part of the suit land. The basis of such judgment is nothing but that the Assistant Judge decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiffs in respect of only 0.84 acre of land without mentioning any plot number or khatian number. But finding of the learned Additional District Judge is apparently illegal because the learned Assistant Judge arrived into his decision on consideration and discussion of the materials on record and the suit was not decreed finally. The suit as being a suit of partition as well as for declaration of title was decreed preliminarily and to make it as final the Advocate Commissioner should specify shares of the plaintiffs or it may be specified amicably between the parties before drawing up the final decree. Before drawing up the final decree finding of the learned Additional District Judge is not sustainable.

Hence, this Rule is hereby made absolute. The judgment and decree dated 04.01.2007, passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Fourth Court, Khulna, in Title Appeal No.203 of 2003, is hereby set aside and the judgment and decree dated 31.05.2003, passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Domoria, Khulna, in Title Suit No.105 of 2001, is hereby restored.

However, there is no order as to costs. Send down the lower Court’s records immediately

End.
