full_judgment:
Sashanka Shekhar Sarkar, J: This rule nisi was issued at the instance of the petitioner on an application under Article 102 of the Constitution in the following terms: Let a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the inaction of the Respondents for not accepting the power of attorney dated 9-4-2014 as contained in annexure-K and not approving the plan executed in favor of Project Builders Ltd. in respect of House No. CN(H)4, Road No. 109, Gulshan-2, Dhaka-1212 should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. At the time of issuance of the rule, the parties were directed to maintain the status quo in respect of the position and possession of the House No. CN(H4), Road No. 1, 09, Gulshah-2, Dhaka for 6(six) months from the date, which was extended time to time. 

3. Facts for the disposal of the rule are as stated in the writ petition: 
"That the then the Dhaka Improvement Trust (presently known as RAJUK) leased out House No.CN(H)4, Road No. 109, Gulshan Dhaka, to one Shahabuddin vide Lease Deed No. 3997 dated 25-4-1962. The said Shahabuddin approved a plan dated 5-2-1963, which consisted of a one-story building. Subsequently, the said Mr. Shahabuddin entered into an Agreement for Sale on 10-1-1971 with the Imam Dockyards and Engineering Ltd. but as the said the Mr. Shahabuddin failed to execute a sale deed, the Imam Dockyards as plaintiff filed Title Suit No.409 of 1985 in the court of the learned Subordinate Judge, First Court, Dhaka, for specific performance of contract. The suit was decreed by the judgment and decree dated 18-5-1989, and for execution of the decree, the Imam Dockyards and Engineering Ltd. filed Execution Case No.12 of 1990, and in the course of the execution case, the Executing Court registered a Deed of Sale No. 9780 dated 23-8-1990 in favor of the Imam Dockyards and Engineering Ltd. The decree Execution Court on 13-9-1992 delivered the possession of the said plot to the Imam Dockyards and Engineering Ltd. 

4. In the meantime, the Government by the order dated 13-7-1985 enlisted the said plot in the "Ka" list of the abundant property, against which the said Shahabuddin filed Writ Petition No. 244 of 1985 before the Hon'ble High Court Division and the Hon'ble High Court Division by the judgment and order dated 25-9-1990 made the Rule absolute and also declared the inclusion of the said property in the "Ka" list is illegal and also directed the govt. To release the said property within 3 months from the date of receipt of the copy of the judgment and order. Thereafter, the government vide its gazette notification dated 19-3-1992 released the said plot from the "Ka" list of the abundant property. 

5. Thereafter, the Imam Dockyards and Engineering Ltd. applied for mutating the said plot in their name with RAJUK, but the RAJUK did not mutate the name of the Imam Dockyards and Engineering Ltd and accordingly, it filed a Writ Petition No. 3276 of 1996 before the Hon'ble High Court Division. After hearing the said writ petition, the Hon'ble High Court Division, by the judgment and order dated 19-2-1997, made the Rule absolute, directing the RAJUK to mutate the name of the Imam Dockyards and Engineering Ltd. in the official record of RAJUK. Subsequently, RAJUK, by the letter dated 15-6-1999, asked the Imam Dockyards and Engineering Ltd. to deposit the required fees and costs, and on the same date Taka 6,52,500/- was deposited in the concerned bank account of RAJUK and the RAJUK by the letter dated 01-7-1999 mutated the name of the Imam Dockyards and Engineering Ltd. in its official record. 

6. Thereafter, on 9-4-2014, the Imam Dockyards and Engineering Ltd. executed a registered Power Attorney Deed No.5675 dated 9-4-2014 for constructing a multi-storied building in the said plot in favor of Project Builders Limited, herein, the writ petitioner. Subsequently, the petitioner submitted the said power of attorney deed for acceptance, and also for approving the plan and drawing for the construction of the multi-storied building to the RAJUK. But the officials of RAJUK for the last 10 years have not taken any action upon the said representation. Subsequently, on 13-3-2016, Imam Dockyards and Engineering Ltd, represented by its Managing Director, submitted a representation to the RAJUK and on 30-12-2017, sent a notice demanding justice for accepting the power of attorney and approving the plan and the RAJUK duly received the letters but the RAJUK did not pay any heed of it. 

7. In the meantime, the Anti-Corruption Commission conducted an inquiry in respect of 37 plots of Gulshan and Banani area upon an allegation of forgery, and by the letter dated 28-8-2017, the Commission asked RAJUK to supply necessary papers and documents, but the Commission submitted a report on 2-12-2019. In the said report, it has been categorically pointed out that the Commission would investigate with respect to those plots in which the interest of RAJUK is involved. The Anti-Corruption Commission specifically mentioned that in the present plot, there is no interest of RAJUK, and the writ petitioner owns the said plot. 

8. However, the said Mr. Md. Shahabuddin filed Title Suit No. 202 of 2002 against the Imam Dockyards and Engineering Ltd. and the petitioner, praying for a declaration of title and the cancellation of Deed of Sale No. 202 of 2002. After hearing, the learned Judge dismissed the suit by the judgment and decree dated 30-4-2009. Thereafter, by suppressing the previous facts against the said Md. Shahabuddin, filed Title Suit No. 78 of 2013 in the court of the learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Dhaka for recovery of Khas Possession. The instant petitioner filed an application under section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint. The learned Judge, by the order dated 18-7-2018, allowed the application and dismissed the said suit on the ground of res judicata. 

9. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the inaction of the respondent in not accepting the Power Attorney Deed No.5675 dated 9-4-2014, and not approving the plan executed in favor of the petitioner in respect of the said plot situated at House No. CN(H)4, Road No. 109, Gulshan-2, Dhaka-1212, the petitioner hasfiled the instant application under Article 102 of the Constitution and obtained the present Rule Nisi and an order of status quo. 

10. Facts as stated in the affidavit-in-opposition filed by the respondent No.2 (RAJUK): 
The land measuring an area of 16 Katha 5 Chatak, at Plot No. 4, Block-CEN(H), Gulshan Model Town, Dhaka, was initially listed as "Abandoned Property" but was released on 19-3-1992, per a High Court order. The writ petitioner claims to be the constituted attorney of the lessee, but RAJUK's original record for the plot is missing, preventing it from ascertaining the initial lessee. Two claimants have provided photocopies of documents, indicating the plot was leased to Mr. Sahabuddin, who then entered a sale agreement with Md. Siraj Uddin Khan on January 10, 1971. 

11. M/s. Imam Dockyard and Engineering Ltd., represented by Md. Siraj Uddin Khan secured the plot through a specific performance of contract suit, decreed on May 18, 1989. They obtained Sale Deed No.9780 on 23-8-1990, via Execution Case No. 12 of 1990, and gained possession. The High Court, on 19-2-1997, directed RAJUK to mutate the plot into Imam Dockyard's name, which occurred on 01-7-1999, after payment of the fees requested by RAJUK on 9-5-1999. 

12. Subsequently, on 12-8-2009, Md. Siraj Uddin Khan reported the original record missing and sought file reconstruction, providing photo-copies. He then entered a Joint Venture Agreement with Resource Housing Limited on 7-8-2009 (Deed No. 8268), simultaneously granting them power of attorney No. 8269 for the construction and sale of the developer's portion. He repeatedly asked RAJUK to accept this power of attorney (letters dated 6-8-2009, 30-6-2009, and 27-12-2010). Later, on 9-7-2014, Imam Dockyard, represented by Mrs. Majeda Begum, issued a new irrevocable general power of attorney No. 5675 to Project Builders Limited, requesting RAJUK's acceptance on 9-11-2014. 

13. On the other hand, Md. Sahabuddin appointed Md. Atiqur Rahman with Irrevocable General power of attorney No. 17004 on 9-12-1999, requesting RAJUK's acceptance in 2007 and 2009. RAJUK, on 16-6-2009, asked him to appear with original documents. Sahabuddin also petitioned the State Minister of Public Works to direct RAJUK to accept his power of attorney and reconstruct the record, claiming to hold the original lease deed, providing an affidavit and NID. He also sought direction for RAJUK to accept his service charge. 

14. In the meantime, RAJUK has listed the plot among 32 disputed plots, while the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) listed it among 44 plots claimed by "fake and fictitious persons." The ACC requested documents from RAJUK on 28-8-2017, which were supplied on 28-9-2017. Md. Sahabuddin filed Title Suit No. 1018 of 2011 to correct the City Khatian recorded under the Ministry of Public Works, and the Deputy Commissioner, after a report, forwarded the matter to the Ministry for direction. RAJUK formed a committee, which reported on 19-12-2009, with RAJUK's board deciding on September 23 and 26, 2010, to further investigate and present findings to a future board meeting. 

15. Given that two Powers of Attorney have been submitted, two civil court decrees are in force favoring different claimants, the ACC is investigating potential fraud, and RAJUK's original file is missing, it is contended that the petitioner's power of attorney cannot be accepted, and the Rule should be discharged, also asserting the writ petitioner has not approached the court with clean hands. 

16. Mr. SM Mahbubul Islam, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that the RAJUK failed to discharge its statutory obligation as per Rules 3, 6, and 14 of the Dhaka Imarat Nirman Bidhimala, 2008. The RAJUK itself mutated the name of Imam Dockyards and Engineering Ltd. in its official record on 01-7-1999, according to the judgment and order dated 19-2-1997 passed by the Hon'ble High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 3276 of 1996. Admittedly, RAJUK did not challenge the legality of the judgment and order dated 19-2-1997 in the Appellate Forum. so RAJUK is duty-bound to accept the power of attorney deed dated 9-4-2014 and also to approve the plan and drawing to construct a multi-storied building. For the past decade, RAJUK's inaction has deprived the petitioner of their lawful rights, suggesting a bias influenced by a "vested quarter" and a failure to uphold their legal obligations. 

17. Mr. Islam further submits that the Anti-Corruption Commission conducted an inquiry in respect of 37 plots of Gulshan and Banani area upon an allegation of forgery by the letter dated 28-8-2017, the Commission asked RAJUK to supply necessary papers and documents, but the Commission submitted a report on 2-12-2019. In the said report, it has been categorically pointed out that the Commission would investigate with respect to those plots in which the interest of RAJUK is involved. The Anti-Corruption Commission specifically mentioned that in the present plot, there is no interest of RAJUK, and the writ petitioner owns the said plot. 

18. Mr. Islam further submits that RAJUK has illegally and unlawfully refused to accept the power of attorney and the multi-storied building plan for House No. CN(H)4, Road No. 109, Gulshan-2, Dhaka-1212. This inaction violates Articles 27, 31, and 40 of the Constitution of Bangladesh. Given that RAJUK officially mutated the plot in the name of Imam Dockyards and Engineering Ltd., thereby acknowledging them as their lessee, RAJUK is legally bound to accept power of attorney Deed No. 5675 dated April 9, 2014, and approve the construction plan. RAJUK's failure to act should be declared illegal and without lawful authority, and a court of equity should direct RAJUK to approve the writ petitioner's plan and drawing as a consequential relief. 

19. Conversely, Mr. Md. Imam Hasan, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No.2 submits that the land measuring an area of 16 Katha 5 Chatak plot in Gulshan Model Town, Dhaka (Plot No. 4, Block-CEN(H)), initially listed as "Abandoned Property," was released in 1992 following a High Court order. However, its ownership has since become highly contentious, partly due to missing original records from RAJUK. M/s. Imam Dockyard and Engineering Ltd. (represented by Md. Siraj Uddin Khan) claims its ownership. They successfully pursued a specific performance of contract suit in 1989, leading to a court-executed sale deed and possession in 1990. Despite RAJUK's initial resistance, on 19-2-1997, a High Court directive compelled RAJUK to mutate the plot in Imam Dockyard's name, which was finalized on 01-7-1999. Subsequently, in the year 2009, Md. Siraj Uddin Khan formed a joint venture with Resource Housing Limited for construction and delegated development power through a power of attorney, repeatedly requesting RAJUK's acceptance. Later, in 2014, Imam Dockyard (represented by Mrs. Majeda Begum) again appointed Project Builders Limited with an Irrevocable General power of attorney, also seeking RAJUK's acceptance. On the other hand, the original lessee, Md. Sahabuddin continues to assert his claim. He appointed Md. Atiqur Rahman, via an Irrevocable General power of attorney in 1999 and has consistently pressed RAJUK and the Ministry of Public Works to accept his power of attorney, reconstruct records, and acknowledge him as the owner, even submitting his original lease deed and NID. He also filed a title suit in 2011 to correct the City Khatian. 

20. Mr. Hasan nirther submits that the situation has been further complicated by the fact that two individuals are currently claiming the plot, submitting various photocopied documents for record reconstruction. RAJUK has acknowledged the plot as one of 32 disputed properties, while the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) is investigating it among 44 plots allegedly claimed by "fake and fictitious persons." The ACC has requested and received records from RAJUK regarding these investigations. RAJUK itself formed a committee in 2009 to examine documents and claimants and identify those responsible for the missing records, with further board investigations decided in late 2010. This ongoing dispute, marked by missing records, conflicting claims, civil court decrees, and an ACC investigation, highlights the significant challenges in determining definitive ownership and moving forward with any development on this valuable Gulshan property. 

21. Heard the learned Advocate for both sides and perused the materials on record thoroughly. 

22. It is admitted that the measuring of an area of 16 Katha 5 Chatak plot in Gulshan Model Town, Dhaka (Plot No. 4, Block-CEN(H), originally allotted by the then Dhaka Improvement Trust (for short, DIT, presently Rajdhani Unnayan Kartipakhkha (for short, RAJUK), in favour of one Mr. Md. Shahabuddin by way of registered Deed of Lease No.3997 dated 25-4-1962 (Annexure-A to the writ petition). Thereafter, the said Md. Shahabuddin constructed a one-storied residential building upon the said land after approving the plan dated 5-2-1963 from the then DIT. 

23. Subsequently, on 10-1-1971, said Md. Shahbuddin agreed to sell his said property to Md. Serazuddin Khan, who entered the agreement on behalf of Imam Dockyards and Engineering Ltd (Annexure-B to the writ petition). Following Shahabuddin's failure to execute the deed, Imam Dockyards successfully sued for specific performance, obtaining a court decree on 18-5- 1989, and a registered sale deed on 23-8-1990, subsequently gaining possession on September 13, 1992 (Annexure-C to the writ petition). Simultaneously, the government erroneously listed the plot as "abandoned property" on 13-7- 1985; however, the High Court declared this illegal on 25-9-1990, ordering its release, which occurred via gazette notification on 19-3-1992 (Annexure-E and F to the writ petition). Despite High Court directives from 19-2-1997, RAJUK mutated the said plot into Imam Dockyards' name on July 1, 1999, after receiving the required fees (Annexure-J to the writ petition). Ten years ago, on 9-7-2014, Imam Dockyards granted Project Builders Limited (the writ petitioner) a power of attorney No.5675 to construct a multi-storied building, but RAJUK has since failed to act on the submitted deed and plans, ignoring subsequent representations and a demand for justice. 

24. The respondent No.2 (RAJUK) does not deny the above facts regarding the said plot. However, the respondent No.2 stated that on 12-8-2009, Md. Siraj Uddin informed RAJUK that the original record for the plot was missing and requested its reconstruction, providing photo-copied documents (Annexure-7 to the affidavit-in-opposition). Concurrently, on 7-8-2009, Md. Siraj Uddin Khan signed a Joint Venture Agreement (Deed No. 8268) with Engr. AZM Bashir, Managing Director of Resource Housing Limited, for building construction. On the same day, he executed a power of attorney (No. 8269) to Resource Housing Limited, authorizing them to construct on the land and sell their portion. Md. Siraj Uddin Khan sent letters to RAJUK on 6-8-2009, 30-6-2009, and 27-12-2010, asking them to accept the power of attorney (Annexure-8, 8/1, 8/2, 8/3, and 8/4, respectively, to the writ petition). 

25. Respondent No.2 further states that, meanwhile, Md. Sahabuddin appointed Md. Atiqur Rahman with an Irrevocable General power of attorney No. 17004 dated 9-12-1999, concerning the same plot (Annexure-10 to the writ petition). Through letters dated 3-7-2007 and 9-4-2009, he applied to RAJUK for accepting this power of attorney. RAJUK responded on 16-6-2009, instructing him to appear in person with the original documents (Annexure-10/1, 10/2, and 10/3 respectively to the writ petition). But, the respondent No.2 did not confirm to this court whether the said Md. Sahabuddin appeared before RAJUK with all the relevant property documents. 

26. Respondent No.2 further states that Md. Sahabuddin further attempted to establish his claim by petitioning the Hon'ble State Minister of the Ministry of Public Works. He sought a directive for RAJUK to accept his power of attorney and, in a letter dated 10-8-2010, requested the reconstruction of the plot's record, asserting he possessed the original lease deed. To bolster his claim, he provided an affidavit declaring himself the owner and submitted his National ID. He also sent another application to the State Minister, requesting that RAJUK be directed to accept his service charge. 

27. It further appears from the Annexure-10/8 and 10/9 submitted by the respondent No.2 in its affidavit-in-opposition, that there are two national identification cards in the name of Md. Shahabuddin. How is it possible, though the Bengali name as it appeared in the two NID Cards with two different numbers as gill and DTs respectively. 

28. Additionally, an Anti-Corruption Commission inquiry, completed on 2-12-2019, affirmed RAJUK's lack of interest in the plot and confirmed that the said plot is under the possession of the instant writ petitioner (Annexure-O to the writ petition), from which it appears that the said property is legally holding possession by the writ petitioner as an attorney holder of the principal, Imam Dockyards and enaineering Ltd by way of the said registered power of attorney No. 5675 dated 9-4-2014. 

29. It's evident that Md. Shahabuddin's repeated attempts to reclaim the property through legal action have been unsuccessful. Both Title Suit No. 202 of 2002 and Title Suit No. 78 of 2013 were dismissed, with the latter specifically on the grounds of res judicata (as documented in Annexure-N of the writ petition). This indicates a pattern of failed litigation by Md. Shahabuddin concerning this particular plot. 

30. By now, settled law, the actions of the respondents (government functionaries) while dealing with the people, if they are unfair or unreasonable, can be corrected by the Constitutional Court on the principles of legitimate expectations and promissory estoppel. The doctrine of promissory estoppel and legitimate expectation are equitable doctrines evolved by the judges while adjudicating upon the grievance lodged by the aggrieved party against an unfair and arbitrary action by the government. It falls in the sphere of neither contract nor statutory estoppel. It can be said that if the government promises to any person and the promise is not inconsistent with the law of the land and not against the public interest, then afterwards the government cannot refuse to abide by its promise and in case the government acts inconsistent with its promise, then the said action of the government is subject to the judicial review by the Constitutional Court. Where the government's controlled functionariesmakea promise, which ensures a right to anyone who believes them and acts under them, then those functionaries are precluded from acting detrimentally to the rights of such person/citizen. 

31. It also appears that the Mutation letter dated 1-7-1999 issued by the respondent No.2 (Annexure-J to the writ petition) in the name of the Imam Dockyards and Engineering Ltd. is still valid, and the respondents are still silent about accepting the registered power of attorney No.5675 dated 9-4-2014, executed by the Imam Dockyards and Engineering Ltd. in favour of the writ petitioner, which cannot be done in the eyes of the law. 

32. In some cases within our jurisdiction; a writ of mandamus is involved, where the court orders government functionaries to perform their duties or take other necessary actions. Mandamus will apply in cases where any person or authority refrains from doing an act that they are not permitted by law to do or fails to do an act that is required by law to do. It can reach individuals or corporations only if there is some public duty to perform. Herein, the RAJUK has refrained from accepting the registered power of attorney No.5675 dated 9-4-2014, and also in not approving the building plan of the writ petitioner as an Attorney holder of the Imam Dockyards and Engineering Ltd., who is the lessee of the respondent No.2 (RAJUK) of the plot situated at House No. CN(H)4, Road No. 109, Gulshan-2, Dhaka-1212, which the respondents ought to do. 

33. Given the above, when, according to the respondent No.2's mutation letter, the petitioners' principal, Imam Dockyards and Engineering Ltd., has performed its duties by depoiting the stipulated payment for mutating the said land with the respondent No.2, then the respondents cannot refuse the petitioner to accept the registered power of attorney No.5675 dated 9-4-2014, and from having approving the building plan of the writ petitioner as an Attorney holder of the Imam Dockyards and Engineering Ltd., of the plot situated at House No.CN(H)4, Road No.109, Gulshan-2, Dhaka-1212. Accordingly, we find merit in the Rule. 

34. As a result, the Rule is made absolute. 

35. Consequently, the respondents' inaction in not accepting the power of attorney No.5675 dated 9-4-2014 as contained in Annexure-K and not approving the plan executed in favour of Project Builders Ltd. in respect of House No.CN(H)4, Road No. 109, Gulshan-2, Dhaka-1212 is hereby declared illegal, without lawful authority, and is of no legal effect. 

36. The respondents are hereby directed to accept the registered power of attorney No.5675 dated 9-4-2014 executed by Imam Dockyards and Engineering Ltd. in favour of the petitioner, Project Builders Limited (as contained in Annexure-K to the writ petition) for constructing a multi-storied building and to approve the plan made for constructing the multi-storied building in favour of Project Builders Ltd. in respect of the plot situated at House No.CN(H)4, Road No. 109, Gulshan-2, Dhaka-1212, within 30 (thirty) days from the date of the receipt of a copy of this judgment and order. 

37. There is no order as to cost. 

Communicate the judgment and order at once. 

End.

full_judgment:
Mohammad Ullah, J. On an application under Article 102 read along with Articles 27, 31, 42, and 44 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, this Court, by an order dated 04.09.2023, issued Rule upon the respondents in the following terms: 
"Let a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why a direction shall not be passed upon them for taking action/steps to make specific allotment of a-3(three) katha plot in favour of the petitioners in the project namely "সম্প্রসারিত উত্তরা ৩য় পর্ব প্রকল্প আবাসিক এলাকা", and hand over possession thereof to the petitioners and/or why such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper shall not be passed."

2. Subsequently, on 07.02.2024, considering an application of the petitioners, this Court directed the respondents to keep/preserve 6(six) individual plots to make allotment of three Kathas plots in favour of the petitioners within the project area, namely সম্প্রসারিত উত্তরা ৩য় পর্ব প্রকল্প আবাসিক এলাকা.

3. The facts leading to the disposal of the Rule, in short, are that the government under L.A. Case No.7/2000-2001 acquired 16.50 decimals of land from the petitioner Nos.1, 5 and 6 while 16.63, 17.40, 24.00 decimals were acquired from petitioner Nos.2-4 respectively for establishing a residential project namely " সম্প্রসারিত উত্তরা ৩য় পর্ব প্রকল্প আবাসিক এলাকা ", (in brief "the project") in respect of aforesaid acquired land respective notification of awards were issued in favour of the petitioners. According to the award notification, the petitioners obtained compensation as the affected persons. Rajdhani Unnayan Kartipakka (in brief,"RAJUK") initiated the establishment of the residential project on the acquired land.

4. On 07.05.2001, respondent No.2, RAJUK, published an advertisement in the National Daily asking the affected land owners whose land had been acquired under L.A. Case No.7/2000-2001 to submit applications for allotment of plots of three Kathas land for their residential purpose.

5. Accordingly, the petitioners comply with the requirements for allotment of plots for their residential purpose, having deposited taka 50,000/-(fifty thousand) earnest money each applied to the RAJUK. Photocopies of the respective bank receipts have been Annexed to this writ petition as Annexures-C, C-1, C-2, C-3, C-4, and C-5, and the photostate copy of the respective applications have been Annexed as Annexures-D, D-1, D-2, D-3, D-4 and D-5.

6. From those applications for allotment, it appears that the petitioners submitted their applications on 13.08.2001, 29.08.2001, 28.08.2001, 14.08.2001, 23.07.2001, and 31.07.2001. After filing the applications for allotment of plots, the petitioners, through their lawful agents, requested respondent No.2 RAJUK to allot their respective plots, but it kept silent inexplicably.

7. Subsequently, RAJUK informed that the petitioners' applications for allotment of plots could not be traced as they were missing. After a few years, when the affected persons, including the petitioners, demonstrated their serious dissatisfaction against the RAJUK, the Ministry of Housing and Public Works (in brief, "Housing Ministry") held a meeting on14.01.2009 regarding the allotment of plots to the affected persons. At their meeting dated 14.01.2009, the housing Ministry and the RAJUK took the following decisions: 
"সম্প্রসারিত উত্তরা আবাসিক এলাকা (৩য় পর্ব) প্রকল্পে ক্ষতিগ্রস্থ ক্যাটাগরীর জন্য সংরক্ষিত প্লটের মধ্যে যেগুলো এখনো বরাদ্দ করা হয়নি সেগুলো নীতিমালা ৮ (ক) ও ৮ (খ) প্রতিপালন করে বরাদ্দের জন্য রাজউক প্রয়োজনীয় ব্যবস্থা গ্রহন করবে।" 
৪. নীতিমালা ৮(ক) and ৮(খ) runs as follows:-
“৮ (ক) যে সকল ক্ষতিগ্রস্থ ব্যক্তি বসতভিটি জমি হারিয়েছেন এবং যারা ঘর বাবদ ক্ষতিপূরন গ্রহন করেছেন তাদের বসতভিটি জমির পরিমান যাই হোক না কেন তারা পরিবার প্রতি ১ টি প্লট পাবে।"
“৮ (খ) যে সকল ক্ষতিগ্রস্থ ব্যক্তি কৃষি/নাল জমি হারিয়েছেন তাদের ক্ষতিগ্রস্থ জমির পরিমান বিবেচনায় এনে অগ্রাধিকার ভিত্তিতে প্লট প্রদান করা হবে। তবে পরিবার প্রতি একাধিক প্লট প্রদান করা হবে না। (Annexure-E)".

9. According to the direction of the Ministry of Housing and Public Works, respondent No.2 RAJUK at its Board Meeting No. 9/2010 dated 23.09.2010 and 26.09.2010 decided that:- 
"১৪(৩) ক. নীতিমালা ৮ খ অনুচ্ছেদ অনুযায়ী অধিগ্রহনকৃত জমির পরিমানের অগ্রাধিকার ভিত্তিতে নূন্যতম ০.১৬৫০ একর ও তদুর্দ্ধ পরিমান জমি ক্ষতিগ্রস্থ হয়েছে এমন ৫৬০টি আবেদনের বিপরীতে ৫৬০টি প্লট বরাদ্দের জন্য সাময়িকভাবে নির্বাচন করা যেতে পারে (Annexure-F)"।
 
10. Subsequently, respondent No.2 RAJUK, at its Board Meeting No.6/2012 held on 28.06.2012, decided to allot three Kathas of land to those people from whom it had acquired a piece and parcel of land measuring 16.50 decimals or above (Annexure-G).

11. Subsequently, after long years on 12.09.2021, RAJUK, at its Board Meeting No. 5/2021 held on 12.09.2021, took a similar decision that from whom 16.50 decimals of land were acquired they would be provided to a three kathas residential plots (Annexure-H).

12. Upon addressing the issue in the assembly of the National Parliamentary, the Minister of Housing and Public Works informed that there are a total of 95 vacant plots remaining for the affected persons from whom 16.50 decimals of land had been acquired for the project under L.A. Case No.7/2000-2001.

13. It has been stated in the writ petition that some of the affected persons filed Writ Petition Nos.1342 of 2017, 150 of 2019, 151 of 2019, and 263 of 2019, whereby the High Court Division issued a Rule on those writ petitions and finally made the Rule absolute, directing the respondents therein, including RAJUK, to allot 3(three) Kathas plots to each of the petitioners therein within 60 days from the date of receipt of that judgment.

14. This Court further directed before allotting the petitioner plot, the RAJUK shall not allot any plot to any stranger, and if there is no plot remaining in the scheme area, the RAJUK shall accommodate each of the petitioners therein with a 3(three) Kathas residential plot to any other scheme or project of RAJUK as soon as possible.

15. In those writ petitions, though respondent No.2 RAJUK filed an affidavit in opposition, it did not controvert the claim made by the petitioners therein; instead, it conceded that the respective files were missing, for which it could not give a final allotment letter.

16. When respondent No.2 RAJUK did not take any step to allot plots for the residential accommodation of the petitioners, they, through their learned Advocate, sent a notice demanding justice on 24.07.2023 to the respondents requesting them to allot three Kathas plots in favour of the petitioners in the project and hand over the possession thereof (Annexure-J and J-1).

17. In such facts and circumstances, when the respondent RAJUK kept silent, the petitioners approached this Court and obtained the Rule and the direction as stated above.

18. The respondent RAJUK did not contest the Rule.

19. The learned Deputy Attorney General could not assist this Court without any instruction.

20. The learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that RAJUK made a general declaration in the prospectus that the affected persons would be rehabilitated by allotting three Kathas plots, and as such, RAJUK can not go beyond its promise and hence, the inaction of the RAJUK in allotting plots in favour of the petitioners are barred by the principle of promissory estoppels in as much as the inaction of the respondents in this regard are liable to be declared to be without lawful authority and are of no legal effect. The learned Advocate submits further that according to the decision of the Housing Ministry, RAJUK was required by law to allot residential plots in favour of the petitioners, and hence, a direction should be given to the RAJUK to allot the residential plots in favour of the petitioners. The learned Advocate next submits that since the RAJUK made a declaration in the prospectus that the affected persons would be rehabilitated, the petitioners can legitimately expect that the RAJUK shall go by at its own decision and, accordingly, RAJUK should be directed to allot plots in favour of the petitioners.

21. We have heard the learned Advocate for the petitioner and perused the writ petition and Annexures.

22. The Annexures-B, B-1, B-2, B-3, B-4, and B-5 information slips show that 16.50 decimals of land were acquired from petitioner Nos.1, 5, and 6 while 16.63, 17.40, and 24 decimals of land were acquired from petitioner Nos.2-4 under L.A. Case No. 7/2000-2001 for establishing the project.

23. From Annexures-C, C-1, C-2, C-3, C-4, and C-5, along with Annexures-D, D-1, D-2, D-3, D-4, and D-5, it appears that according to the advertisement for allotment of plots, the petitioners filed respective applications for allotting three Kathas residential accommodation each. RAJUK decided by a general declaration that the affected persons would be rehabilitated by allotting three Kathas residential plots.

24. Accordingly, the petitioners filed the respective applications to RAJUK for obtaining three Kathas plots each, and they deposited earnest money in favour of Chairman RAJUK at taka 50,000/- each, along with requisite papers and documents. Time and again, the Housing Ministry and RAJUK made several decisions that from whom at least 16.50 decimals of land have been acquired, they would be provided three Kathas residential plots to rehabilitate the affected people with their residential accommodation.

25. Despite such facts, RAJUK has not yet allotted any plot in favour of the petitioners.

26. The RAJUK, in the exercise of the power conferred in section 38 of the Town Improvement Act, 1953 (in brief, "the act 1953"), may proceed to frame an improvement scheme.

27. Section 42 of the Act 1953 provides for the re-housing of persons displaced by an improvement scheme which runs as follows: 
"42. The Kartripakkha may frame schemes (herein called re-housing schemes) for the construction, maintenance and management of such and so many dwellings and shops as they may consider, ought to be provided for persons of the poorer and working class who- 
(a) are displaced by the execution of any improvement scheme sanctioned in this Act or (b) are likely to be displaced by the execution of any improvement scheme which it is intended to frame, or to submit to the government for the sanctioned under this Act."

28. Under section 42 of the Act, 1953, the RAJUK is to provide dwelling houses or shops, as the case may be, for the persons to the poorer and working class who are displaced by the execution of such scheme.

29. On acquisition of what quantum of land the affected persons shall be construed as poorer or working classes has not been defined in the law.

30. Article 15(a) of the constitution castsa duty on the government to provide, amongst others, shelter to the citizens of the country. Accordingly, a residential plot should be allotted to the respective petitioners for their shelter since they have no alternative plot in Dhaka City. It shall be the fundamental responsibility of the state to secure the shelter for the petitioners by first rehabilitating them to residential accommodation.

31. Therefore, the provision of section 42 of the Act 1953 is mandatory as shelter is a basic necessity for the displaced persons whose land was acquired for the improvement scheme. Accordingly, the residential plots should be allotted to the petitioners for their shelter as it shall be the fundamental principle of the state to secure the shelter for the petitioners in rehabilitating them to residential accommodation.

32. Moreover, it appears from clause 8 of the "সম্প্রসারিত উত্তরা ৩য় পর্ব প্রকল্প আবাসিক এলাকায় প্লট বরাদ্দ নীতিমালা, ২০০৪"(নীতিমালা, ২০০৪) that to the priority basis the affected persons should be rehabilitated taking into consideration of their displaced situation from their homestead or agricultural land.

33. On a plain reading of clause 8 of the allotment নীতিমালা, ২০০৪, it appears that it does not put any limitation or restriction for qualifying the affected person on the quantum of land acquired. As such, as per নীতিমালা anybody would be considered an affected person from whom some land has been acquired for the improvement scheme.

34. The preamble of the plot allotment নীতিমালা, ২০০৪ runs as follows: 
“The Town Improvement Act, 1953 এর ১০২ ধারার অধীনে প্রনীত ঢাকা ইমপ্রুভমেন্ট ট্রাষ্ট (অ্যালটমেন্ট অব ল্যান্ড) রুলস, ১৯৬৯ মোতাবেক সম্প্রসারিত উত্তরা ৩য় পর্ব প্রকল্প আবাসিক এলাকায় প্লট বরাদ্দের নিমত্ত নিম্নোক্ত নীতিমালা প্রণয়ন করা হলো।”

35. It further appears that the allotment নীতিমালা was framed under the Town Improvement Act 1953. So, it has a legal force, and according to allotment নীতিমালা, RAJUK made an explicit promise to take measures for allotting plots among the land owners of the scheme area.

36. In such facts and circumstances, the RAJUK is bound to perform its promise by allotting plots to the affected petitioners.

37. In Writ Petition No. 150 of 2019, heard and disposed of along with Writ Petition No.151 of 2019 and 263 of 2019, we have made a clear finding that the RAJUK is to rehabilitate the distressed or affected persons first and then to allot the plot to any stranger to the scheme area.

38. It should be the prime duty of the RAJUK to rehabilitate the displaced people first and then accommodate the stranger.

39. By an order dated 07.02.2024, this Court directed the respondents to keep/preserve 6(six) individual plots to make allotment of three Kathas residential accommodations in favour of the petitioners within the project area.

40. Accordingly, before allotting the petitioner's plot, the RAJUK shall not allot any plot to any stranger.

41. In such view of the matter, we find merit in the Rule.

42. Accordingly, the Rule is made absolute.

43. The respondents are hereby directed to allot a residential plot measuring three Kathas to each petitioner within sixty days of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

Let a copy of this judgment and order be communicated to the respondent nos.1 and 2 for compliance.

End.
